text:
Took the whole fam jam, including Gramma, out to Wok House last night in St. Albert.  We've been eagerly awaiting the opening this past week because their banner outside read:  Chinese, Dim Sum, Bubble Tea!  Yep, that's right - St. Albert now has Dim Sum and Bubble Tea!!!

The location is in the old Banana Leaf Restaurant next door to Simply Donair in the same strip mall as Dairy Queen.

We were greeted by a friendly family who let us choose anywhere in the restaurant to sit - kiddos opted for the booth/bench option.

The decor was modern and clean.

The menu variety REALLY surprised me and all Dim Sum is cooked to order rather than coming around on carts. 

We decided we might as well go hard and try stuff from all parts of the menu.

First off, we ordered bubble teas:

Fresh fruit mango dairy free with sago, fresh fruit peach dairy free with sago, and milky matcha green tea with sago.  ALL WERE EXCELLENT.  The waitress waited to see if I liked he matcha because she warned that it's not very sweet and said she could make it sweeter if I preferred but I'm a matcha monster and this was exactly what I was looking for :-)  

Next up, they brought out a couple of small appetizers for us to share in celebration of their opening - spring roll, tempura shrimp, and a dry garlic rib:  all were excellent with my 7 year old requesting more of each!

We decided to share the dinner for 2 which came with spring rolls, chicken fried rice, 2 bowls of soup (won ton and hot & sour were both decent) and 2 entree choices:  we selected Honey Pepper Shrimp (DIVINE) and sliced Szechuan beef. 

Both of the mains were good and flavourful with a good amount of sauce.  Everyone in our group noted that the use of onions was pretty heavy and more peppers, corn, carrots, etc. would be nice.  I'd say the dishes were at about 1/3 white onions - usually this is a deal breaker for me but the sauces and meat quality were superb. 

Next up was our never ending sampling of Dim Sum:

Pork Buns - $4.99 good but smaller than most; my daughter didn't care for them here  and neither did Gramma (not sure why).

Sticky Rice (Excellent but it only comes with 2 small leaves for $4.99 - this could be vastly improved by adding a 3rd one for that price or putting more rice in each banana leaf.  Literally, the banana leaves had less than 1/2 of the amount of rice you would have at Jumbo). 

Beef skewers - not as pictured and not up to snuff in my opinion for $4.99 for 2.

Green Onion Cake - $4.99 a standard that my kids will insist on every visit though I prefer mine to be a little crunchier.

Pan fried meat dumplings - $4.99 standard but they don't bring red wine vinegar or whatever that sauce is most Dim Sum places serve with it.

Curried Squid - $4.99 Excellent and tender but I would LOVE the sauce to be a bit thicker and more plentiful to pour all over my rice :-)

We'd order 80% of the food again and to be able to have Dim Sum in St. Albert any day of the week at any time, we will most DEFINITELY be returning here.  

Even if Mom and Dad want regular Chinese food, the kids in our house will jump for joy at Sticky Rice, Green Onion Cakes, and Bubble Tea!

Service was friendly but slow tonight with our dishes coming as much as 60 minutes apart - YIKES!  But I won't fault them on this as they work out their bugs, hopefully in the future we will get things (like rice) before the rest of the meal.

Cheers Wok House, can't wait to come back!

P.S. They deliver, too!

Best Chinese food around! Great flavor and not greasy, like a lot tend to be.  War wonton broth actually tastes like broth! Not just flavory water (as I have encountered).   Reasonably priced (10% off if you pay cash :) ) with a good variety to choose from. Very family friendly. It is now our go to for Chinese food.

This is my go-to costume place of choice.  It is worth the drive to St. Albert for the selection and the staff that can help you find just about anything!

We are part of a non-profit group called "Rigor Productions".  A group of horror enthusiasts that are really just big kids that like to have fun and give back to the community.  We like to dress up as ultra realistic zombies, and other horror movie characters.  

Karrie's doesn't even bat an eyelash when I order "the good blood" by the gallon container!  

They have the best selection of Ben Nye theatrical makeup that I have seen in the city.  The staff is great at helping pick out what you need for a specific look (bruises, cuts etc)  They are also one of the only places that I have found that carries sclera professional special effects contact lenses.  

The main floor is a smaller costuming section with the theatrical makeup area and the dance costumes.  If you are looking for a costume, you may want to phone ahead to make sure they have enough staff to be able to take you upstairs to go poking around in their very large costume collection.  

Karries also does costume rentals.  

If you are looking for a specific accessory, they have a great selection of hats, tiaras, wigs, gloves, jewelry etc, etc, etc.

Great place to go when its not Halloween season, but you need some costume pieces for cosplays or parties. They also have full costume sets upstairs. The staff is always friendly and attentive, and always happy to answer your questions. Oh! They also have an awesome variety of special fx makeup.
Pretty good place. Went Friday night. Not overly busy but steady. Had some Dim Sum items. All good. Price was ok for the two of us. Will definitely return.

Finally!  I have been craving Chinese food for such a long time and have tried several in St. Albert, only to be immensely disappointed.

My daughters and I ordered the meal deal for three for take out.  When we placed the order we were told it would take only 15 minutes.  When we picked up the order it came with a large container of won ton soup, (3) spring rolls, chicken fried rice, chicken balls, beef with broccoli and dry ribs (a bonus).

The chicken fried rice looked very plain (chicken with rice and a few peas) and I was skeptical that it would have any flavor, but I was wrong!  It didn't require any soya sauce for flavor as it was delicious without it.  We will try the special fried rice next time.

The spring rolls were crispy and tasty, however it looked like the stuffing had been put through a food blender.

The chicken balls were tender and not greasy.  The sauce was sweet and sour.  Both were delicious!

The beef with broccoli had lots of broccoli and lots of beef.  Very tasty!

The won ton soup was devoured by my daughters so I didn't even get a taste.  It must've been good as they usually leave me some.

Finally, the dry ribs.  Totally unexpected and the package was marked "free dry ribs".  Again, they were devoured quickly.  The meat was tender and the outside crispy, not greasy at all.

We will definitely be back to order our Chinese!  We may even try the dim sum!  The Wok House was a delightful surprise.

I've been on the hunt for a 1920's costume for a stagette. This place is one of the only places in Edmonton that has Halloween costumes year round. The place was very easy to find with a large parking lot. The bottom floor is dance supplies, to access the costumes you have to go around the south side of the building and up the stairs. The selection is huge with everything from rentals, accessories and theatre quality costumes. The prices are about the same as you would pay online or in a store during the season ranging from $40 on sale to over $100 on the higher quality. The women was very helpful in grabbing me sizes and suggestions. Unfortunately I could not find anything that would fit me. The rentals are another option, the cheapest being $50 and up. They come with all accessories included.

Stopped here hoping for some dim sum after visiting the Farmer's Market. For only 2 people, the dim sum would have cost a little more than we wanted to spend, so we decided to order two of the combos instead. We were happy with both the quantity and quality of the food for the price. The food was fresh and tasty and the restaurant was clean. The staff was friendly and helpful. We were there not long after they opened, so there was plenty of parking in front; there's also a large parking area behind the building. In the end, we didn't get dim sum, be we did get good food at a decent price- I'll consider that a win!

Exceptional customer service & variety!

I stopped by Karrie's Kostume & Supplies store on my way home from work tonight to check if they had my toddler's ballet clothing in stock - I was greeted by a professional and friendly young lady who quickly showed me the available options; I decided to come back later with my daughter to try the items in for size.

..............................................................

2 hours later:

I returned to the store with my twirling and giggling toddler in tote.  We were helped by Anne, who was exceptionally good with my daughter.  My four year old has a hard time talking to strangers and will sometimes run away and hide when spoken to.  Anne knew just how to charm my toddler and after trying on the approved leotard options for ballet class, my daughter insisted on showing "the nice lady," before making a final selection.

My daughter discussed all her favorite Princesses and Halloween costume ideas for the coming year: LaLaLoopsy & Monster High, of course!

Anne even asked my daughter if she would like to try on their LaLaLoopsy costume; to which my daughter lost her marbles and a costume show and Photoshoot immediately followed care of Mommy's iPhone.

Anne even brought us upstairs (stairs are on the outside of the building) to the Costume floor where we marveled at the amazing Super Hero & Star Wars Costume selection!

I just cannot get over the selection of dance, costumes for adults & kids, stage/costume makeup, wigs & more!

Karrie's, you have made a fan out if me!

I stopped in at Karrie's to see if I could get better pricing on my children's dancewear for the 2013/2014 season and I was pleasantly surprised. Not only are they knowledgeable and professional, their prices on dancewear can not be beat! Thank you Karrie's, I will definitely be back for all of my dancewear needs and possibly some costuming supplies for Halloween!
Good food. Reasonably  good size portions for the price. Friendly  service but limited English. Good variety of Canadian and authentic  Chinese food. Dim sum items are limited but cooked to order.

Very disappointed. Ordered dinner for delivery at 5:00. It's now almost 8:00 and still no dinner. We've phoned 5 times and each time they've promised it's on its way. Needless to say we are giving up and never ordering again.

I've been there quite a few times since it opened. The food is good and authentic. The dim sum surprisingly made from scratch as a lot of restaurants buy frozen dim sum. My daughter loves their noodles, my hubby loves heir fried rice and I love their vegetable dishes. There are 3 ladies working as servers. They are nice and friendly. I highly recommend it.

Fantastic store! My boss sent me here for a Mrs Klause outfit and man I am so happy he did. It's a bit out of the way for me (I live in South Edmonton) but worth the trip. From costumes, to accessories to makeup this place is your one stop shop. I was greeted by a very friendly staff member who lead me to their clearance section and then explained their rental policy (boss gave me an $80 spending limit). What I really loved was how she didn't try to push me for the expensive rental. If anything, she guided me away from it and to the clearance rack. Which, after trying it on, was great anyway cause that dress was comfy! They also have a selection of wigs, which I try to keep to my normal supplier but this costume was too last minute to order from them. Which was also fine cause Karries Kostumes has a decent quality to choose from. All in all, great place!
We were looking for a good Chinese restaurant in St. Albert, so we went for dim sum, it was disappointing. Not much selection and they taste mediocre.

MY FAVORITE HALLOWEEN SHOP
Every year our family waits for the fall of the first leaf to begin searching for pieces and planning our perfect halloween celebration. There is NO comparison to Karries. A lot of the "pop-up" stores will carry some of the lower-end options from Karries, but at the same cost. 
The main reason for venturing to Karries is the knowledge and love of the craft. They have theater quality makeup (such as Ben Nye) and most importantly 

MAKE SURE YOU KNOW HOW TO USE IT. 

They have great makeup, prosthetics, costumes (to buy or rent), wigs, accessories, etc...

Also, from what I have been told their children's dance selection is also top notch (I can't compare as I don't have children, or dance myself).

Very good!  Best I've had in a LONG time. Place is very clean and has a nice atmosphere. Hosts were really nice.  I ordered take-out and was seated. Given water and some deep fried wontons with honey drizzle while I waited. Portions were really good for the price (dinner for 4).

The dried garlic ribs were awesome and not over cooked like every other place I've been. Same with the honey garlic chicken. Crispy and tender as well. Overall, was excellent. The vermicelli noodles were spicy. The spring rolls were VERY good.

Do not order online for delivery. I ordered 5 dishes and after waiting for over an hour I tried calling and got no answer. So I got in my car and started driving there instead. I kept calling and someone finally answered and said they were just packing up my order. I told them I was almost there so not to bother deliver it. Food was cold when I got home and I live 10 min away. The food was typical Chinese food. It all comes from the same place frozen. All they have to do is deep fry it and throw on the sauce. I could have done without the long black hair in my ginger beef though. I will try another place next time.

This store is absolutely packed with Halloween costumes - literally from floor to ceiling! They rent costumes as well as sell. There's a large wall of makeup and accessories - everything you'd need to make the perfect gunshot wound, natural looking devilish pointed chin, scars or clowns. They have a setting spray for the makeup which I thought was cool. They even have everything you need to get it all off when it's over. There are change rooms available at the back of the store. The staff are all dressed up in costumes, I was greeted by Snow White on arrival. At the moment, most of the dance stuff is covered by the Halloween stuff but you can see it peeking through. 

It's a lot of fun browsing this store. They didn't have any costumes that were too racy. They had some catsuits and the typical "sexy" costumes consisting of short shorts and short skirts and low cut tops and crop tops. Fairly PG rated. I was interested in their selection of belly dancing sarongs which I think are standard for the store. Very jingly.

I have never reviewed a restaurant before but I feel this one deserves it. 
I'm a huge won ton soup fan and this place has, by far, the BEST wontons I've ever had 

This will deff be my go to from now on !  Just amazing

We ordered here last night hoping to enjoy a great Chinese take out for New Years Eve. We order every year and just moved to St albert and because this one had rave reviews, we thought we'd try it. We called and ordered and we're told we could pick up our order in just over an hour, so we waited an hour and a half. When I walked in, I was surprised to see so many people standing around waiting to pick up their orders. In the 20 mins that I stood there waiting to be served, I only seen one person leave with their take out. There was a lot of commotion going on in the kitchen as the wait staff went in and out but never any food being brought to people. A young server finally came and asked for my name and went to see about the order. He came back from the kitchen with nothing and told me it would be at least another hour wait!!! He said the other people here had ordered 2 hours ago and my order would be after they were served!!! We left empty handed and waited today to see if this restaurant would reach out to us and possibly make this situation better...they did not! So, I can only rate them on the service and they could have handled this much better. First thing would have been to warn me ahead of time that they were extremely busy and the wait would have been at least 2 hours. Second would have been to have the manager come and speak with me after I asked and third would have been to call me the next day and offer to remedy the situation.

We're very grateful to have dim sum and bubble tea made with fresh fruit available here in St Albert, and i hope the restaurant does very well.   It's a challenge to take over a location where the previous owner did so poorly, so I hope everyone gives this place a chance.

We entered thru the back entrance for better parking,and were greeted by not only the servers but also everyone in the kitchen, starting the evening very pleasantly.   I feel we were given very good attention all evening, with various checks to make sure the food was good, and the surprise of complementary appetizers was great.   However, the arrival of food was sporadic and a bit strange - the rice was the very last thing to appear, after all other food had been consumed over a quite long period of time.   As it was their grand opening and they were trying to give the appetizers to everyone, cooked fresh for each table, plus the dim sum cooked-to-order, I imagine it was quite a challenge for the kitchen and timing will improve.

Best dish, for me, was the Honey Pepper Shrimp.  I wish the rice had come sooner so I could have bathed it in the sauce that was heavenly, but that's a minor complaint.  It was absolutely scrumptious and I would make sure to always order it.   Other dishes were okay, none had me ready to cheerlead for them, but none "awful."  The only real downside is that onions seemed to be the only accompaniment in all  of them - some bok choy, celery, carrots, mushrooms, etc would have raised my opinion of all of them.  

Will I go back?  Definitely - still so many things to try - and those shrimp are calling my name!

Went for supper on the first night they reopened after the shut down. Had some dim sum items, salt and pepper prawns and ginger beef. Wife said this was the best ginger beef she has ever had. The salt and pepper prawns were as good as I have had anywhere. The dim sum arrived hot and speedy was great. I will definitely be going back as this is one of the best Chinese restaurants in the Edmonton area.

Five stars for Karrie's! 

I wasn't sure what I would do about Yelp's Prohibition Party. I knew the clothes I could put together at Value Village, but I was worried about what to do with my hair, and I wanted some white and black makeup. 

I found a perfect curly black Flapper wig, got some guidance on which types of makeup would be best for what I wanted to do, and even found the perfect T-strap dance shoes here (they're ballroom dancing shoes, but look great for 20s-30s theme stuff. 

The clerks were all great and friendly, and seem like they really enjoy what they're doing. I was told that they even have a 2nd floor upstairs with yet more costumes, some to buy! 

If you need the perfect costume, accessory, or tutu for your little princess, you'll find it here.

Amazing store - even better now that they've expanded! An entire first floor dedicated to a wide selection of dance outfits, plus any kind of costume accessory you can think of. Hats? They've got fedoras, pirate hats, feathers, bowlers, top hats, you name it! Costume jewelry, masks, plus random things like cigarette holders. Even make-up for specific looks. The staff were incredibly helpful when I came in, too. I told them I was looking for 1920s style accessories and they pointed out a ton of pieces that might go with the theme.

Because most costume shops are only open around Halloween, this place is definitely your best bet for a costume party or dress-up opportunity all year long. Plus, with staff who are knowledgeable about their inventory and incredibly friendly, you can't go wrong here. Best of all, they have costumes for rent and purchase, so you don't necessarily need to invest as much money into a one-time get-up.

Definitely worth the drive!

Ordered a variety of dishes. It was okay, not that flavourful. Did not speak good English, difficult to comprehend what waitress was saying. Ordered to go. They use reusable containers, which is nice. $55 for 4 dishes.

Nothing will ever beat my dad's restaurant and since his retirement I've been on the constant search for something that approaches the quality and goodness. Wok House isn't equal, hence the 4 stars, but it comes close! We'll be back!

I absolutely love this store! I've been going here for years for my daughters dance gear. Today I went in with a big, very specific wish list of theatre/ special effects makeup for my daughter and they had everything on my list and were so helpful and friendly! Every time I visit the store I'm always impressed and leave with a smile.

I got a last-minute message from my daughter that today was the one-day-sale for dance class regalia and to please rush to this store and get the items my granddaughter needed.  I thought the parking lot looked crowded when I arrived, and once inside I could see why.  Every mom and daughter in St Albert must have been inside, trying on costumes and shoes, leotards and tutus, sparkles and tulles abounding.  I was approached immediately by a roving employee (they were all dressed in black, so easy to spot) who took my list and filled it in record time with exactly what I needed, and emphasized that if any size wasn't perfect they would be happy to exchange it for my daughter when she was available.  At checkout, they asked if my granddaughter had her heart set on anything in particular for Halloween, as they were making lists for special ordering hard-to-get costumes, such as Elsa (and if you don't know who that is, you obviously do not have a young girl in your family!).

It's pretty amazing to walk into a store you don't know, finding it crowded with so many enthusiastic customers, get helped immediately with lots of smiles, and be checked out and back in your car in six minutes.  I am impressed.  I am also eager to return on a quieter day to explore all the goodies I spotted, and go upstairs to the costume area.  The employees get big kudos from me for being knowledgable, friendly, and efficient.  

p.s. I also loved the sign in their window that said, "Thank you for shopping local."

Located in a really sweet part of downtown St.Albert; This corner cafe is a great stop to make before wondering around and absorbing all of the  surrounding summer scenery. The coffee is pretty standard self-filling with milk and cream off to the side, but the price is right for the large Dixie cup. My husband got one of their 360 cold drinks, which was pretty flavorful. They offer a wide variety of gluten free food, but it appears that all of their food is pre made and frozen, so it gets microwaved when you order it. All and all, I'd return here for a quick cup of coffee.

Stopped in here with a few friends on the way back to Edmonton from an event in St. Albert. Cozy little place, with lots of gluten-free items on the menu. I had a cappuccino and I thought it tasted great, albeit reading a bit more like a latte with extra foam, but I don't necessarily think that is a bad thing. The others at my table said the soup was really good, as was the sandwich that was ordered. There was only one person working the front counter, so it did take a while to get acknowledged as he was busy getting other people's orders together. However, I would come here again if I am ever in St. Albert and need coffee.

My fav place to hit up a class or go for a run. They have stations set up on the side of the track so you can spin, do stairs, do weights, hit the mat for some abs, whatever you wish! For 50 bucks a month, it's well worth it if you actually go everyday. The equipment in the gym is iPhone compatible. The only place I dislike is the workout studio. Whenever we have 30 people crunched into that room, it's like 100 degrees of nastiness. Luckily most of the classes we take are in gym 3. ;)

I grew up in St. Albert, and while I go back frequently (usually every week or so), my trips are usually only to my parents' place (my childhood home!) and back home again.

Yesterday, I had an appointment with my eye doctor, the same one I've been going to since a kid. His office is in downtown St. Albert, and I got there early (miracle), so I actually explored the city a little more than I usually do. Even though it's only been a few years since I've lived here, a few things have definitely changed.

My beloved St. Thomas Cafe is no more. I had lots of memories of that place. Mostly awkward first dates in high school. But those are different stories for a different day.

It's been replaced by La Crema, which looks pretty similar in set-up and tone. It's still comfy and cozy with lots of tables.

I swung by and ordered a London Fog, my usual drink. It was very, very hot (a good thing) and pretty delicious. Not quite as sweet as I would have liked it, but still quite tasty.

I didn't try any of the baked goods, but I did notice that everything is gluten free. Very cool!

Next time I'm in St. Albert, I'll definitely come by for a cup of coffee here!
I LOVE this place!!! It has absolutley everything you can imagine in a recretional facility! I have nothing negative to say about servus place.

I have been going to drop in classes on Monday and Wed eve at Servus Place .
This drop in classes starts at 545-645.
The instructor's name is Gina well if you want a workout come to these classes.
I am so hook on these classes she does i wish there was on one a Fri eve.

This is a nice cozy cafe that my Mom and sister and Grandma's and I came to specifically because of the gluten free menu as my Mom is Celiac. We had soups, sandwiches and salads. They have really good cornbread (gluten free) and a nice caramel macchiato. It's priced accordingly to what you get, maybe a little pricey but I think it pays for the ambience you get. The staff is pretty welcoming, though a few of the girls seemed snooty. Overall a good experience!

My Saturday mornings in the summer are always started with a visit to the St. Albert Outdoor Farmers Market. Located right in the middle of the Market is La Crema Caffé. Nothing makes the market any better than a great cup of coffee and a cinnamon bun. 

The morning starting goodness doesn't stop here, everything is gluten free! Pretend I didn't tell you that, because you never would have guessed that they were gluten free.

Stop in for dinner for a great gf pizza or even a quiche and follow up with one of the most delicious desserts you will ever find.
Excellent facility! Friendly and helpful gym staff that greet me with a smile and ask about my progress :) You guys make my days.

This is a cozy little cafe in St. Albert. I discovered it by chance, and I now whenever I come to St. Albert to watch a movie at Grandin Theatre, I make sure to stop by this little cafe. La Crema serves coffee, Italian sodas, alcoholic drinks (mostly beer and wine), as well as grilled paninis, soups and lots of yummy baked goods such as pies, cakes and cookies. There are even gluten-free foods available.
The location of this coffee house is discrete; the place feels cozy, so it's no surprise that is gets extremely busy. Even when it is, the atmosphere is relaxed, and it's easy to spend several hours here without even noticing. Both food and coffee are excellent. 
What makes this place even more charming is that from time to time it hosts live performance nights. I had a chance to see a wonderful young guitarist perform 70s/80s songs. 
Service is fast and hassle free.

Great little family owned Italian cafe in St. Albert!  

They make excellent lattes and specialty drinks.   If you order your latte to stay, they serve them in large latte cups with a little gingersnap cookie on the side... nice touch you don't see too often these days!

They've recently started a Sunday brunch buffet from 11am -2pm for $13.95  It's excellent!  They always have an assortment of scones, bagels, breads, muffins, hashed browns, belgian waffles, bacons, several sausages, fresh granola, yogurt, fruit, scrambled eggs, poached eggs in a tomato sauce, fresh homemade berry topping for your granola, yogurt, or waffles and real whipped cream.  Juice is included in the buffet - coffee is extra.  Though, coffee refills are included with the buffet.

Very charming and they do accept reservations if you're worried about getting a spot big enough for your party as they seat approximately 30 inside and another 15-20 outside.

The walls are decorated with old family photos of Italy... Quite charming!

I'm hoping they open up their gelato stand again this summer once it warms up!  If you go to the St. Albert Farmer's Market, they are located on Anne street in the heart of the Farmer's Market.
Nice place. Chai was excellent. London Fog was so so. Panini with pesto and artichokes was tasty.

It's a great place to go when you're in need of a close gym in St Albert. Friendly staff, clean facilities (although the changerooms can get a bit smelly at times), friendly people -- for the most part (you will find 'bro' types at just about any gym, tho!).

Only complaint is quite a bit of the equipment seems to have been going 'Out of Order' lately. Maybe it's because it's a busy summer gym season? Who knows. It's a little dissapointing having the Jacob's Ladder crap out after 3 minutes because it was not charged up, or seeing at least 3 of the exercise/cardio machines down at a time lately.

I'll keep going to Servus. It's the same price as any other gym but month-to-month available (no fishy contracts!), and there's enough equipment to get me by -- although I wish there was a little more (inner thigh machine, not having kettlebells constantly locked up) but I realize that may become a hazard with the size of the facility and all-ages range.

Would I recommend Servus? Yes! For all ages! Just be curteous to your fellow gym go-er (please stop texting and chatting on the machines) and put your weights and plates away when you're done. None of that is the staff's fault tho, they do a great job here!

The coffee experience was a great one, this is why I'm going there in the first place. The customer service side was not the same. We usually come to a coffee shop to relax, the environment at the front till caused tension and frustration, one can only hope this changes as the rest of the experience was great
Their espresso machine, including the milk steamer was on the fritz and it was taking about 15 minutes for each drink to come out :( how disappointing.

Sunday Brunch Buffet price has increased to $14.95 from $13.95.  

Not really a big increase, but worth an update none the less.

I did notice on my most recent visit that they did not have homemade granola out.  It may have been an oversight or perhaps they do not make that anymore?

Great family fitness center with many options!

As a mother of a young child, I really appreciate that they not only have 2 ice arenas, but that they also have a separate and smaller family ice arena great for teaching children!

The children's playground is great for letting your kids run amok while their hair dries after swimming before braving our winter cold on the way back to your car in the winter.

The swimming facility is great for "families" with a phenomenal toddler section where they can run and run and run in a shallow section.  But for adults, there is only one lane for lap swimming - lame!  Couldn't they have just made the pool 6 feet wider so that there could have been 3 laps for adults to swim in?

The water slides are AMAZING for an indoor pool - especially the fact that you can ride tandem on tubes down one of them.

And it's a saltwater pool - hooray!  So much easier on the skin and hair!

The hot tub area is again nice in that there are two large hot tubs with two different depths to make it more accessible to families.

I haven't taken the opportunity to use the work out equipment yet... so I can't comment on that.

There is a Booster Juice, a little Mom and Pop stand with ice cream and snacks, and a grill upstairs called Sky Box (and if you have an Entertainment Coupon book - Sky Box is in the coupon book for B1G1 free).

They also have toddler preschool programs, cooking classes, yoga, the list goes on and on.  There is really more than I could ever explain in one review - and more than I will ever explore.

We did have the opportunity to go to their Halloween Bash which was amazing!  There was a Thriller Dance Party, cookie decorating, Mad Scientist Lab, Haunted House, and all sorts of games for kids!  Very impressed.

This is a very nice place for families, that offers a wonderful water-park, and lots of basketball gym/courts space.  Their membership price packages are very good, and they are worth for the swimming alone. (for a family)
Now that being said, I wouldn't recommend it for a serious gym minded individual. The gym floor space is tiny, very few machines, and anytime I went there it was extremely busy. If you only do cardio, it is great though, never run out of cardio equipment, but the weight equipment is minimal.  It's a sub-par gym, but for ok for an occasional user doing mostly cardio workouts.

This new and beautiful Centre has an amazing selection of services! The facility is set on the outside of town and offers numerous opportunities for teams, events and different age ranges. If you have ever been to one of these facilities you know my review will never explain how much they can give to a community and family. We can skate, play, swim and have supper within two hours and all for a very reasonable price. I have even heard of people moving over to this part of the city to help save time when taxing kids around for sports.

As a young family we often utilize the pool, the skating rinks, play park and food services. We are always pleased with the cleanliness, easy going staff and well priced services.

By far my favorite evenings have been spent swimming with the kids, having a snack at Skybox Cafe and then dropping the littles in their AWESOME DAYCARE service and then going back to Skybox for a drink and some sports viewing with my husband (we love close enough to walk home:)

Fun and fitness all in one location! Access to a water play center, leisure ice, fitness and wellness center, track and training center, and a children's playground is available to everyone with daily admission (monthly and annual memberships are available). 

I have been attending Servus Place a minimum of five times a week for eight months now and have nothing but positive experiences. The gym has ample equipment, the employees are always friendly, and the facility is clean. The drop-in fitness classes are offered with everyone in mind. Different fitness levels are accommodated in all classes and the instructors are welcoming and knowledgeable. These classes can get very busy and often fill up so sometimes I wish there were more classes offered in a week. Another downside is that there are no early morning drop-in classes so if you work a regular work week your options are even more limited.

An added bonus is in the last month the facility has upgraded lots of the fitness center equipment including (but not limited to) the body bars, cardio machines, steps, mats, and resistance bands. It is always nice to not worry about the equipment breaking, or not working properly, or generally being old. I think sometimes I take that for granted because equipment is never a concern.

Servus Credit Union Place offers the best bang for your buck if you are looking for a no-commitment all around fitness center in north-west Edmonton.
Servus has such a great pool and indoor waterpark. The staff are very friendly too.

awesome facility, been attending for last 6 months!
never too crowded, prices are reasonable.

I was very impressed by the workout facilities here. The drop in rate is very affordable. Staff are friendly and knowledgeable. Everything is clean and in good repair. I was even able to get a bandaid when my dry finger cracked and started bleeding. It's well organized and there was a good cross-section of people working out. Not pretentious at all. Very relaxed atmosphere. I'll definitely be back.

Confused staff, horribly long wait to get a simple latte.
Evidently according to someone else waiting 15 mins. For their order , it is the norm here not the exception.
At the end latte was average at best.

Food is consistently very good. The drinks are delicious, as well. Best of all, I adore the dining area. It's cozy and the ambience is comforting. The only downside I've noticed thus far is that there is usually only one staff member working whenever I go, so they are responsible for cashing out customers and then making their entire meal. While is this fine during slow periods, I believe it slows down overall service and must be quite stressful for the staff member. However, if you're not in any rush then the
La Crema Caffè is a great option.

Customer service has gone downhill.

I had fond memories of this place. Had gone a couple years ago and had one of the loveliest matcha lattes in a huge ceramic cup.

So I went back yesterday and had a hot chocolate that tasted like it could've come from a gas station. I was disappointed, I was in disbelief.

And then I came back today, in denial (I was down here for the Farmer's Market anyway -- great way to spend a Saturday if I do say so myself!) -- and ordered a caramel macchiatio and my boyfriend ordered an iced matcha latte, and his order came out 10 minutes before mine. They forgot about mine. They even forgot about the brownie we were going to share until we reminded them.

Yes, I will give them the benefit of the doubt -- they were moderately busy. But forgetting a customer's order completely, and then putting our drinks and food in styrofoam when we didn't even ask for anything 'to go' as a sort of, "Well, we forgot, take them, styrofoam, we don't care".

I am a little shocked and appalled. Not to mention dissapointed.

For a go-to local coffee shop, unfortunately, I will begin to look elsewhere. I may return sometime, but it may be in a begrudging manner at this rate.
Great prices and I love the gluten free menu. Their gluten free dessert squares are awesome! Especially the white chocolate rasberry one.

My daughter begs to go here all the time. She has so much fun at the pool and indoor playground. As a family, we also really enjoy our time here. I also attend an annual convention here, which the venue handles pretty well. My only complaint is the daily rate, $15.50 for just my daughter and I . The monthly rates are still pretty high, but if you manage to go a few times a week it is worth it.

I pop in here the odd morning when I'm in St Albert for lovely lattes or teas and sometimes a snack. They have great mugs for when you are staying in, but if you are like me and it takes forever for you to finish, to go cups are also an option. A fairly standard menu when it comes to hot drinks, but all the usual suspects are there so it definitely can give you your caffeine or none caffeine kick in the morning. 
  As for snacks I've only ever had the spinach quiche, but they do offer some gluten free options I've noticed in the pastry case as well. I unfortunately haven't really paid attention to the rest of their menu options, but look forward to venturing into it further in my subsequent visits. 
  The staff is always pleasant and timely with the preparation of the drinks and food for the most part, this is where I'd say the 5th star could be garnered. When food is ordered with the drinks it tends to take a little longer than I would think is necessary, but by no means too long, just could be a little better is all. 
  The quality is consistent and the space is always clean and inviting, it's definitely worth stopping in to try!

Recently visit Servus Credit Union Place again after they just updated their swimming area and put in new murals.

Unfortunately, somebody had an AFR (Accidental Fecal Release) and the swimming had to be cut short :-(

I did hear them offering any non-members the option to be refunded at the front desk which I thought was good customer service (not something you always see these days!)

They have new water toys for the kidlets, everything has been freshly cleaned, and new murals on the walls.  

They close down every year for 2 weeks for regularly scheduled maintenance and upkeep - they try to have it coincide with the St. Albert International Children's Festival.

Servus pool - we are so glad to have you back!

FYI - The family ice rink (the small one) is now closed for the summer and for maintenance.  It will reopen in the fall - the meantime be sure to check for open ice times if you're brining your kidlets skating!
Servus is a great facility. There is loads to do and a great place to keep fit; especially in the winter! I'm a huge fan :)

This facility is fantastic. They have a wonderful indoor water park that is never closed to the public. The indoor playground is perfect in the winter. The gym is well maintained, clean and ecstatically pleasing. The indoor running/walking track is perfect for training, cool down and sprinting. With two ice rinks, two indoor soccer fields and two basketball courts I see people playing all the time. The leisure rink which has two bouncy castles in the summer is perfect for the little ones. My only complaint is the open concept showers in the pool area are not my cup of tea. The gym showers are a button you press and gives you 30 seconds of water. It's kinda annoying. But other then that I love this gym. I also love the membership options. You can buy month to month or sign contract for a discount. They have a couple of options for the contracts and the annual gives you the best bank for your buck. Their child minding is also a great option for parents. I have used it and it was perfect.

I went to this cafe for the first time last weekend and was surprised and impressed by their gluten free options. The menu offers gluten free pizza, sandwiches, chicken pot pie, and several desserts. 

I tried the gluten free chicken pot pie and it was pretty good.  The pie was filled with chunks of moist chicken and veggies, all in a savory creme-based gravy filling. The crust was a little soggy on the bottom, but otherwise the pastry was flaky and light. My husband had a non-gluten free Italian sandwich and reported it was tasty. The price of our meal seemed reasonable, especially given it included a gluten free option. 

The service was just okay. The staff weren't especially friendly. Our meal took over twenty minutes to be served, which seemed a bit long considering my pie was simply reheated and a sandwich usually doesn't take too long to prepare. Still, I plan to return and to try the rest of their gluten free options.

This is a great place for new moms to stay fit. Once my baby was 4 months old I joined the mamas and babies spin class. It's so wonderful how you could keep your baby in the stroller as you spin. You can also use the track and bring your baby in a carrier or in a stroller and run or walk. There are weights up near the track so you can lift weights while your baby sleeps or enjoys watching you. This is a great service for moms who don't want to yet put their baby into gym daycares 

I will be back to try out the swim pool

Have been going to Servus, specifically the gym for the past six months now and I must say I am impressed with the cleanliness and comfort of this gym. No juice monkeys here and for the most part everyone is there to simply work out and is friendly. Ample parking and good pricing for month to month users. Only complaint I have is there silly rule about having to be 12 years old to enter the gym area. I tried to get my 11 yr old son in to use the elliptical as he's trying to be healthy but he was kicked out even though I was on the machine next to him. I do understand their concern for safety but I think as being a father I have the most concern for his safety. Other than this one issue it's a great place to go.

This place is great. First the building has tons of shit to do. Swimming, track, gym, rinks, courts. Plus it has many good drop in classes at very decent rates. Everything is clean and well kept. My only real beef is with the size of the mens gym change room. Like if there is 3 guys it is crowded. When you build a nice big building maybe make a big more changing space!!

I really enjoy this rec centre.  Great track on the third floor, ice rinks are awesome and I love taking their classes.  I've taking all the spin classes and have enjoyed them all and continue to take them.  I've also noticed that the people who go here are also really friendly.  Staff are helpful and knowledgeable.  Washrooms are relatively clean and accessible.  I also love it's convenient location and tons of parking. The instructors of every class (registered class) I've taken has been great and keep you engaged.  They always introduce themselves to new people in the class and are helpful if you have an injury.

The location is easy to get to and there was enough parking both times I was there.  The first time we walked in the front door and got a glimpse of those enjoying the swimming area.  It looked like a fun place! There was a sports store, Starbucks, and Booster Juice.  For those looking for a more substantial sit down meal, there's a restaurant upstairs too.

I've been here a few times.  The first time for Eek Fest where there were a few of the large fieldhouses were transferred to booths for those to shop and play at, and one of the arenas had the Lego display.  The next visit was more recent for the Rock n' August concert to see Chilliwack and Loverboy in the Go Auto arena.  We went upstairs and I liked it was spacious and not too crowded with people lined up to get it and congregating outside the arena.  There's seating and washrooms are clean.

Inside the arena, they were selling liquor on the concourse and ice level.  They had popcorn for sale but only on the ice level so I had to walk down the steps.  The steps are narrow so glad I didn't have high shoes on to maneuver up and down them.   There were a lot of seats available so we ended up seating ourselves where it wasn't crowded to watch the show.  In between acts, we went out on the concourse.  There were a few people working out and gym looked decent.

The staff working the concert were nice and informed us there were 2 doors we could go in for the concert.  We enjoyed the show and had a good time.  Would come back if they have another concert here.

Service Credit Union Place : home of lifestyle and fitness. Hosts ice rinks, public gym, swimming pool and soccer fields. Upon entry is Starbucks and sports store. My friend and I went to see the "Lifestyle Expo" hosting different local and General AB businesses. Spaced out were 3 large zones for vendors. People were friendly. We ended up meeting a nice lady from the Healing centre. Bought some tea and now interested in their sell for body scans to identify ailments. Cute shops for clothing - and wood working , many businesses were able to draw people in. I'd have to say for someone on crutches / cane - not so accommodating. Large arena but no break or space in between to sit or rest. We only made it to one arena out of 3 . Required a full day. 5$ Entry which wasn't too bad. Kids were involved by using "passport stamping method" - each vendor would stamp their business name on the passport card and at the end the kids would get a prize. They did offer free water bottles and bags to keep info pamphlets in. Take credit / debit / cash. Parking as it should be for any public facility. Volunteers marked and were all around to assist with any info. Useful for those who live in St Albert .

First time ordering from La Crema Caffe! The Calabrese panini was tasty as well as the cinnamon bun. I ordered over the thanksgiving weekend, and they gave me a free ginger cookie with a cute note :) I will definitely check them out in person once dine in is back!

It's not very often I found myself in St. Albert, since I'm usually on the other side of Edmonton, but I was in St. Albert today. I remember visiting this cafe last year, before attending a Litfest session at the library, and I wanted to go back. Of course my stupid GPS didn't recognize the address of the cafe (it also did not recognize half the addresses in St. Albert) but I found the cafe. Went in and ordered an Americano and a piece of carrot cake. The have a gluten free bakery so the carrot cake may have been gluten free. I didn't check (I'm also not celiac so it's no bother to me either way). The point being the carrot cake really good, nice and moist (or un-dry for those of you with an aversion to the "m" word). The coffee was good, they have a nice selection of coffee drinks. They apparently have fair trade coffee. I also saw a poster about live music and dinner, but I didn't investigate too much. I loved the yellow colour, and the pictures on the wall - not sure of it's of the owner's family or what but it gives a little homey touch to the place. Free wifi, plenty of seating. The coffee was good, nothing mind blowing, but good and the service was prompt and friendly. If I lived in St. Albert I'd likely make this my regular coffee spot.

I nice coffee shop in a really cute location in " downtown" St Albert.  It was a beautiful day so I decided to sit on their patio in the sun and have a coffee before my appointment 

There have a big selection on cold and hot drinks as well as treats and food.  The menu includes salads, soups and sandwiches. I was also happy to see they have different milk alternatives.  I ordered a reg decaf toffee oat latte.  I be reminded the lady that I wanted decaf.  When it arrive it was definitely a large and piping hot!! It was so hot that I could drink it in the 25 minute window before my appointment.  I enjoyed it on my way home but then a couple hours later realized it was definitely NOT decaf .  Not good.
They have a nice outdoor patio.  Coffee shop with muffins and paninis.  Friendly staff.  Lattee was good.

Me and my family have been going to Servus Place for various reasons since it's opening. One thing that keeps bringing us back is the pool. We have made 8t a point to visit every swimming pool in and around Edmonton  and for its price Servus Place is gonna give you the best bang for you buck. 

I think what the kids like most about it is that there are two large slides to play on. A smaller one that's faster and has more turns. And a slightly larger on that fits tubs. I have been down these slides several hundred times and they never fail to give you that bit of thrill and exhilaration that makes you nostalgic for your elementary school  days.

Servus Place has pool area is broken into have different swim areas. One for babies and infants. One more suitable for kids just learning to swim with water about 2 ft tall. The next a joining pool is about 3 to 4 ft high. And finally the largest pool that would qualify as the deep end. This pool usually has one lane roped off for lane swimming only.

And finally there is a lazy river pool. My kids have renamed it into The Maze. This pool provides endless entertainment to play games of catch-me-if-you-can or hide and go seek. Each pool has its own temperature and non of the pools are overly cold, which is nice when your with little ones.

They also have two large hot tubes. One that is more suitable for younger children and the other that will make your skin a nice lobster red when you leave. Either way there is something for everyone to enjoy at massive water Playland.

Servus Place is chalk full of amenities, from a full servus restaurant to professional sized ice rinks and soccer and basketball courts. I mean really the list is endless and you can very easily send a whole day keeping yourself busy here.

Great place for a date or anytime you are looking for a delicious sandwich and some good tunes. I stopped by for a sandwich on the way to the library and was completely impressed. I'll be going back for sure! 

Also, the torpedo sandwich is awesome. Get one!

First time going here and I felt like family. Had the prego sandwich and it was delicious, a nice bite to it. Next time I'm having the classic pasta and meat sauce.  The atmosphere is very warm and inviting and such a great addition to St. Albert , especially downtown.  I definitely will be back, even if just for the custard tarts ( can't remember the actual name) they were delicious.   Paint nite in 3 weeks!  Thank you Anna for being an amazing host.

Fantastic little place on Perron Street.  Was in St. Albert Arden Theatre for a show and walked over for a coffee and desert.  

Inside, the decor was interesting, black and white checkered tables, nice view of the St. Albert river valley, large paintings of notable bands featured on the walls; but the most interesting feature was that the walls were also filled with pictures and prints for sale by various artists, we really enjoyed perusing through the one nature series of pictures.

The lay out can be a little confusing, when you first walk in, it feels like a take out place where you order/pay at the counter before sitting down, BUT, it is not, take a seat, menus will be brought to you, then the friendly chat with the staffs can begin.

The cafe only seats about 30 or so, not a big place, it was quite busy when we were there, almost full but it was right after a show at the theatre.  

The staffs were friendly, like old friends, laughing with us, coming up with suggestions.  The whole time we were there, the waitresses were always at one table or another chatting with patrons, I like them, I like them a lot!

The two of us had their Latte and Americano; the drinks were fresh, hot and delicious, definitely better than the chain stores.  Desert wise, we had their pasteis de nata - "a thin, crackly crust filled with luscious egg custard" and the Cornetti - "Ppuff pastry dough with a vanilla cream filling twirled into a horn shape"; they were fantastic.  I have never had the pasteis de nata before, very rich, very sweet and very very good, I may be hooked.  Only complaint was that the pastries were served refrigerator cold, wish they were slightly warmed up. Their menu is small but they served savory foods as well; we didnt partake so I can't comment.   

Price wise, $4 for an americano, $4 for a med. latte, $3 for each pastry; not cheap but quite acceptable.  

The service was excellent, the waitress was always smiling and was extremely attentive.  Yes I would definitely return if I am in the neighbourhood again.

"Latte" seemed like regular drip coffee with a bit of warm milk. Menu said $4, but was charged $10.25 for two lattes, not sure how they calculated the extra $2.25 in there. Also last time I was in here, purchased food and paid the server in cash. Server "forgot" to give me my change.... A significant amount, and then when I asked for my change back said she had already given it to me. No one else in there at the time so not sure how that got mixed up. Nice location but not impressed with the service or quality of food and drink for the price. 

Your review helps others learn about great local businesses.

Please don't review this business if you received a freebie for writing this review, or if you're connected in any way to the owner or employees.I will be there. Thanks

Vinyl rock "Cafe" - came here for a coffee... Weird right? Stay with me... Went to the counter to order said coffee and the reply from the girl behind the counter: "we don't have the staff to do that right now".  Weird ... 5 or so people behind the counter and a restaurant that looked empty.  Maybe don't call yourself a cafe and have a coffee mug for the logo? Definitely won't come here again.  

Thumbs up guys, thumbs up.

This Cora opened in the beginning of March.  Naturally, it was a very busy place and with staff being trained while trying to operate I was very impressed.

The second time I went to Cora's I was very disappointed in the quality of the food.  I had ordered the same meal as my first visit which was was exceptional at that time.  I did contact the head office and was then contacted by Sunny from the restaurant.  Sunny apologized profusely and asked that I give her restaurant another try.

Well, I went back today and was impressed again.  The food was exceptional and the fruit ripe.  I totally enjoy the fruit presentations!

Sunny did a wonderful job of assuring me that this is the quality I should expect every time I visit the location.  I intend to continue going to this location and recommend others do the same.

It is unfortunate that they do not have someplace for people to sit while they are waiting in line - most restaurants I visit offer this.  It is also unfortunate that they do not provide quicker wait times when you arrive with a party of five, especially when you have an 83 year old birthday girl with you.

If you like breakfast you will love Toast! This charming little restaurant is a family run business (hosted by an Irish family that ran a successful restaurant of the same name in Ireland).  Now with two locations one in St. Albert and one in Sherwood Park they are easily accessible for anyone in Edmonton or surrounding area.
The food is truly delicious and you can actually get tea by the pot (which if you drink tea like I do it's a big bonus!).  The eggs benedict is amazing and always done just the way I request. 
I would recommend this restaurant to anyone that enjoys tasty comfort food with an Irish twist! Oh and the service is great, they listen to your needs, they are attentive, and they are actually friendly from owner to host!

I'm originally from Eastern Canada so I'm glad to be able to enjoy one of my favourite places to go for brunch. 
Our family went to this location on Sunday. I was happy that, even though we arrived at lunchtime, we were seated right away. 
The staff was very nice and our waitress was great. The tables around were clean and ready and I noticed that as soon as people were leaving staff were quick to clean up and set up for the next people.
Our waitress offered us beverages right away and was good to come around during our meal to check on everything and to refill coffee as needed. 
While it can be pricy, especially as a large family, I find the portions are very generous. I love that there are so many options with plenty of fresh fruit! I enjoyed the "mountain of fresh fruit". It's a really big waffle topped with custard and loaded with a variety of freshly cut fruit. I do find the waffle tends to get a bit mushy by the end because of all the custard on top but it's still one of my favourites! 
Our order was prepared correctly and we didn't have to wait long for food and everything was good.

I've always had excellent service here. Staff are polite and interact with customers in a positive way.  Food is great and the selection is always plentiful. What would make this just a bit better is a better priced coffee ( It was over $3 for a coffee, that was not all that great). Also the crepes didn't seem to be made fresh.  They are a bit crusty on the edges.  I'll still go back as the food is pretty good and the service rocks.

Went there with a friend today based on pervious reviews and found the place totally disappointing. First impression was the noise even when there weren't that many people there. The acoustic was better employed for musicians. Secondly, I asked to substitute white pudding sausage with black but was given white. The fries were dry and obviously frozen variety that you can get at any supermarket. The omelette I had was cool at best.  I expected better but was totally disappointed. The soup my friend had was very good but she did not like the fries either, since she left most of it that I shared with her. I don't blame her. 
The salad that with with my meal was totally uninspired. 

Won't recommend this place i will I go there again. 
 Rating no star

We like to search out places for a great breakfast and Toast fits the bill perfectly. The Hollandaise was excellent and that is from my wife who was a chef for years and had to prepare it everyday. Omelet was excellent, as were the crepes. Highly recommended will return

When we moved to Edmonton a year ago, my wife and I began our search for a great local butcher. After meeting Kyle, the owner, at a Yelp event a few months back (my wife has been posting on this site a lot longer than I have) we decided to give them a try despite them being a bit of a hike from our south side house. 

Well, we're very glad that we did. We've been in about a half dozen times and the items we've purchased have always been fantastic. My personal favourite is their dry aged ribeyes, which I consider the best in metro Edmonton. They also had an amazing block of pancetta on one occasion (unfortunately they have not had it since, although on our last visit Kyle told us that he'd hired someone who specializes in cured meats that is starting in September who will be doing pancetta and a number of other similar type items). We've tried a number of other fresh and frozen products.

They are also the only place in Alberta which sells my absolute favourite steak spice (Sexy Spice, made by a small Toronto based company), although they were disappointingly out the last time we were there.

Kyle has personally served us and answered our questions on three of our visits. Once we really needed skewers and they didn't have any pre-made, but when asked about them he quickly made us some bison ribeye skewers (our request) on the spot. 

They also have a really great deal where if you sign up for their e-mail club they send you a coupon for two-for-one ribeyes and a free steak spice. 

They are the only place in metro YEG that I have seen that sells sell Wagyu beef (which is the American version of Kobe beef) which I REALLY want to try at some point, although I'll need to find a time I can get there when it's fresh, as all I've seen is frozen and if I'm treating myself to beef that expensive, I really want to throw it on the grill that day.

My only complaint is that the last time we were there their prices seemed to have been significantly higher than previous visits. I understand the price of beef has gone way up, and that pork is in short supply, so I am certainly not averse to paying more for great meat and supporting independent butchers. However, it is quite a bit further for us than our other regular butcher and for some items (bacon, being one) the cost was almost double of what we ended up paying for bacon at our other butcher that same weekend. This hadn't been the case previously. Not sure if our other place has simply not responded to market pressures yet, or if it was simply a supply and demand decision on D'arcy's part, but if prices stay that high, we won't be able to justify quite as frequent visits.

One other comment is that one of the reasons we frequent our other butcher is that they sell some pretty great dog treats (smoked pig ears and beef bones) that I haven't seen at D'arcy's. They may do them custom order, but I've never seen them out or advertised on their website.

All that to say, however, we will certainly keep going to D'arcy's whenever we get the hankering for amazing dry aged beef, or when we are making the trek to that neck of the woods. A great local butcher.

Absolutely love this butcher shop, the owner is so knowledgeable and friendly, when you tell him about a product you'd like to see, he'll actually make it happen. I understand he gets all of his meat from local producers, and most of it is hormone free (all of his pork and pork products), some nice grass-fed beef too. Those prices are a bit higher, but worth it in my opinion. 
The only item I've been missing for a while now were his deli meats, and he just brought them back, amazing!
Most of his staff is really great, the store is very busy so it happened to me that one staff member was a bit rushed, but it won't happen if you deal with the owner!
Absolutely recommend!!!

Hard to find when using the map on yelp!  Glad we finally did after driving around a few buildings as it was most enjoyable.  I had pancakes and bacon and my husband had an omelette with cheese, ham and mushrooms.  Service was great and the food came to the table piping hot after a short wait and was very tasty. Coffee was a bit of a disappointment but overall this place was great and we will be back.

I've got mixed feelings about Cora's.

We've been a handful of times now.

Service is hit and miss as are the prices.

$7 & under for a kids meal - great!

$4 for 1/2 of a sliced banana - WTF?!? I mean, when I asked for more banana I didn't expect a $4 fee!  It would have been nice to have been warned/advised.

A side of 4 slices of bacon costs less than 1/2 a banana! 

Crepes are ginormous and totally shareable.

Atmosphere is pleasant usually but something had burned in the kitchen on our last visit and it stunk so bad that my 5 year old didn't want to eat and asked if we could leave :-(

Another time we ordered coffee and never had a single refill?  At $4 for the world's smallest restaurant mug - we weren't pleased.

The kiddos always enjoy bringing a balloon home and colouring while they wait for their meals.

Amazing food! Everything is fresh and delicious. Our new favourite breakfast place! 

P.s. If going as a couple order the a main breakfast dish to share and order a fruit salad and scone. Fills you up and you have lots of variety to enjoy with your partner.

One of our favourite breakfast spots.   

Excellent food.  Great service.   You can't go wrong.  

Ann and her staff treat you like family.    Lines are normal on weekends but worth the wait.

The Bennie's were a little runny. Omelette was good and quite filling. The side salad is a nice touch with every breakfast. Noise carries in this place so it tends to be noisy when there are more than 4 tables. Decor is cute, what I expect from a diner. 

My only complaint was that we were not approached for coffee or water refills once. 
Prices are competitive with every other breakfast place in town. Parking is a nightmare.

My husband has been going to Toast for quite some time, but this was the first time for me.

I ordered the Classic Eggs Benedict and he ordered an Omelette.  We both ordered their dark roast coffee as well.  

When my order arrived I was surprised that there wasn't much hollandaise sauce but realized there was more than enough once I started eating.  I also am a fan of the crispy English Muffins!  The salad provided with the meal was just enough as there were ample potatoes as well.

My husband ate his salad first, which surprised me as he usually only enjoys Caesar salads.  He indicated that his omelette was delicious as well.  He was able to finish his potatoes, but had no room for anything else.

The service was friendly and quick.
 
My only complaint would be that there were no coffee refills.  The dark roast was so enjoyable  I would have appreciated another cup.

Great service and coffee! The food was fresh and hot, nothing wrong with it although it was not what I expected. A small cozy Irish family owned and run you would expect the food to reflect that. I had the eggs Benedict but the eggs are steamed in cups not poached in water, the hollandaise is not house made, it's knorr ready to use hollandaise, and for the Irish family to use a mccains premade deep fried hash browns I was disappointed. If you say Irish I would expect you know what a great fried potato is. 
Also the owner delivered the groceries through the front door, why not the back door. 
Wish you all the best but you need some work what food you want to serve.
Contacted the owner, Kyle,  by phone to ask about wholesale supply..Kyle got back to me in a couple of days with prices. Very helpful.

we decided on this place because it was close to the hospital... man was it ever a great choice!  it's a quaint spot tucked in a busy strip mall. the atmosphere is very dinerish.  I settled on the dark roast coffee and the florentine Benedict.  that was an amazing choice. at first doesn't look like a lot of sauce but it was perfect!  my daughter got crepes with fruit and a side of ice cream served with it... yep ice cream for breakfast she was a super happy girl!  the icecream was soft and fluffy almost like gelato!  would suggest this place for anyone wanting a feeling of homecooked meal with some special twists!  

definately I will be back!

If you are trying to explore foods and places like me, this is one of the places I would go. I like varieties. Been to some all-day breakfast but I find this quite interesting. I had the full Irish breakfast, loved their toasted Irish bread; heavy for just a slice. I like how they cook the potatoes, sausages kind of bland which I really love, alongside, they also have this beans which reminded me of home. Ambiance is like lay back and cozy. It's a nice place to have breakfast here.

This is my new favourite breakfast restaurant in St.Albert. My boyfriend and I go every Saturday for breakfast and never leave disappointed! The servers are very friendly and the menu has a great selection. The Eggs Benedict are some of the best I've ever had! The hollandaise sauce is homemade and delicious. The prices are fair for the serving size as well. I've never experienced the "dirty grill" taste here that so many other breakfast restaurants struggle with. A really great addition to the city!

If you would like to get grossly overcharged for an average quality job, take your wild meat to this place..... Would not send my worst enemy to this place. There are several butcher shops in and around Edmonton that are far superior to this place.
Both my hubby and I had the English breakfast. It was pretty good, quick service and a bit on the pricey side but all and all, we would definitely come back!

This was my first time at a Cora's, this location having recently opened in St Albert.  I'm assuming it's typical for the chain, with cutesy graphics on the wall, small tables, and fairly noisy.   It impressed me as quite a gathering place for friends to meet and eat - and eat VERY well.

Although it's a bit pricey (expect about $15 for breakfast), the quality - and quantity - is excellent.  Platters are filled with fresh, tasty choices ... LOTS and LOTS of variety with great pictures on the menu to help you decide.  Many times breakfast means grease and heavy carbs, but not here.  Food is "clean and healthy" while being absolutely delicious - worth every penny.  My platter included two light and blueberry-stuffed pancakes, eggs which were soft-scrambled exactly as requested, oven roasted (NOT fried) potato wedges, bacon, and fruit (there was a choice of fruit or tomato for garnish), plus toast in a dazzling array of choices.  It was every bit as yummy as it looked, and again I'd emphasize that it all seemed prepared in the healthiest way possible.

My only complaint, which my dining companion laughingly called me "old school" for thinking, was that I thought charging an extra $2.95 for a small mug of coffee seemed a little unnecessary considering the price of the meal -- I'd include it for free, personally  :-)  Other than that, however, big thumbs up for this new addition to the city mall - call up a friend and go treat yourself!

I expected something better, from the reviews. The breakfast was average, and on the higher scale of prices for this type of restaurant. My wife liked the eggs Benedict; I  had pancakes and found them filling but not as good as other breakfast places around - or home, for that matter.  The coffee was good and servers friendly and prompt, but I would not rank Toast as anything special.

Outstanding breakfast. Most places were closed on Canada Weekend. But I called TOAST and very nice lady said "Yes, were open."  So we followed the GPS and found this little place in the corner of a strip mall. Their service was terrific and super friendly. The breakfasts were way above average. 

Thanks, TOAST!!
Outstanding Rum and Banana Crepe! A wonderful place to eat if on a budget and like a good variety of choices. A must visit for sure! It won't disappoint your taste buds or wallet.

It was a cold and snowy morning and we had an appointment in St. Albert. Having missed breakfast we stopped into this nice gem of a place.  My wife had the French toast, I had the pancakes.   What a relief to have delicious pancakes like I make at home.  Chain restaurants serve the powdery commercial blend, but not this place.  Light and fluffy cakes that do not disintegrate when adding a bit of syrup.   I love the two options of coffee, and the local artwork distributed across the walls is not only beautiful, but for sale.  Highly recommend this place if you are looking for a home cooked breakfast.  Price was decent as well

Went around lunch time and was seated right away. Servers were very polite. Despite that it was 1pm, we can still order breakfast. Ordered a Spanish Omelette and chocolate chip pancakes. Omelette was done well. It came with salad and home cut potatoes. My favourite was the pancakes! Fluffy on the inside and slightly crispy on the outside. It was done perfectly. It seems like it was made by pouring a thin layer of batter  on the pan/griddle, then sprinkling the chocolate chips and then adding another layer of batter. Personally I think it's better to be incorporated with the batter then cooked. Still tasty none the less.

I signed up for Darcy's mailing list and got a sweet coupon for 2 for 1 rib eyes.  they were literally the best rib eyes I have ever purchased in Edmonton.  The quality of their meat is a cut above!  I went back and got myself a suckling pig leg for a dinner party and Kyle even came out of the back to debone it himself for me.  Can't wait to go back again and try their wagyu beef.  Looks amazing.  Only complaint is I live in SE Edmonton and they are in St. Albert, otherwise I would probably go there every week.

This small cafe is phenominal.  Excellent food.  Great prices. $8.25 for two eggs, irish bacon and crispy hash browns.
Excellent coffee.  They offered medium or dark roast.  When our coffee was refilled a couple of times Ann came back with cups of fresh coffee to replace the ones we were drinking from.
Awesome service.
Highly recommended.  They have captured me as a customer.

I have to say, we were just not wowed by this place. We decided to stop in as our regular butcher is on the south side, and we don't live there anymore. With a new little one, getting over there is becoming more of a challenge. D'Arcy's is a quick drive for us, and we were hoping it would be our new go to for fresh delicious meat. 

Don't get me wrong, they had some delicious looking steaks and roasts, but there was a surprisingly large amount if frozen product in the store. Not only that, but every sausage product we thought about getting had sulphites and artificial flavours in it. Because of my migraines, I can't have sulphites, sulfates, and should avoid nitrites and nitrates as well. I was expecting a butcher of such renown to skip on the fake stuff and keep it fresh and real. 

We did grab some Saskatoon berry bison jerky to try, and it was average. The berry flavour was a jam like glaze that flakes off when we ate it, leaving very little other flavour underneath. There is still a piece in our fridge, and for us that is saying a lot. 

My husband and I really wanted to like this place, but we just weren't feeling it. We shall continue to make the trek to Ellerslie to visit Real Deal.

I'm a fan!

Having recently moved back to St. Albert after more than a decade away, I'm having fun discovering all the new food in the area!  From what I can tell, Toast seems to have joined the scene in the last 2 - 3 years and we're sure lucky to have them!

According to the history on their website, Toast Breakfast & Lunch was first opened in a small town in Ireland.  Even before I read this, it was obvious that every staff member I encountered had a lovely Irish accent.  The Brady family moved here from Ireland and opened this location of Toast.

There isn't a waiting area, so if there is a lineup, you'll just be scrunched together in the doorway - and it does fill up on the weekends, so be prepared to wait a little.  The parking lot can be a little cramped, even on the weekend when the surrounding businesses aren't busy yet.  The is plenty of parking though... you just have to be prepared to walk across the parking lot.

The servers are all incredibly friendly.  As other reviewers have said, we weren't offered any coffee refills... but we didn't want any so I can't possibly deduct a star for it.

We shared the Classic Eggs benedict and a side of bacon.  Bacon was steep at $4.50 for 3 slices.  Eggs benedict is worth anything they want to charge for it... and next time I won't share it, I'll just get a whole order to myself.  It is by FAR my favourite eggs benedict.  The hollandaise was like nothing I've ever tasted.  I can't even put my finger on what was different about it but it was amazing.

When we were done, I asked (who I assume was the manager/owner) if they made the hollandaise in house and she proudly said yes.  I told her that it was the best I've ever had and she said that in all the time they've been open, they've only had 2 customers not like it (that they know of).  She was so proud of the food coming out of the kitchen.

I agree with others that the prices are high.  We had 1 coffee, 1 small orange juice, 1 eggs benedict, and 1 side of bacon and our bill came to just over $25.00.  But it's clear that everything is made fresh and they are very passionate about what they do.

There is a kid's menu, but no senior's menu, which is strange in St. Albert.

I will absolutely be back.  And I will absolutely not be sharing this time!

This place is AMAZING. We stopped in late in the afternoon on a warmish Saturday so the shop was getting to be a picked over (the manager apologized profusely for the lack of product but we found everything we were looking for and more so I can't even imagine how full the product cases are first thing in the morning!) but there was still so much meat available it was an absolute non-issue.  He was so excited telling us about the steaks and offering to cut all sorts of others for us if we didn't like exactly what we saw in the cases.  Not only did we like what we saw but when I checked in on my Yelp app I was given a 25% off all house made sausage discount code so we stocked up on smokies, pepperonis and other meaty snacks (whoo!).  Some prime rib steaks, a lobster tail, the sausages and we were good to go--and did we ever eat like kings after that.  He was not kidding, they were hands down the best pieces of meat I've ever had.  I can't wait to go back and try all of the other exciting things that we saw... it is going to be a very delicious summer, I can't wait.

The food is fine, typical breakfast food. The service was poor. My friend had already been seated when I arrived and I sat waiting for fifteen minutes not being offered anything to drink.
