I eventually flagged someone (not my waitress) to help. We ordered when my drink came and when the food came it was incorrect. Then when my friend was asked if she wanted more coffee it never came. She eventually had to flag someone down too. The only thing that came quick was the bill to rush us out for the line of people waiting at the door.

I've always enjoyed Cora thoroughly with every visit. The presentation of the dishes is always a treat and the selection is expansive. The prices can be steep, averaging about $25 a dish. Although this is a breakfast and lunch place, I'd love to see extended hours. Sometimes you can't always go brunching in the early hours. Other than cost and hours of operation, I have never had any issues with Cora and I have had a great time every visit.

Whoo!  Hoo!  Locally owned and operated by the same family since 1991 - does it get any better?  While D'Arcy has turned over the meat shop to his son, Kyle, he can still be found running their casual catering business (http://www.darcyscasualcatering.com/)

D'Arcy's Meat Market is filled with all kinds of awesome and local goodness!  I love that you can special order sausages or other meats prepared to your liking - including nitrate and preservative free!  I liked that the meat shop itself was wide open so you can watch how they prepare and process the meats from start to finish in the back end of the market.

The fresh meat butcher case made my mouth water and this is definitely the place to hit up for your perfect backyard BBQ.

I'm impressed at how many local and high end restaurants use D'Arcy's Meat Market as their supplier including both the River House, Jack's Burger shack, and Privada in St. Albert!  I've been lucky enough to try all kinds of meat ranging from elk to bison to pork loin roast served up fit for a king by our local chefs.  I've even seen Kyle debone a chicken WHOLE at an event.  If you need any tips, from the beginner to the experienced, Kyle is more than happy to help!  And if you're wondering, does he really know his stuff?  Heck yeah, he does!  Kyle graduated with honors and highest in class from N.A.I.T. with a Certification in Meat-Cutting.  If you're a nerd like me and want to read up on the store's history, check out their website at: http://www.darcysmeats.ca/

We checked in on Yelp on our most recent trip and snagged a 25% off sausages check-in reward!  George, being the great front end manager that he is, showed us some other things we just couldn't resist so we walked out with enough treats for the week!  I mean lamb sausages?  Yes PLEASE!  And a delicious boneless smoked pork chop that is great as is cold or pan fried for a bit of a crust.  George was also knowledgeable in discussing ways for us to cook what we purchased today.  I really appreciates the tip that I can boil the sausages from frozen and then pop out on the grill to get the marks or casing cooked to my specification.  This was a super easy way to ensure that my sausages were plump and juicy on the inside while still cooked crispy (the way I like it) on the outside!

If you sign up for their newlsetter on http://www.darcysmeats.ca/ you will find a lovely surprise 2-for-1 ribeye coupon in your inbox!  I know what we're gonna have for supper this weekend!

With so many options including local, free rage, and hormone/antibiotic free - you just can't go wrong with D'Arcy's!  As mentioned by other reviewers, the price range is at the higher end of meat markets.  If you are looking to stock up your freezer, ask them about ordering a 1/4 or 1/2 cow to your specification.  This may not be a discount store, but you can certainly shop the weekly deals or buy a larger amount at a time to save moola.

Would I buy ALL my meat here for a 200 person family reunion?  Probably not?  Would I like to?  Heck yes!  Will I come back again and again for speciality items or that perfect steak for father's day?  You betcha I will! 

Thank you D'Arcy's for rocking it local and fresh!

Oh man! I love going out for breakfast and I definitely love going out to toast!

My boyfriend and I always get amazing service and the food is so quick and tasty. It has an amazing eggs Benny and the eggs Italiano is to be tasted!!  

You can order true Irish breakfast here including Blood Pudding!!!
It wasn't bad. Way too pricy for "average food". I wouldn't bother going there again. There is better places for breakfast/lunch.

Forgot to review it on the same day as I went there but the breakfast was amazing. Everything was fresh. Good sized portions. Real hash browns none of that grated potatoe, half cooked garbage most other chains have switched to. I had the eggs Benedict. Really good hollandaise sauce. Give this place a shot. You won't be disappointed.

Good experience, very nice and friendly ambiance! 

Cute restaurant, tucked away in the st.Albert complex. Love the decor. 

Ordered spinach crepes with hollandaise sauce. Crepes were cooked perfectly and filled deliciously. The hollandaise sauce wasn't the best, but is only drizzled on top. Not a big deal!

Sweetest server. Huge smile and seems to genuinely love her job.

Quaint and cute place, recommended !

St Albert has had two recent trends... Fast food burger joints (6 and counting) and breakfast cafes (2-3 new ones in the past year). Toast is the newest member on the block and they look like a force to be reckoned with! Serving authentic Irish favorites like black & white pudding imported from Ireland as well as English/Irish bacon they are showcasing the food from their country quite well. 

The full Irish breakfast has eggs, 3 different meats, beans, tomatoes, homefries and of course their namesake... Toast! Now that's a hearty first meal of the day! 

They are open most days until 3pm so you can have your breakfast for lunch as well! I haven't tried the coffee yet but if they've put as much thought into that as their food then I'm sure its good! 

The restaurant is tucked away in the corner of a shopping complex and has a bakery and pub as neighbors. The parking lot can get somewhat full but there is overflow spots that are still very close. The decor is simple and clean with a homey touch of some books lining a shelf. 

I enjoy a good breakfast/brunch and I'm looking forward to enjoying many of the options that Toast offers!

I took my Irish mate here because someone told us that they had a proper full Irish breakfast. The breakfast comes with eggs, toast, bacon, pudding, beans, and fried tomatoes. It was approved of and appreciated by the Irish lad who had been missing having a fry up like at home. I had a burger with poutine. The burger was very good but the poutine was very disappointing. It came with grated  mozzarella and floury gravy but the fries underneath were very good. I will say the service here was some of the worst o have experienced. There was no greeting and we were left standing by the door for close to 10 minutes. When we were finally sat things moved very slowly and it took forever to get the bill and pay at the end. I think this is a great spot if you know someone from Ireland or the UK and they want a full breakfast.

Went at 9am on a Saturday and had no problems getting in, however shortly after we were seated a line started to form. The atmosphere is comforting and homey, and I liked the local art that you can buy that's hung on the walls. I think it's supposed to be an Irish restaurant  because there's an Ireland flag hung up on the wall and there's an Irish version of an eggs benny, but other than that I saw no sign of Ireland, which is kind of confusing. My friend and I both ordered the classic eggs benny. Pretty good hollandaise but definatly not worth the drive from Edmonton. The sauce is creamy and lemony. They aren't generous with the hollandaise however, so I would suggest ordering a side of it. The potatoes were definatly from the frozen section in a grocery store. Service was pretty good, with the waitresses constantly asking if we needed more coffee. We did have to ask for our bill however. Overall it was pretty good. The staff were good and the food was good as well. I wouldn't ever drive from Edmonton again but it was good to try.
Shouldn't give such a high rating, because everyone will want to go there. Food is fantastic, Prices are great, Staff is friendly and helpful. My new favorite restaurant in St. Albert.

This place is the best! It's small, so it can get really crowded (as it did when I picked up my Thanksgiving turkey last weekend), but they have just about everything you might ever need. Lots of fresh meats but lots of good frozen stuff too like game meat and sausages. They have great marrow bones (Safeway ones are gross in comparison) - perfect for roasting and eating with rye bread, parsley salad, and a sprinkle of Maldon sea salt (à la Fergus Henderson).

Anything you need, just call them ahead of time - they are friendly, knowledgeable, and willing to take the time to talk to you about your needs. I had wanted a small turkey for Thanksgiving and when I called a week ago, the lady on the other end of the phone knew right away that she had a 12-lb turkey in her freezer that had been delivered the week before; did I want her to put that aside for me? Sure did!! When I went to pick it up on Saturday, the place was a zoo, but all staff members were on hand to help out and move things along. The turkey itself was great - smelled like a happy fresh bird out of the bag and tasted even better :) I will definitely be picking up another bird for my upcoming turducken project (along with the duck and chicken) - though I'm told that for a nominal fee, they will assemble it for you! 

They also sharpen knives for a nominal fee - I usually bring mine in twice per year. I think I would shop here a lot more often if I lived closer - otherwise, the only drawback for me is that they aren't open on Sundays, but I guess the butcher has to rest too :)
Came from out of town. First time I'm in a lineup at the door to get into a breakfast place! The deliciousness of the food explained why we had to wait to get in

Wow, wow, and yes wow. I feel like that is basically 'nuff said... But in case it's not: 

This is place is the mecca of meat. The king of edible animal awesome. At D'Arcy's they are rock stars in the restaurant world, supplying meats to some of the best dining establishment in the city. But you and me and every normal person out there can also walk in and become King or Queen of the grill in your own back yard with just a bit of guidance and the amazing cuts from D'Arcy's Meat. 

The 'stuff' in the coolers like smokies, hotdogs and jerky look too amazing to pass up. They are more expensive then what you would pay at Save-On or Safeway but just by looking at the colour you know it is going to be more then worth it! I will most definitely do a follow up, but for now, I am just so excited that I made the trip out to St Albert to find D'Arcy's and I can't wait to start grilling!!
Great breakfast spot in St.Albert. our second time here, I had the Irish breakfast and my girlfriend had the veggie omelet. Hot, fresh and delicious.

We went here for breakfast. It was excellent. They have a great variety. They have gluten free options available as well (you do need to ask your server). The gluten free pancakes are delicious, you get 3 huge ones. Plus your choice of side. You can get fruit with them as well. Their crepes are delicious as well (not gluten free unfortunately). I do believe they make them from scratch. The bacon and egg crepes are delicious. 
There is a great variety on the menu which is always nice. Coffee is good, you can get regular or dark roast. 
The service was great, friendly. It was a week day on this visit so not overly busy. However on weekends this place is generally packed. It is on the smaller side with not a lot of seating so sometimes there can be a bit of a wait for a table, but it's worth it. 
It's located in a strip mall, lots of parking available.

I've been to Cora's now a half dozen times or so since it opened in St. Albert.

Both the food and service have been hit and miss.

Somethings on the menu are priced excellent and others make no sense - like $4 for a half a banana that I think my wife mentioned in her review.

I'm happy that bacon costs less than the banana because my son ALWAYS wants an extra side or two of bacon.  I mean, the boy's got good taste.

The fruit is always fresh and the food is hot but the wait times can be all over the place.

Also, we've been here when something like toast gets burned in the kitchen and it stinks up the entire restaurant due to the open concept.  

I don't know about you, but burned food really turns my stomach.  

So does $3 for a small cup of coffee that never got refilled.

So Cora's, you have improvements to make but still offer up a wide variety of family friendly breakfasts that are sure to delight the pickiest eater in the crowd.

I love brunch and my favourite is egg-benedict   I got to try "The Surfer" which has 2 poached eggs with smoked salmon and red onions (i asked to omit) on a grilled english muffin with a dill hollandaise. The grilled english muffin made a huge difference! The crunchy-ness of the bread made everything taste better. I'm not a huge fan of dill but it complimented the salmon taste. 

For those who don't know or haven't heard of Toast - it is an Irish family own restaurant located in Sherwood Park and St. Albert. I havent worked up the courage yet to try an Irish dish but i will next time I stop by.
Excellent breakfast and cheap :) . Service was good and fast , deco was nice too . Small Irish feel , we loved it
Great prices, friendly servers and amazing food. Best breakfast place in St.Albert for sure.

Wonderful grass fed, pasture raised choices for beef, pork and chicken and cold northern manitoba fish.  Loving the prices, the selection and the social media interactions on facebook, twitter etc.

After my favorite deli for 10 years had burned down, I was left wanting of a new meat place that met my grass fed pasture raised criterion.

I buy a lot of my meat directly from the farmer.  I've toured his farm and gotten to know him and his family.  However, he's occasionally out and i can only purchase wh'ole chicken from him. I'm in need of some other local options.

Darcy's is on the south east corner of St. Albert and they're easy to get in and out of from Northern Edmonton.  

Then there's the selection.  I'm overjoyed.

Wild northern cold lake fish, 
Gluten free sausages
Bison
Pork, certified hormone free and farmed 15 minutes away
Elk - Lacomb Elk

They're BUSY too.. a great sign of a good place and a understanding that they may be out of things when you get there... so they're stock is constantly changing.

I'm stoked.
 
I spent a good 30 minutes interviewing the meat cutting girl (from NB) about their sources and getting to know their standards and such.  Most of their products met with my satisfaction.

Totally worth the trip... stock up... try it all.

Thanks to the gang handling my food there and a shout out to the social media guy tweeting all the time.

Cheers

Rob - @formerfatguy

This place is amazing! Great homemade food for great prices and friendly warm staff. You can come for breakfast or lunch and the menu has so many great options. Plus the special everyday is something new that is not on the menu. So the variety is appreciated. Hands down best breakfast/lunch in St. Albert!

The place was busy with a short lineup when we arrived. No one greeted us at all, they definitely looked understaffed as the waitresses were clearly overwhelmed. They cleared a four top for the three of us and then some old dude (clearly a regular) decided to seat himself there even though he was alone and there were two tops available. The waitress said she had meant to seat us there, but didn't say anything to the guy. Luckily another table was opening up at that moment.
The food was underwhelming to mediocre. My french toast was more regular toast than french toast (not dipped long enough). My husband's eggs benedict didn't have enough hollandaise for his liking. It was pretty pricey for the amount of food ($50 for the three of us, one being a toddler). The service was really terrible. When the bill came she ran by and dropped the bill and the machine at the same time. She didn't even break her stride and kept on moving without comment. Maybe it'd be better if they were staffed correctly? She was clearly busy.

Exactly as advertised: a simple but well executed breakfast offering at an affordable price. Service was prompt and polite, and the meal itself looked to use high-quality ingredients, which often isn't the case for many of Toast's value-focused, chain-restaurant competitors. Good espresso-based coffee in addition to standard drip. It appeared to be Irish-owned and our server was also Irish.

This place was awesome! I looked at the menu beforehand and the veggie sandwich sounded great. When we got there it wasn't on the menu I asked our server and she said their menu had changed a bit. She asked the chef if he could prepare one and he said yes. It was so good! I got fries and the chefs salad with the house balsamic vinaigrette. I'll definitely be back!

My mom and I shared a gluten free pancake breakfast here with eggs and sausage.  The mean feed both of us and was really tasty. My mom is a regular here and sleeks very high of it as she is celiac and can not eat gluten.  I would eat there again.

Cute and quaint and definitely delicious. This is a small little place, so when I came on a Sunday in the early afternoon I was shocked to even get a table, but my mother and I managed to with no wait. The homey decor and what I assume is local art on the wall makes for a great atmosphere.
The menu is standard breakfast/brunch/lunch fare. Lots of egg dishes, cubed potatoes, and sandwiches. Everything is averagely priced.
I opted for a healthier alternative and got poached eggs with a fruit salad and cottage cheese. It's a fairly easy meal to make, but all that aside it still tasted great. The coffee is great and the service was even better, which impressed both of us because they appeared to be understaffed. 
Overall everything was exactly what I would expect from a place of this nature.
If you're an early riser or in need of a little brunch, I recommend stopping by.

Came around 1 on a Saturday, so it was pretty quiet - though I can see it being very busy if we'd been there for the breakfast crowd. Service was really friendly and prompt, which was nice since we were in a bit of a hurry.

The Surfer Benedict (smoked salmon) came with a healthy portion of potatoes and a side salad. The salad didn't seem like a great match - a fruit salad would have worked better. The Benedict was cooked properly, but the dill hollandaise wasn't our favourite. It came out too creamy, and was reminiscent of a mayonnaise more so than a hollandaise. 

The full Irish breakfast had a lot going on: two eggs, sausage, baked beans, Irish bacon, potatoes, grilled tomato and toonie-sized pieces of black & white pudding...oh, and toast (or you could have Irish bread instead). The white pudding was delicious! Crispy, flavourful and a nice change to typical breakfast fare. The black pudding didn't have as much flavour. My bacon was over cooked so it was tough and dry. Very sad face. :( Aside from the white pudding, the rest of the items were pretty standard and didn't really jump out at me.

Both breakfasts and a coffee came to $40ish before tip. Not the cheapest breakfast option, but I liked that there were things that you don't always see offered.

I've been to this place a few times now and have always left wanting to go back again. This  is a nice little spot tucked into a corner of Inglewood Towne Center by the Crown and Tower pub in St. Albert. Inside you will find a warm inviting setting filled with an assortment of books and nic nacks giving the place an eclectic homey feel. The food offers a homestyle menu with a touch of Irish flair. I've had their mushroom burger and was very impressed with it considering this is more of a breakfast/lunch kinda place. Their Ruben sandwich is also quite tasty. Unless you are very lucky don't be surprised if you find a slight lineup to get in because this place is quite popular and has its regulars. There is usually parking close by with many spots in the larger parking lot that serves the strip mall. If you're looking for a nice cozy, non franchise place for a coffee and snack with a friend this place could be just the place you're looking for.
Food is so yummy here. My daughter loves the jam and I love the vegan options! I've had the avo toast and the tofu paneer on toast options and both are . We will be back for sure!

I adore D'Arcy's Meat Market. Their cuts are absolutely amazing and, to make things better, they source everything from local farmers! 

I've had excellent sirloin, sausages, and skirt steak from D'Arcy's and can't wait to go again. The skirt steak was unbelievable - tender, flavourful, and oh-so-good!!

The owner, Kyle, is a really nice guy and is extremely passionate about his business and about local produce. I've had the chance to interview him for my blog and he's definitely got the right idea in terms of eating right and supporting local!

If all you ever eat is Save On/Costco/Safeway/Superstore meat, branch out and give this place a try. Chances are you'll never want mass market meat again.

This is truly one of the hidden gems in St. Albert! The food is always tasty and the service is always great. The pricing is fair and you can tell people love it here since there's always a lineup at the door on the weekends! The atmosphere itself is unique and it's decorated so nice. Support local and enjoy your breakfast there for sure!

Decided to try this place when we were down in St. Albert based on the reviews on Yelp. However, I left feeling quite disappointed.

When we walked in, no one acknowledged us and when we eventually got seated, the hostess/waitress was quite rude. Maybe she was juggling many tasks?

We ordered the specialty toast sandwich and eggs Benedict both with fries. The fries were exactly like Costco food court fries and I'm willing to bet they were frozen since they were quite mushy.

The specialty toast sandwich was just a piece of bread loaded with tomatoes, a chicken breast, and cheese. I thought the topping was delicious with the balsamic vinegar but the  bread on the bottom was saggy. However, that was to be expected since that's what happens when you put tomatoes on toast.

The Eggs Benedict was pretty average. We ordered our eggs medium but they unfortunately came back well done. The hollandaise was quite bland and tasted a bit gritty. 

All in all, I didn't have the best experience at Toast but perhaps it was just an off day for them.

I was here last Sunday with my fiance, and although our service was good, the food was...extremely close to inedible at best. We came later into the brunch service (between 1:30-2, I believe), and I ordered a smoked salmon omelette. What I got was the thinest piece of shoe leathered eggs with some salmon and very sad looking capers thrown on top. There was absolutely no flavour besides the salmon and the salt of the capers, the potatoes we received were extremely soggy, and in all honesty, if I hadn't been starving from running around doing errands all day, I wouldn't have eaten it at all. With a price point that now competes with higher end breakfast establishments like OEB, I would have expected something at least pleasant to eat.

I typically really enjoy Cora, so this was quite the disappointment. Maybe this was just an off day or an off location, but I can't say we'll be back.

Random stop on our way to a different event. I don't live in St Albert so this stop was especially a pleasant surprise. Hungry for breakfast, Toast did not disappoint. Small, quaint and trendy Cafe with Irish roots. Small bookshelf with interesting art pieces along the wall. Accommodating for all, individuals and families. Fast seating and friendly service. We ordered brunch: pancakes, omelets, came with toast and hash-browns.  Reasonably priced for delicious food. Wide variety of options. Coffee fresh and unlimited. Located in the corner of a shopping complex, parking lot tends to be busy but there is overflow spaces. Wifi is available.

Returned for another "breakfast treat" and ordered the same meal simply because I enjoyed it so much last time.  Sadly, today's plate did not have me waxing quite as poetically.  While it was still tastier than usual breakfast fare and a visual treat as well, the eggs were obviously cooked by someone different and were over-scrambled and cold (as were my companion's) and my pancakes hadn't felt any heat for a while, either.  Right now I'm not feeling the love for a third visit for just myself, although I would take a newbie guest simply because I've not found anywhere else that meets their standards.  I would, however, voice my disappointment a bit more strongly to the waitstaff, in the hopes something might be done to rectify cold food.

I'm really not sure what the hype is about this place. It's mediocre in both food and service.  Mind you, I came on a busy weekend so  staff were run off their feet. We waited several minutes to be  acknowledged and then seated. A simple acknowledgement would have been nice but staff just walked past until they were ready for you.  I observed all customers experience the same lack of acknowledgment.  I think this restaurant is supposed to be modelled after a European style breakfast place, so I guess this is standard treatment. Food came out very quickly and was your typical and average restaurant food. Nothing unique.  I'd give it 4 stars but this place lacks in the hygiene department. For example, servers were observed  wiping the seats of tables and then wipe the table with the same cloth.  I'd come here again but there are some other great restaurants in town much more worthy of my money.
Great eats great service great menu short hours though open till 3pm on Sundays lots of fruit on the dishes

Makes an edible breakfast but given the price they charge I expected both more food and a little better quality. Portions are on the small side with the average omelette priced about $15 and while 3 egg they are small eggs. Also, neither the fries or hash browns are gluten friendly. They do have gluten free bread though. Service is just average. Friendly and gets the job done but with only 2 waiting on tables they are stretched  when busy. Final point, restaurant in REALLY loud inside. There are a lot of better breakfast places in St Albert. Even Ricky's to me is a step up from this.

We went for brunch yesterday and got in right away. The service was prompt and she was very friendly. We had our baby with us and she had him smiling and laughing. Food was really good. Both our eggs were cooked perfectly and the proper portion sizes.  Defiantly coming back to try your pancakes! They looked delightful.

This is my favourite breakfast place. The staff are incredibly friendly, and the hollandaise is delicious. All of their Eggs Benedict options offer their own twist on the hollandaise, which is fresh and fun. My mom always orders a side of hollandaise with her meal, whether or not it is a benny. I love that you can get black and white pudding and soda bread! Their homemade soups are incredible, especially if you love a good Cream of Mushroom or Clam Chowder. Hashbrowns here are deep fried cubes, but you can always substitute fruit if those aren't for you. (I'm a shredded potato person, myself, but I still like the cubes, and my husband loves them.) Sandwiches like the Dubliner come with real roast beef, and their fries are always crispy. This is just a small, quaint place, so expect to stand in line during the weekend rush.
Still fairly new and working out the bugs.  Busy and somewhat disorganized.  Food was cool but good.  Waitress not engaged and disappointed in the service.

I've been here many many times. The staff are great really friendly but don't hang around you which I love. We come here for the Irish/English breakfast it offers pudding bacon and sausages like home. The Sosa bread fried is a must FYI when they offer you a choice of bread go for it!! The reason for the 3 stars tho instead of 5 well they have stopped using the nice tea and baked beans from home they used to it was a major plus for me. Especially the cup of tea I was so disappointed when I tasted it on my last 2 visits. Also I think at the weekends they pre cook it all I get it it's so busy but the bacon was very dry the last 2 weekend visits.. Overall it's a nice treat and saves me from cooking but I know it can be better it was before....

Visited this little hidden Traditional Irish Gem, tucked away in a corner of a busy plaza in the St. Albert area.

The service was swift, and just saying that simply isn't enough.

Our server had us sanitize our hands before entering and seated us promptly thereafter and took our beverage order.

We both ordered the hungry man, with a few additions.

The food was amazing, very cheap and affordable. Made with that special "home made care" we all love and crave so much.

The service and the meal were pretty amazing, planning on returning there very soon.

Visit this restaurant for a unique dining experience and happy dining!

I hope your experience is as amazing as mine or better!
Was one of the first places I was told to go to when I arrived in St. Albert. Nice place, good food excellent staff. They work too hard. Give them bigger tips.

This seems like the kind of place where you pay $6 at the counter when you walk in and they yell "order up" from the kitchen for you to go grab your food.  The decor is simple and the food is mediocre.  And it's not $6.

The service throughout is extremely efficient and friendly and the food can be relied upon to taste good and be warm if not hot.  It's a great place to go to saunter over breakfast or to go for a quick breakfast as the food comes out super quick!

Wonderfully Wet and Wild Wonderland... Okay enough with the alliteration, I know!

But seriously, we just visited this Spray Park for the first time and I was absolutely blown away!  I only took a few pics but will definitely upload more after our next visit.

The spray area is huge with 3 separate sections - all geared towards different ages.  I really appreciated the fact that they had sections that were more appropriate for wee ones!  They have a snack shack that serves hot and cold food & slushies - of course! 

And an even bigger surprise, they have an amazing playground complete with a spongy rubber floor to play on while the kids dry off!  And the playground was HUGE too with different levels of climbing and slides - again geared to meet the needs of multiple ages groups.

There are staff on site - although this is definitely not a daycare drop off sort of situation.  There are both male, female, and family change rooms/washrooms.  There is a skateboard/bike park right behind the spray park and loads of baseball and sporting fields!  This park is huge!

I was also impressed with the number of covered benches available providing lots of shade in addition to the grassy knoll areas.

The spray park and playground are fenced in with only one entrance/exit located directly in front of the snack shack - a definite bonus when having to watch and chase multiple yard apes... Oops, I meant children :-)

A huge 2 thumbs up... I'm even considering having my toddler's birthday party here this summer!

This is the St. Albert river valley. The Sturgeon River flows alongside the paths used by walkers, cyclists, and joggers. I brought my bike here last summer and rode around a bit - the trail system is reasonably complex and very beautiful.

Summer came early this year so a lot of the spray parks aren't open yet but St. Albert is. Tons of parking as well as a large grassy area with shade trees to retreat from the hot sun. The spray park itself is bigger than most and the have added a play park with slides and swings for a break from the water. They have a large first aid station as well as big bathrooms. The concession stand is big and well stocked. All in all a great place to take the kids to cool off.

This continues to be my family's Favourite spray park!

It's not as large as some like Jackie Parker or Castle Downs but it is enclosed by a fence and has ample shade and grassy tree lined areas for a perfect siesta.

There is also the snack shack and St Albert rec staff on hand at all times for first aid.

Last summer we visited more than 20 spray/splash parks and this one still knocks it outta the park!

St. Albert has really invested a lot in Red Willow Park locations over the past decade or so. A lot of people are familiar with the splash park and skate park near Woodlands. I've got to say that I've always been impressed with the network of paths in St. Albert. As a kid I used to ride my bike everywhere. Sometimes I'd have a destination, other times I just followed a path to see where it would take me.

They've added maps and kilometer markers in the past decade or so. It's really neat that you can measure out your workout that way if you choose. The 0KM mark is just behind St. Albert Place. You'd have to check the maps to see how it's structured. The paths are very well maintained and multi-user friendly.

This place is definitely 5 star. It is a clean and safe place to spend an afternoon or even an entire summer day. The canteen is decently priced so you can even have lunch here too. If the kids get bored playing in the water the playground area is pretty great as well. I love that St. Albert has this splash park available to all for free

Best park EVER - I feel so fortunate to have this little paradise right here in St Albert!

The Spray Park is a child's wonderland - three large areas for different ages/stages, ample washrooms including one for families, lots of seating including shaded areas, a snack bar with hot and cold treats, a first aid station for those inevitable spills, grassy areas for picnicking, and so much space it never feels crowded.  Your child will instantly make new friends with lots of giggles.  We love to take along a bunch of squirt guns, buckets, pump sprays, etc. from the dollar store and share.   

Right next door, figuratively speaking, is a great playground area with one of those spongy rubber "floors" that cushion falls and are kind to bare feet.  Again, lots of different apparatus aimed at all ages - let your kids dry off here before loading them in the car.  Between the water, climbing, and sunshine, you may get them to nap or fall asleep early, a no-charge bonus!

Consider having your young one's birthday party here - we've done two and they were smashing successes.  You can bring in your own food, decorations, etc, come early to claim a couple tables or area in the grass, and let the kids be kids.  

Love watching the skate park just a bit away - gosh, there's some real talent out there - some FEARLESS talent  :-D

All in all, a wonderful way to spend the day.  Dress for wet, even if you don't expect to indulge initially, because you'll find it hard to resist joining your happy children and they'll love splashing you.  And don't forget the sunscreen!!

As far as spray parks go, Woodlands is the best one I've found by far. 

The Trophy Wife and I (with our trophy kids) have been on a quest for the best spray park in the greater Edmonton area. After trying seemingly countless spray parks, the little gem (that is conveniently only 10 minutes from our house) is exceptional.

It boasts a very large water area (with recycled water, I might add), a big dry playground, a large green belt, four shaded areas with benches and many huge trees for shade! 

As a wonderful safety feature, the entire park is fenced off to prevent little ones from venturing off into the parking lot, road or adjacent skate park. It only has one entrance/exit so parents can always keep an eye on whether or not their kid sneaks out. 

There is a concession stand, nice big restroom/change rooms and an overall feeling of comfort in letting your children run amok. The park is fully staffed, garbage cans are emptied, change rooms are kept clean and there is a First Aid room available for minor cuts and boo boos.

The water is turned on when the outdoor temperature reaches 16 degrees Celcius or warmer. I think we came here in late May, at one point. 

I love to grab the kids, a lawn chair and a cold drink and head down to Woodlands. I'll let my kids go crazy while I park my arse underneath a shady tree, with my ice cold Coke Zero (shameless plug) and write Yelp reviews. 

Bring your kids to Woodlands! Expect to make a day of it! Maybe bring a cooler of your favorite bevys and snacks. Make sure your smart phone or tablet is fully charged. Yelp will appreciate it.

Heat wave, schmeet wave! The best place in St. Albert to cool is definitely at Woodlands Water Park. We have gone a few times this year, early June and it was quite cold to the plus 30 degrees and have a great time each time.

As on now there are no capacity limits or lines ups which was great when it is so hot. There is a concession on site as well so if you want a cool treat it is covered.

Bathrooms are also on site so please of for the love of all things that are fun have your children use the washroom. We went when a (hopefully) child left a log and the staff were quick to close the park down, clean the deck and the water treated.

Also there is a nice sized park right in the same area and picnic tables. Lots of places to sit or there is lots of grass to lay a blanket down. But double thumbs up to the staff that monitor the park, they are the real mvps.

I've given this shop two chances, and I don't think they'll get a third. 

For Christmas I needed a goose and went to them for a high quality bird. I called ahead and made arrangements to have a large goose put aside. Due to limited hours, I sent my cousin who lives in St. Albert to pick it up on my behalf. When he arrived, they didn't have one on hold. It caused a little bit of chaos, but in the end we got our goose. The problem is, we paid almost $90.00 for it, and they paid $35.00 to their supplier. Now, I get overheard and travel, but considering they purchased it from a colony, close to the city, it was way overpriced. Not to mention, there was no discernible difference in quality between this goose and the one I purchased last year from K&K Foodliner for $50.00, which was the same size.

To be fair, I tried to give this place a second chance. They had a special on variety packs for the month of January so I called in advance to make sure that I could make substitutions, as me and my partner aren't big pork eaters. They assured me that I could and so I decided to head out to St. Albert and take a chance.

Here's what was advertised: 

Variety Pack

5lb. AAA Top Sirloin Steak (About 10 steaks)
5lb. Baron of Beef Roast (2x2.5lb.)
10lb. Lean Ground Beef (8-10 packs.)
5lb. Centre Cut Pork Chops (wrapped 2/pack)
5lb. Pork Loin Roast (2x2.5lb.)
5lb. Signature Pork Sausages (choose from: Maple, Breakfast, Chorizo, Andouille, Italian, Bratwurst, Medisterpolse, Loukaniko, or mix and match)
3lb. Boneless Skinless Chicken Breast or 1 Whole Chicken
2lb. Chicken Drumsticks, Thighs, or Legs 

$199.99 Each - 40lb. @ $5.00/lb.!

We ended up subbing out the pork roasts and chops. However, they weren't overly pleasant or helpful with the substitutions. They were impatient with us as we carefully made our decision. We were told that we could sub for anything in the store so we chose to get a ham and stewing beef. The problem is that the substitutions were made a full dollar value rather than the $5.00 per/lb price. We ended up getting only half a ham and 1.5 lbs of stewing beef for what they said was $70.00 worth of meat. They allowed substitutions but it basically made the box a sub par value. 

Apparently, after heading to Facebook and reading comments, written by the person in charge of their social media account, there are two different options for substitutions. Either by dollar value or fair weight substitution at $5.00 per pound. We were only given option one, and the second option was not explained. We ended up getting far less meat, and for a couple on a budget, it was a tough thing to swallow. I ended up feeling like they had taken advantage of our lack of knowledge and as we felt rushed, we didn't get the best bang for our buck. To add to that, while I was in the store, I didn't feel like a valued customer. 

Not the best experience either time, so I won't be back. There are better butcher shops that aren't as far away.

Best customer service ever!  Kyle, all the staff actually, are always ready to help in any way.  First time in there, we had never barbecued beef ribs before.  Not only did Kyle take the time to inform us on the types of cuts, but his preference, as well as how to (in his opinion) properly cook them.  He spent a decent amount of time with us, making sure we were fully satisfied and confident in what we were doing.  It was a very impressive first experience!  And we receive the same great service every time we go in :)

Great quality meat as well.  My boyfriend can not eat pork from a regular grocery store (huge stomach upset) but he can eat Darcy'y pork no problem! This is a sure testament to good quality, well taken care of, no filler/funny business meat.  
Only butcher we go to :)

Ps-they will cook your turkey dinner for you, carved and all, if you require such a service.

After writing my last review D'Arcy's reached out to me to correct the issues that I had experienced. I really appreciated both Kyle and Ryan and their willingness to listen to customer issues and to make things right. 

When we returned to the store, at Kyle's request, Ryan was there and ready to help. We were given extra stewing beef and a ham on the house to account for the previously mentioned substitution problems and we were offered a full store credit for the cost of the goose that we purchased at Christmas. Ryan also gave us great advice on the types of sausage we should purchase with part of our credit. He was welcoming and enthusiastic. He made us feel like valued customers.

They've gone well above and beyond any other business that I've dealt with when it comes to fixing a bad customer experience. We will definitely be doing business with them in the future and you should too.

Would highly recommend this place, very good selection on cuts of meat and a wide range of products that compliment their foods. Customer service is very good and the staff are always there to help me with explaining knowledge about my choices.

This new Floral Boutique in St Albert is stunning!! Each and every arrangement was breathtaking and there is no competition when it comes to price!! Defiantly the lowest prices in town hands down! I had the pleasure of meeting the owner/florist and she is amazing. Not only friendly but went out of her way to make sure I was thoroughly satisfied. There was a dissatisfied customer from a different floral shop nearby at the same time I was in, and she went over and above to make her happy with her new and unique bouquet she put together on the spot. This will be my floral boutique from now on! Congrats to Charmed Floral!!

Still the best butcher around! 

D'Arcy's continues to offer both local and the best cuts of meat!

Nowhere else will you find a meat shoppe with this level of passion and care. 

From custom made smokies to butcher value packs, D'Arcy's has got you covered! 

I highly recommend following them on social media to keep abreast of their current promotions and sales.  

I've never bought anything here I didn't love!

I am an absolute sucker for customer service and this place goes above and beyond!  I've followed them on social media for a very long time but had never actually gone in... until this last Friday when they advertised a Buy 3 Get 3 promotion on all their sausages.  When I got to the store, they explained that this was valid basically on anything with a casing.  

When I walked in, I was absolutely like a kid in a candy store.  I didn't catch anybody's names, but there were two people working.  The first lady approached us when we walked in and asked if we needed any help.  I told her I was just browsing for now but would probably need help once I finally took everything in.  She took a minute to tell us about all the amazing deals in the store and then left us to look around.

The second very helpful employee stayed behind the counter but made his presence known in case we needed anything.  We did ask them a lot of questions.  I was focused mostly on the various turkey sausages.  Once I got to the turkey sausage ring, the lady came up and asked if I'd ever tried it.  I said no.  She said "oh, you have to!  I'll cut some up so you can try it".  And she actually took it to the back and cut it up so everyone in the store could try it.  Very smart because ALL of us bought a ring.

I couldn't be happier with the service I received or the quality of the meat I got.  And I honestly can't wait to come back!

I can't say enough good things about Charmed floral. I ordered two arrangements and had to call back a few times for various reasons ( all my own doing). Mandi was so professional and personable during each conversation we had and the arrangements are absolutely beautiful. 
I will definitely be using Charmed whenever I need beautiful flowers for a fair price.

Best local butcher ever!

I can't believe that tonight was my first visit to the new location since they moved last year just down the block.

The new building is AWESOME with loads of parking and sooooo much space!

It's all the same fabulous D'Arcy's meats and local goods we've come to love from 2nd generation butcher, Kyle Isaac!

There are so many things I loved about the new space including the wall to wall chalkboard behind the counter with a hand drawn map of Alberta highlighting where all the local meat cuts are from - SO COOL!

A huge bonus about this location is the customer washroom, which as a mom with 2 small children is a HUGE bonus.

D'arcy's always specials to encourage you to try some new to you things or stock up on favourites!  Today we eyed up the fresh hamburgers with 1/2 ground beef and 1/2 ground pork - I cannot wait to cook these up for supper tomorrow night!

Another really cool think about D'Arcy's is that they will butcher/prepare wild game you've caught to your liking.  I have several friends that SWEAR by the talents here and will never take their hunting wins elsewhere.

Also, Kyle and the gang at D'Arcy's will can customize orders - want extra spicy sausages or gluten free hamburgers?  They can do it!

2 years ago the hubs and I had custom made sausages with locally sourced meat for a cookoff contest at the Taste of Edmonton and all 3 judges picked our dawgs!  I can't help but be a little biased towards this great local business!  

Sure the prices are a little higher than a grocery store but the quality and service is second to none!

Congrats on the new location and I can't wait to come back all summer for more grilling goodies and tips!  And don't forget to check in on Yelp for a surprise!

P.S.  D'Arcy's serves up lunch from 11-2pm on weekdays - You'd be hard pressed to find a better quality lunch on the go for the favourite carnivore in your life!
Do you like meat? Good. Do you love meat? Great. Do you want to come to the Disneyland of meat? Come to D'Arcy's. Great selection. Super friendly service and the meat variety is outstanding.

I been there looking for chineese fondue meat, their prices are outrageous high, and the quality of the meat was not there.  After telling them, they argued with me and were really rude.  I will never go back there ever again.

I just had the most delightful time dealing with these lovely Ladies, Megan in particular. I had an occasion to order a bouquet for my Grandaughter who Is Ariel in the little Mermaid This shop is extraordinary in their customer service they went above and beyond to make the delivery on a Sat. night. I have forwarded their info to my Family who lives in  St. Albert so they may have the wonderful experience that I had,  Thank you Ladies very much again it is greatly appreciated. Beverly Aisenstat.

We hired Charmed Floral Design for our wedding and it was a GREAT decision. 

Everyone couldn't stop commenting on how unique and beautiful the centerpieces were. At the end of the night almost all were taken home by guests.

My wife absolutely loved her bouquet and is currently doing everything she can to extend its life in a vase. 

Mandi is unbelievable to work with through out the entire process and the final product really showed her creativity and skill.

if you have any event coming up and you want unique, eye catching arrangements this is your spot.
The arrangement was so much nicer than I anticipated.   Every aspect of this order exceeded my expectations.  Thank you.

A staple for the locals and it easy to understand why!!! Quality meat, quality service and fair prices: there is a reason this place can find itself lined up thru the door on weekends. 
Order your fresh turkeys for the holidays or fresh chickens weekly.... I know I will!!

We pre ordered a corned beef brisket for St Pattys day. It was really good. Not over salted, well balanced flavors, and very fresh, good quality cut of meat. Customer service was also excellent from start to finish. They carry a lot of specialty meats here, I highly recommend if you are looking for something a extra special that you might not be able to find at the average grocery store. They are pricey but without a doubt, you get what you pay for.
Definitely recommend going with the florists design to get a beautiful bouquet of flowers!

It has taken me many months to write my review and I feel guilty as hell. People are quick to tell you about a bad experience but not the extraordinary ones. I think I just needed to finish grieving. I was referred here by a former co-worker and I always kept it in my "back pocket" until 6 months later a friend passed away and I needed an arrangement that reflected the uniqueness of Dusty. Nothing @ the major chains spoke to me and then I remembered Mandi. I sent her a FB message explaining what I needed and that my budget was fluid as it needed to have wow factor. I asked her for a "fabulous non-funerally funeral arrangement".  We shared a few messages and a phone call. I described him as a guy who loved hunting but also Lady GaGa in short. She kept me up to date on lil accessories she was finding for the arrangement during the week. I think this started on a Tuesday and I needed it for the Saturday. I was at the Rain Maker Rodeo on the Friday night when she sent me the photos of the final arrangement. I opened the attachment and started ugly crying right there!  Up until that point I hadn't cried nor have I cried since, except while I type this I'm starting to cry. The arrangement was beyond fabulous it was magnificent!  It exceeded my expectations is every way. I am astonished that one phone call and some messages resulted her in nailing Dusty perfectly in the arrangement I lovingly call Lady GaGa meets Duck Dynasty. She had feathers, sparkles, camo, antlers, tree branches and the coolest vase/vessel that looked like a tree stump. It was gorgeous. Spectacular really. I picked the arrangement up Saturday morning and the photos did not really show the true size of this glorious beast!  It barely fit in my Ford Escape. I tried the cargo area 1st, nope too tall. Front passenger seat floor, nope too wide. I crammed it in the back seat on the floor and it was still touching my roof. This creation was just big in so many ways! It was over the top and I LOVED it. Mandi wasn't there when I picked it up so I never got to meet the genius behind the arrangement which probably was a good thing or I'm sure I would have been ugly crying worse than the night before. The drive was little stressful I was afraid that any turns would make it tip over, I drove like an old woman all the way to venue. This baby was a show stopper let me tell you. People were flocking to me as I walked through the door. Every person would notice one of the many Dusty inspired details and squeal with glee. I heard so many clicks of cell phone cameras it was like a celebrity on a red carpet. This masterpiece demanded attention and it got it, damn it. I think if Dustin could have spoken to me he would have been pleased and that is all that matters. Mandi is such a wonderful artist. I told her she would be my florist for life now. I haven't had an occasion for flowers since but maybe I will order flowers just because, so I can enjoy her creations. I wish I could attach the photos to this review but if you search the posts on May 25th 2018 you will see her breathtaking design. Please forgive any spelling or grammatical errors as I am typing this out on my phone b/c if I didn't do it this VERY moment it would take another 8 months. Oh nevermind I went to publish and it asked me to add a photo. Behold!

Have been seeing a stylist at this salon long before the current owners took over about three years ago.  Since acquiring the business they have let the physical space go downhill.  The chairs in the reception are so worn your not sure whether you should sit on them.  The floors in this area are not swept.  You can see a layer of dust on the shelves of hair products they are trying to sell.  As well there is a collection of dust, etc on the work counter of every stylist.  With the overall appearance, how clean is anything else?  Another disappointment is the lack of acknowledgement of the owners when you walk in if you are not their customer.  They would rather be talking on their phones.  Very disappointed in how this place is being run.  Would not recommend this salon - they need to take some pride in their ownership.

Came to this salon a week ago without hearing anything about it - it was simply open the evening I decided to have my hair cut, and it was a short drive from where i live, which was a bonus. Usually, and I mean almost always, letting only these factors dictate my decision end up badly. But surprise, surprise! - it turned out to be one of the most delightful experiences based on an on-a-whim decision! Zeina was skillful, that lovely lady knows her thing! I thought I wasn't  even very clear about what cut I wanted, but she knew right away what i was trying to have achieved. She was accommodating, cheerful, and confident with what she was doing. That made me feel assured she knew exactly how to get there. When I asked for a cascading side bangs, she didn't just pull my bangs in front of my face and chop the hair to a cascade and get done with it ( an annoying thing a lot of lazy, less skilled hairdressers do), she skillfully spent time to pull my bangs up, gradually trimming it, and did her thing the way skilled, professional hairdressers do where when they're done and they drop your bangs in place it just falls perfectly in place. 

Suffice it to say that I walked out of Signore happy and content, the way one does when one has gotten her money's worth.  I guess i just found a gem in my neighbourhood! Here's hoping it's a start of a wonderful, long-term relationship!

Usually, and I mean almost always, letting only these factors dictate my decision end up badly. But surprise, surprise! - it turned out to be one of the most delightful experiences based on an on-a-whim decision! Zeina was skillful - that lovely lady knows her thing! I thought I wasn't  even very clear about what cut I wanted, but she knew right away what i was trying to have achieved. She was accommodating, cheerful, and confident with what she was doing. That made me feel assured she knew exactly how to get there. When I asked for a cascading side bangs, she didn't just pull my bangs in front of my face and chop the hair to a cascade and get done with it ( an annoying thing a lot of lazy, less skilled hairdressers do!), she skillfully pulled my bangs up, spend time gradually trimming it, and did her thing the way skilled, professional hairdressers do where when they're done and they drop your bangs in place - voila! - it just falls perfectly in place. 

Suffice it to say that I walked out of Signore happy and content, the way one does when one has gotten her money's worth.  I guess i just found a gem in my neighbourhood! Here's hoping it's a start of a wonderful, long-term hairlationship!

Now known as Signore Hair Co.  I was very disappointed with the hair colour.  I specifically said I wanted the end result to be per the sample shown, not the colour as per the sample to be applied regardless of end result.  The stylist said, "You people come in and ask for... blah blah".  First of all, I don't appreciate being referred to as, "you people" in the collective with her other customers.  Secondly, I made it abundantly clear that she should use a colour probably one other than the sample, such that the end result is as per the sample.  I did not want to argue so I took whatever she did and left, knowing I would have to fix it at home myself with a solid colour, saying goodbye to the so-called highlights I paid for.  What's worse, I had a lot of grey after I washed my hair that night, so it was a terrible job of covering grey even if she had got the colour right.  I can do better at home.

Fantastic cut and colour from here. The stylist had to adapt my colour choice due to the shade I had in my hair and they managed to do exactly what I wanted! Bit expensive but totally worth it to get exactly what you want with your hairstyle.

Signore is my standing hair dressers now. After discovering them a couple years back, I was happy with the cut. Since, ownership has changed, there's been some reno's and it's even better! 
All the stylists are friendly and will talk as much as you want to (if you're not feeling it, they won't talk your ear off!)
Great prices, plenty of products and hot shaves available. Give them a try!

First the high point: the beet and roots salad is lovely, if a little pricey.

Then the low points: the overpriced hamburger is entirely forgettable, featuring at its heart a hard, totally overcooked patty (if I'm not mistaken, kitchens in Alberta can cook patties to order -- not to the disgustingly overcooked standard demanded by public health officials -- provided the meat used for same is ground on premises the same day; the owners should look into that), the creme brûlée is pricey and forgettable, and the iPad menu is not entirely intuitive (I ended up with a more expensive version of that salad than I had intended to do because it wasn't obvious to me that there was a full-size version, the one I was served, and a side order size, the one I had intended to order).

It isn't all bad, though.  My waitress was equal parts charming and gracious, the dining room is pleasant enough, and the toilets are kept tidy.  I'm going to give this place another shot for dinner one of these days and I'll update this review to let you know how it went.

Amazing, inspired, friendly, local. These are the words that come to mind when I try to describe my experience at 12 Acres. 

We went for brunch on a Sunday. I had the sausage and hash, my girlfriend had eggs Benedict. We both agreed, we'd be back.

What initially sparked my interest was the concept. All the food on the menu grown by one farmer on 12 Acres of land. Local, organic, and well... Real. We met the owners, they're real. We met the farmer, he's real. We met the chef, he too is real. They cure their own meats, they make their own sausage, they bake their own baking and it's all very, very good. The Knackwurst in my brunch dish was amazing. The whole dish was amazing!
If you care what goes into your food, eat here. If you don't care, and you just want amazing food, eat here. This place is beautiful and I want it to stay. Once you come, you'll want that too.

I've been overwhelmingly disappointed in my last two visits here.

Over cooked pasta that was stuck together in my bowl in a lump - staff shrugged it off and was like, oh yeah it is.  How about offering to replace it?  Server had to be flagged down to refill our waters - and when you're waiting an hour, you've got lots of time for water. 

Waiting an hours for our mains when we had 5pm reservations!  Not an apology and then our food was subpar.  The manager came out and apologized profusely to the table next to us but they got their food before us and came in after us!  Maybe he meant to come to us? 

Can't say that we'll be coming back. 

Also something happened and the restaurant has split from the farm - so no longer farm to fork.

Also while we were dining, my phone rang and it was 12 acres!  They wanted to know if we would be coming in for our reservation - um yeah, we're sitting here at the table still waiting for food.

As always the service is great, the food is awesome, and atmosphere is worth spending time in. 

We have been coming here for years, and I've never had a bad meal, or a bad experience.

I first visited Sweet Boutique about a year ago at their former location and was not impressed, to be honest.  There was only me and one other customer in the store, but no staff to be seen.  I tried to navigate the store on my own and figure out what everything was, but I just couldn't.  So I left.

But I've been following them on Social Media and I'm so glad that I decided to check them out again.  The products are unique and fantastic.  And the staff know so much about all of it.  It's actually really impressive.

I love the variety of product.  You can buy funky socks, clothing, lotions (including some great fragrance free options!), and chocolate covered licorice.  

Great local business with passionate staff.  Check it out.

Service was non existent. We were told 5to 10 minutes and waited 45 before being told another 5 to 10 minutes and we could see empty seats. We were told she could not seat anyone. So she did not seat us we left.

There's something to be said about a product with no preservatives and no artificial stuff in it.  Davinci's Gelato is a first class product and you can tell by the freshness and pure heavenly flavour.   This tiny shop is located in a medium industrial area and has limited hours (I believe 12-6).  They do have food trucks around town so I assume they have varying hours with those.   Regardless, the gelato is one of the best I've tried and the service is exceptional.   We came based on a coupon we found in a local paper and will definitely be lifelong customers.   Price was very reasonable at $4 for one giant scoop.  I had two scoops, just for the record!  Amazing!

For the same as I spent yesterday at Soda Jerks I had a FAR better meal and dining experience here. The Brotwerst on a bun is great. View from the patio is also nice. Service is okay though a little slow.

Like the rhyme says... I will scream for ice cream...especially Davinci's homemade Peanutella...YUM!!
I had the pleasure of meeting the owners of Davinci's at the ZOOlander event in August. 
We were so impressed with their selection we invited them to be a part of Yelp's Ultimate Picnic Party over the labour day weekend. 
They came with so many flavors that I had to keep sampling and I'm not complaining!
The chocolate flavor had been handmade that morning and I probably would have eaten the entire tub if I could have. 
Tip: ask the staff which flavors pair well together. Like coconut and raspberry. It'll be a real treat for your tastebuds!
We went there for girls night Friday but there was no dancing and few people.  Service was very slow, has to ask 3 servers to finally get my drink refilled.

Went for dinner and had the burger and my husband had the steak and sausage. Portions were great, and the food was extremely fresh.  Meal was incredible.  Service was lacking greatly especially considering there were at least 7 staff just waiting to serve tables standing around.  Being that it is new and it was our servers first time working in an environment like that we will be back and predict that service will improve.  Reservations were easy to book online and we got our meal in a reasonable amount of time.

This place is solid.  The service is normally pretty average at best however they make up for it with decent prices, a good draught selection (especially some good euro brews) and good food. 

I recommend the bread pudding for sure.  

Good spot to watch soccer games mid week also.

We were excited to try this restaurant as we love the idea of Farm to Table. Fast forward to today -- we walk in, no reservation.  We are greeted by 3 teenage girls that were clearly not trained in the art of welcoming a customer.

Anyways, we are led to our table. The decor albeit a little forced is nice. Within a few minutes our waiter, younger guy very nice, plops down a couple ipads and asks us if we would like a drink. I look over my shoulder to see a gentleman in his 70's struggling with the electronic menu. Just an idea -- explain the concept of the iPad menu to your customers. We were fine with it but felt bad for the old guy that was clearly confused.

Waiter returns and we order some wine. Ten minutes later two glasses of Shiraz are delivered.  No testing or seeing the bottle -- hopefully didn't come out of a box.

We are ready to order -- start with some bread, I pick the strip loin and my wife has the pulled beef pappardelle. Within another 5-10 minutes the bread is delivered.  Well, bread is a little vague, what they bring out is a slice of multigrain toast with sea salt sprinkled on top. Not rolls or a little loaf -- no, a piece of toast. We have a giggle about the toast and wait for our mains.

Shortly after finishing our light breakfast our mains are delivered. Upon first inspection both dishes look good. My striploin is accompanied with roasted beets, small onions, a sausage and mashed potatoes. The Pappardelle didn't have the best presentation but it is supposed to be rustic dish.

First bites -- my striploin is cooked great, medium rare as ordered. One problem -- everything on my plate is room temperature. The center of the steak is cool to the touch. Aside from the temperature everything tasted good but very overseasoned.

My wife tried her first bite of Pappardelle and before she could utter a word she reached for her glass of water. I have never tasted a dish in a restaurant  that was so overseasoned. I could tell it probably could have been a great dish if it wasn't for the salt. She managed two more bites before giving up.

When we were finished the waiter asked if everything was ok? (as he clearly noticed my wife's plate was barely touched and I gave up on my salt beef about 1/3 the way in.) We told him the food was so salty it was inedible. We were clear we didn't want new dishes nor did we wish to talk to the manager - the waiter was a nice guy and for us we had a laugh and lesson learned, we would not return. 

The waiter brings us the bill, and before we could pay the manager shows up at our table. She gives us a speech about constructive feedback and customer satisfaction -- she was off to revise our bill to reflect the issues we had. Cool we thought. She comes back within a minute to deliver us our new bill. My wife looks at the bill and says to me, "She took off $2.10 from our $90 bill." We were now in tears of laughter -- surreal. After giving us that spiel she removes a toonie. We thought it must be a mistake -- any time I have complained about a dish at a minimum they remove the cost of that dish. We get the waiter to check, no it was right she gave us 10% off my wife's meal. 

WOW.

Do yourself a favour, don't eat here.  We will never return.
Got the bison burger it was burnt but the fries were awesome and the drink was better than most. I'll be going back there to give it a second chance just because of the sides and cocktail skills

Visited DaVinci at their St. Albert location in Riel Business Park the other day for a Fort Mac fundraiser.

As always, we were super happy with the quality of gelato and sorbetto - sooooo good!

The staff are friendly, the flavours are always changing, and locally made! 

What more could you ask for?  Nothing!

See you again soon, DaVinci Gelato and can't wait for Farmer's Market Season :-)

The WORSE experience I've ever encountered, this woman needs to learn etiquette on how to run a business properly. If your planning on hiring this woman for your wedding DON'T DO IT. I tried hiring her for an entire month. It took her 10 days to send the contract and 2 weeks to reply back to my submittal (because she randomly went on vacation). A month later, after the fact she finally responded and informed me that she booked her truck for the airshow. She apparently booked it while she was on vacation and while I was patiently waiting for a reply from her to tell me how she excepted payment for the deposit. 

INSANITY!!!!!
THIS WOMAN SHOULD NOT BE RUNNING A BUSINESS. 

I have to say this is one of THE MOST RUDE things someone has done to me.

25$ for the Following

1 cooked burger that turned cold while waiting for it
1 extremely dry over cooked chicken burger
1 chocolate shake missing whip because they ran out. Also shake arrived after we were done eating
The understanding of the English language was very poor

Never coming back ever

Never go here again the service was off and we actually saw the cooks in the kitchen plating food with their hands and rubbing their beards. Was so sick after seeing this what ever happened to health standards with beards. Stupid trendy thing with beards these days. They don't belong in the kitchen!

As a beginner, I was very nervous to attend. But I reached out to Larissa and she was so welcoming over my email, and when I got there, I was welcomed with a hug and so much happiness! Tara was my instructor and she was extremely helpful. She didn't push me beyond my ability and was welcoming as well. She went around the class and made sure each person was doing well and they were comfortable. I will definitely recommend this studio to many others and I'll absolutely be attending many more classes!

We had a delicious lunch on the patio at 12 Acres! The meals were beautifully displayed and very tasty and we loved the fact that our meat came from just down the road. 
Great use of technology as well in the reservation system and iPad menus!

First time here for breakfast and I was pleasantly surprised. We are heading to the Eskimos game on their bus. 

Eggs Benedict were cooked very well, and the banana bread french toast was great too. Food took a little longer to come out than we expected.

We will be back for brunch here again for sure.

My absolute fav dessert!!! 
Beautiful little shop, quite and peaceful 

All gelato made in house!!

I came across the Davinci Gelato Truck at a charity event at the Valley Zoo. I sampled a couple of their 'signature' flavours such as; straciatella and peanutella (both amazing). And then I had my go to fave, lemon. Oh My Word! Tart, sweet, bright, clean. Everything a perfect lemon gelato that is straight out of Rome should be... If you ever see this Truck out and about, stop and get a scoop or two! You will not be disappointed. 

Oh, and a special shout out to Yvonne and her son Felix who own the truck. Devouring amazing food is just that much sweeter when it comes from wonderful people who you can tell really pour their heart into what they do - the love in this gelato really comes through.

Just celebrated my birthday by having brunch with my family at 12 Acres. It was absolutely awesome. I've had other meals here and always wanted to have brunch here....not sure why I hadn't. Since it is my birthday, I ordered the Espresso Martini to start the celebration. For my brunch, I was delighted to find Chicken 'n Waffles on the menu.....and they did NOT disappoint -definitely the best I've had!! My husband orders Flank Steak and Eggs and was very  pleased. My daughter ordered the Cinnamon Swirl French Toast and absolutely loved them. The service was excellent and it was great sitting outside overlooking the Sturgeon River. We definitely will be going back!

We purchased some local meat at the St. Albert farmer's market from 12 Acres Farm. It sparked me to bring the family to the 12 Acres Restaurant this evening. My husband and son were most impressed with the iPad menus being such techies/geeks. The chairs were super comfy almost like giving you a big hug. We enjoyed a lovely bottle of red wine along with the appetizer of charcuterie, followed by burgers and dark chocolate cake. My son said the bread he ordered as side order was the best he's ever eaten. Our complements to the in-house baker and chef. We were pleased to see this restaurant busy this evening with families and couples. It's wonderful to see that you are wheelchair friendly. I was entertained by one of the guests that was savouring her Creme Brulee dessert (it seemed like an orgasmic experience). Thou shall not covet thy neighbours dessert?! ... Guess I will need to return and have what she had. It's fantastic to have a local menu of food from pasture to plate. We will certainly recommend this place to our foodie friends and family! We look forward to visiting again soon.

This was mine and my husbands first visit to the Celtic Knot, and we enjoyed ourselves as we'll as the meal. I had the Reuben sandwich and he had the steak sandwich. It was fresh, delicious and made onsite. (at least according to the manager who stopped by to chat with us) Everything arrived quickly and we never had to wait very long for drink orders. We'll definitely be back!

Usually a pretty good crowd, the waitresses are on the ball, and most are a familiar face. 
As far as pub food goes, I have always been pleased with what I've ordered. My personal favorite being the lamb sliders, excellent!
The fish and chips, and burgers are also good!

I have heard so much good about 12 Acres and was really looking forward to the evening. We were 4 dining and really did enjoy the staff and how we were serviced. 
The snacks (appetizers) were bland. Only 1 of 3 dishes delivered. Duck wings were not appetizing. The butter chicken and fries were delicious. The Garden salad was boring. 
The mains were very disappointing. Pork loin and strip loin were chewy and dry. The burger was dry.

The brunch menu looks yummi so I might return despite this experience. I hope for more as this place aims high but did not deliver last night.

Oysters and tenderloin from @12_acres

Oysters and tenderloin were nothing special. I personally like buttery/briny tasting oysters like kushi from von's and a little bit more seasoning on the steak. The sausage that came with the steak was delicious and super flavorful paired with the smear of mustard. But I see what they went for here at 12 acres with a very natural and clean tasting menu. I thought the meal was ndm until dessert. Dessert really impressed with a perfect creme brulé and lemon tart. I'm lactose intolerant and the stomach ache drive home was worth all of that creme.

Atmosphere was nice and friendly, great service and the iPad menu was new and cool as their menu always changes depending on local food suppliers. The owner was nice enough to provide shots for us too. Overall a good place to try, but if i go back I'll try the burger. It looked pretty dope. 

Sal says: Just try it

Slowest service EVER. We went the day before my wedding for supper and also to celebrate my sisters birthday. We sat down at 7 and didn't even get food until quarter after 9. When we finally asked what was taking so long they realized the waitress had closed the order and they thought we had left. I didn't really get to eat because; who really want's to eat fried chicken at like 9? They did give us a $25 gift card and my sister got desert; but I just wanted to have a nice family meal after all the hard work of setting up my wedding and to celebrate my wedding the next day and my sisters birthday. It just wasn't worth it;
They have a little cafe here now. Awesome paninis! Had the meatlovers panini and loved it. Very reasonably priced.

Today was my first time visiting a Fatburger.  For the most part, I was impressed.  It was a good burger, and I really liked the gravy with my fries.  I thought that it was a little expensive for what you get, but I will definitely go back.
So delicious. Server was super helpful and kind. Food was fresh and prepared perfect. Beer is good, too! Will be back!

Wow!  All I gotta say is, Wow!

I have never been to a Yoga studio like this one since moving to Canada.

First off, this studio is literally in the same strip mall as my daughter's dance studio - Um, yeah... Why did I not go here last year rather than sitting on a couch for 2 hours every week?

So let's get the cons out of the way - It's located on the 2nd floor and there isn't a washroom in the Yoga studio but there is one in the hallway you can access with a key.  It's a nice washroom and there is nothing wrong with it but I would just rather prefer a washroom inside the Yoga studio itself.

Okay, on with the AWESOMEness!

When you walk in the door, it's like you are walking into an beautiful and bright Indian inspired oasis with gorgeous fabrics and silks draped from the ceiling, brightly coloured walls, comfy couches and chairs and a beaded curtain leading to chagne rooms.

I don't think I've ever walked in without being warmly greeted by at least one person if not two or three.

There is a Sun room (hot and warm) and a Moon room (room temperature),  They offer classes ranging from hot ( flow, yin, etc.) to relaxation to Hiit (yoga and interval) and many more that I haven't even tried yet.  Their website breaks down each style of class offered: http://www.lahariyoga.ca/classes-description/

So far, I've gone to three of the Blissology series by instructor Michellene Kandert and have fallen madly in love with her style.

First off, she's hillarious and sometimes makes us dance - yep, dance (especially on Friday night Happy Hour).  She is real, supportive, and empowering - pretty much all you could ever ask for from a yoga instructor or human being!

After yoga classes, you can sit and enjoy fruit/herb infused water, tea, coffee and snacks at their kitchen bar or lounge in their comfy couches in the "Om Kitchen & Lounge."

If you go to a Happy Hour Friday class, there is literally a mini potluck afterwards and wine.  Yep, that's right.  Yoga followed by wine and treats!  Does life get better than this?  Me thinks not!

Lahari also offers Men's only classes on their schedule (way cool) and kiddo classes as well.

Definitely check out their website and live schedule to see what is coming up and give them a try!  Your first class is always free - You have nothing to lose and everything to gain!

Prices are comparable with all other Yoga studios in town with drop in at $10 or a punch pass of 10 classes currently for $90.  They also offer monthly, three months, and yearly memberships which are the way to go if you practice 2 or more times per week!

I really can't say enough great things about this place and look forward to continuing to explore this studio and the instructors here!  

http://www.lahariyoga.ca/

Was at the Holes Greenhouse and I yelped the closet ice cream shop and this one came up.
Area is very clean limited parking. I loved the colour purple used for their business.
