The ice cream is very fresh. I had the vegan coconut on a cone for 4 dollars. Double scoop 7 dollars. A great selection of gelatos sorbet and vegan choices. 

Definitely a gem in the middle of some industrial area. 

I hope there's one that comes in the south east of edmonton. We need some ice cream
Shops. :)

Second worst service I have ever had, right behind a waitress telling me my order was ready, but she really needed a smoke so she would be right back. I took my family here for a lunch on our way home. So, after unbuckling 2 very young children, we make our way in and try to place an order. The attending cashier looked at us, for quite a few seconds without saying a word, almost dumbfounded. Then, after taking a partial order, and not answering a question my wife had, stopped talking and just left to talk to another employee. This carried on for over a minute with us standing there. So, he just leaves, and we are left at the cash with nobody. Then,  somebody comes over and tries to take an order, again we repeat our daughters order, then she stares at us, and leaves. Rather irritated at this point, but still willing to try, we "AHEM" and she shows back up. My wife asks for my daughters kids meal, which she tries to charge us twice for, then, after we tell her to correct it, she offers us a soda fountain cup, after 3 times telling her that we wanted milk with her meal. She then proceeds to tell us she has to charge us extra for milk, even though it says right on the menu that milk can come with a kids meal. At this point, my arms are tired from holding a car seat, so I tell my wife that I am done trying to deal with these people, I would rather spend more money and at least have servers who are even a little bit dedicated to there job, and not what is going on in there social lives. I have eaten at other locations and love them, food is excellent. Love the burgers. However, this particular location, is awful. Would not go there if my life depended on it. It would be faster to keep driving into Edmonton to another Fatburger, and try ordering there.

I actually have enjoyed the food here on multiple occasions but have yet to have enjoyable experience due to the horrible wait staff. I always wrote it off as my meal was hot and good and counted it as a balance. Today on the other hand, after sitting for almost 10minutes without even a hello, I figured a review was due. Every man that walked into have beer during the jays game, the blonde behind the bar basically jumped at the hop. My husband and I did not even get a smile, or a I will get someone for you. Even other patrons noticed we still had not been greated or attended to and tried to get service for us. What a joke! Get better staff if you want to continue to stay in business.

I've tried dinner at 12 ACRES and can advise that it was a better experience than lunch.  The good: the steak was very good, if about 15-20% more expensive than it should be.

The bad: my beet and parsnip salad came without any parsnip, and I was never warned about that at any time.  (The kitchen should have advised my server, and if he had been so advised, then I should have been cautioned before the salad was prepared and presented for my consumption.)  As it happens, I'm not a huge parsnip fan, so it wasn't a real loss, but it would have been nice to be asked if I'd like to have something to substitute for the missing parsnip.  That contrast would have been nice.  I had to work through a lot of beet.

Also, my mashed potato could have been better, but to be fair to these guys, mashed spud preferences tend to vary a great deal from person to person, so what I prefer may not be what others enjoy.  I do tend to find mashed potatoes from restaurant kitchens underwhelming, so it might be just me.

I do like that the head chef seems to be trying to give young guys and gals a chance to cut their teeth in fine(r) dining -- at least that seems to be my impression, for everyone other than him appears to be less than 30 years of age -- but they have to try and polish up their conduct in the dining room a little bit.  They're all friendly to a fault, and that's a very good thing, but they can be a bit loud from time to time (chatting casually with each other, that is).  While 12 ACRES doesn't seem to want to be a stuffy fine dining restaurant, the surroundings are classy casual and the high-ish prices mean that the staff need to behave appropriately.  It isn't a big deal and I know that they can easily figure out the balance.

Wow, this stuff is FRESH!  You can taste the real ingredients (and love) that go into these treats!  I tried the Coconut, Stracciatella, Strawberry and Lemon flavours at the Yelp Picnic Party (don't judge... it was between 2 of us!) and they were all delicious.  The coconut was more like a nice refreshing coconut milk rather than ultra rich and creamy or an overpowering artificial taste.  The stracciatella was milky and smooth with flecks of delicious chocolate.  You could see the seeds in the strawberry gelato, a nice mild and again not overpowering authentic strawberry flavour.  And the lemon was tart and sweet but not TOO tart (although as a lemon fan, I would have liked a bit more tart!).

They were all solid flavours and I would definitely be happy to go for seconds (fifths?) next time I run into them at a farmers' market.  I do wish that some of the flavours were a bit more inventive (hello, Cravings Gelato?), but Davinci Gelato Originale is classic gelato at its best.

I love a good hamburger. I didn't get one here. For 12 dollars u get 1/4 lb small overcooked cold burger along with some mediocre fries and a pop.I have been to Fatburgers all over and suggest the owner goes to las Vegas so they can learn what a true Fatburgers should be. Don't waste your time here,go to jacks or soda jerks for better burgers and the same $$$.

We had a Wake organized in this Pub, we were given a fair sized private room just off the main bar area, the service was very good, the appetizers were good, pricing was reasonable.
The main decor is good.
All in all a good watering venue!

We arrived for our 8pm reservation Sat Jan 23 and were promptly seated.  Simple yet pleasant decor.  Good start.  I was looking forward to my first time here.  We were presented with the Ipod menu which I loved.
Our first waitress disappeared then never came back and about five minutes later another waitress said she would be serving us. We had the 1/4 chicken and the 12acres burger with the sturgeon chowder and a beet salad.  Nice presentation on slate tiles.
The chicken had a nicely salted crisp skin with tasty meat. The beets were tasty and nicely roasted on top of scalloped type potatoes.
The 12acres burger was mediocre considering that the menu decribes it as the best burger you will have.  The meat was tasty.  A bit overcooked and on the dry side.  Thick beef patty. The bun was quite dry.  Minimal condiments which is good if the patty had been less dry.  The fish chowder was very tasty, however it was lukewarm.  It should have been warmer.  The beet salad was meh.
Now onto deserts.  My wife had the gluten free chocolate and it was good.  Very chocolaty.  I travel alot and have bread pudding almost everywhere I go.  The apple bread pudding was a major disappointment.  It was dry.  I did not taste any apple in it.  There were pieces of bread that had not soaked up any liquid.  Bread pudding should not taste like wet bread.  I could only consume part of it. I informed the waitress of the quality of the pudding and she said she would tell the pastry chef.  I would have expected it to be taken off the bill.  The americano was a typical restaurant beverage.  Espresso extracted from old over roasted coffee beans. I roast my own coffee so I know what good coffee should taste like.  Most restaurants fail miserably in the coffee front.  A really good restaurant needs to deliver quality from the appetizers through to the final beverage. 
12 Acres restaurant is an average 3.5 star restaurant.

The building was such a nice old Victorian style. Inside was comfortable, nice spring day so no temperature issues like in the previous posts.

Husband had garden salad, I have the beet and parsnip. Both were good. I had lots of beets and parsnips unlike a previous post I read. For entrees we had short rib (husband) and the gnocchi for myself. 

The short ribs were so tender and delicious. Came with fiddle heads (husband wouldn't eat but I grew up on them from the east coast but they were just steamed missing the salt.....they are a marsh fern after all.  The buttermilk potatoes were delicious. The gnocchi was so amazing. Pillowy soft. The pesto was fantastic but had some in my teeth. Came with roasted zucchini, carrot and bell pepper....a bit too many peppers for my liking but it was very good. 

We shared the Earl grey tea Panna cotta. It was delicious.  Homemade granola and a Saskatoon compote. Was not too sweet and the perfect ending for a great meal. Draft beer on Tuesday is 4.50 a 20oz pint. 

Service was great. I was a bit weary trying it out as after all I read was hit and miss. We bought a Groupon for 55 worth for 29 so took the plunge. After the Groupon including a 15.00 tip to our waitress we paid 47.00 so about 100.00 for 2 people. Would definitely go again. The menu changes so I'd love to try something else. Great for a date night. We went at 745 pm with a reservation. It wasn't busy. But who knows what a Friday or Saturday at peak times would be. Would love to see a place in edmonton open up in the future.

Wish I took some pictures before we started eating...

At first glance the Celtic Knot is a great addition to the St Albert pub/bar scene. But on further inspection they have a lot to do before it makes it into my regular rotation. 

For a place that just opened in the last few months the tables were clearly bought at some sort of auction of used bar furniture. The booths looked inviting but ended up being uncomfortable. The tables were too small to fill the distance between both benches so you ended up having to sit on the edge of your seat or sit comfortably but have a ton of room between you and the table.

The decor is modern and at the same time retro with large black and white prints of old European streets and buildings. The huge bar in the middle does dominate the landscape but it's a good centre piece and gathering spot.

The service was quite unimpressive. We were often looking for our server and at one point another server came to ask if everything was okay since he even realized we had been left alone. One of our group is a new mother so she wasn't drinking and asked for water. She was given a straw too short for her glass and the server apologized for it. But the two pepsi's that were delivered to the table later on had full length straws. It makes you wonder if they marginalize water drinkers.

Finally we shared a few appies from their late night menu: Pulled pork sliders and crab cakes. The crab cakes were soft and surprisingly filled with more crab then expected. The pulled pork sliders were a disappointment but I'm not sure I've ever really enjoyed pulled pork from a restaurant so I may be unfairly critical. 

I hope that this place does get everything in order sooner rather then later because I think it can fill a St Albert niche that's been missing so far.

Went on Valentine's Day, unaware of the set menu. Food wasn't bad but wasn't amazing either. Small portions for the price. Drinks are outrageously priced! Atmosphere is nice and was quiet. Staff was friendly. Food wait wasn't long, but for it not being super busy when we were there drinks took awhile to come.

Gelato my favorite dessert and treat! Went today to buy a pint of hazelnut to enjoy at home. La Dolce Vita, it doesn't get any better than this, so creamy and delicious. I can't wait to try the other flavours and the sandwiches that they serve.  This by far is one of my favourite places to treat myself to something beyond fantastic!

I go to this location at least 2 times a month, so I am aware of the size of the burger pattie in a fatburger.  Went there to eat the other day but used a groupon for 2 fatburgers and skinny fries.  I also ordered a mini fat burger kids meal.  When the food arrived, my fat burger pattie was half the size it usually is.  It wouldn't even cover half the bun.  The other fat burger was the same.  I called the manager over and showed him and he said that there was nothing wrong with the size of the pattie, and insisted that's the size of the patties in all fat burgers.  I wish I would have took a picture and posted it on this site.  The guy next to me ordered a fatburger with poutine, you could see the pattie was much bigger.  If this location has a problem with groupon's then maybe stop accepting them.  I would gladly take my business elsewhere and in fact I will never return to this fatburger again.  You need to take care of your customers when they choose your restaurant  or they will go somewhere else.  St. Albert has many burger restaurants to choose from.

Pretty much the only place in the greater Edmonton area that is REALLY doing farm to table, not just a few things that hit the menu when the restaurant feels like it. Huge ambitions but if done properly, this will be amazing.

The food was great, large portions at decent prices, a nice change from all the small plates that seem to be taking over the culinary world. Their cocktails are priced well and delicious to boot. I had the Berkshire Pork which was some of the most deliciously marbled pork that I've eaten in years. The menu will change with the available ingredients, so remember to be flexible with your menu expectations.

I'm sad that it's not closer to my end of town!

12 Acres is the latest restaurant in town (well, St. Albert technically) to jump on the farm to table concept bandwagon. If you've never been, don't bother looking for a sign, there's none. But don't fret, they're easy to find - just look for the red house. Previously known as the River House, the restaurant has been reincarnated as 12 Acres to match their new sustainable food philosophy. St. Albert is seriously lacking in solid restaurants so this is a welcome addition to the 'hood. If you want to food-educate yourself, do yourself a favour and watch the documentary: Chef's Table.

We went on a Friday to check out their lunch options. The red house itself is gorgeous and houses a spa upstairs (External Affairs Clinical Spa). It was gorgeous outside so we decided to sit out on the patio and enjoy the beautiful weather. The patio faces north so there is no access to sun but that didn't matter.

The server we had was very enthusiastic and gushed about all the cool things that are happening at 12 Acres. One interesting tidbit that surprised both of us was that their baker is celiac and thus, can't even taste/eat the bread he's making. Craziness, especially considering how good the bread tasted. Must have some good taste testers.

- Daily baked focaccia, pickled red onion, greens, roasted porchetta and aioli. The focaccia was fresh, light with a nice bite to it. The porchetta was tasty but there was a huge chunk of fat on it. I know that gives it all the flavour but my friend took her fat out and was left with only a small chunk of meat in her portion. It was lacking a bit of refinement. The fries/potato chunks were good but you only get five! That's right F-I-V-E.

- Ground ribeye burger (with seasonal toppings) ($16.00) - baked today bun, scratch mayo, heirloom tomatoes, 12 Acres ground chuck burger, scratch mustard, cheddar and garden greens. My friend really enjoyed her burger. And the kid sized Heinz ketchup. Heck, she brought the extra one home because it was so cute. Oh girls. Again, the bun was really fresh and the burger was actually moist and flavourful. The kicker in the sandwich was the scratch mustard (dijon grainy mustard style). Probably a love or a hate for some but I really liked it. You could feel the horseradish awakening your sinuses.

Overall, we were both happy with our meals. Definitely need to try out their dinner menu to see a greater variety of dishes as the lunch menu is pretty limited to sandwiches (and one pasta dish).

We had dinner at 12 Acres in their lounge side. This restaurant is brand new and has a lot to offer with fresh local sustainable foods. The vegetables and meats are sourced from a local farm. The ambience of the restaurant is tasteful in the Victorian style building with view of the Sturgeon River. They have a few tables available on the veranda. This week is a soft opening for the restaurant. Being new, they will have some bugs to work out. This weekend they are opening the restaurant side. Their menu is entirely on iPads which we were handed. The menu is updated to the moment with fresh creations allowing them to update very quickly. For example, if they run out of a specific dish it can be deleted and a new one can be added. I have a severe food allergy. I appreciated them accommodating my allergy. The generous serving of beet salad was fresh and delicious. Our main course, were steaks. Unfortunately, both of our steaks were tough (strip loin, sirloin). The beef is grass-fed and with grass-fed beef, it needs to be cooked at a lower temperature or perhaps with a sous vide and then grilled. Hopefully the chef will clue into this and be able to create nice tender meat for the customers. Also, the timing of the food was off. We had not finished our appetizers when our main courses arrived. It was awkward. The food was tasty. There is a good list of wines available. I'd like to try 12 Acres for lunch to see what the menu is like. I might suggest giving them a few weeks to get into a better flow.  I wish them all the best for the grand opening of the restaurant section, June 13, 2015.
Ugh. Food doesn't look anything like the menu. What a total disappointment tonight was. 2 owns came out terrible and need to be sent back

I haven't had gelato this fresh since I was in Rome! Oh man! I tried three flavours at Yelp's Ultimate Picnic Party (because why not?!), and loved all three. Mango and Coconut were the first to go, and then I rounded it off with Lemon, which was my FAVORITE! Oh man, the tart lemon bite was just right. So good! If I wasn't so uncomfortably full, I would have tried more. I'll have to stalk them and try another day!

Was there for supper last night, Mar 25, 2016. We had two plates of the roasted chicken and Rice, excellent, one order of the Fish and Chips, very good, and one 12 Acre Burger, also very good. Only thing with the Burger is they should ask how clients want them done., Came out medium the first time with quite a lot of pink. Sent it back for a short time and it came back med well as requested. Their potato wedge fries are absolutely superb, we ordered extras of those.

Had two different wines by the glass, 9 ounces. They paired very well with the meals and were both good quality wines. Very reasonable prices, $12 and $15 per glass for the quality of wine served. The craft beer selection is quite wide and the couple we tried were very good.

Service was attentive but you could tell our server was fairly new. Nice, attentive but a little disorganised. Had no impact on the experience. We sat in the main dinning room and once it filled up we did find it very loud in their just from the table conversations. My mother and M-I-L are both close to 90 and they found the noise quite a problem even though neither has hearing problems. My wife and I are 40 years younger and we really noticed the high noise level too.

All in however we all said we would happily go back again. Prices are a little higher than most area restaurants but given the quality of the food and the excellent dinning experience I found the prices quite reasonable. $150 for 4 with drinks is not a lot of money to spend in a restaurant any more, though we admittedly didn't have any appetisers or desserts.

Absolutely amazing! I was with a group of 3, and the entire meal we could not stop raving about how good our food was (between bites).

I was a little worried as I tend to be a picky eater, and usually like my comfort burger and fries type meal. I had a pork Tbone. AMAZING! I didn't want my plate to end! The meat portion was definitely generous, and so flavourful. Loved the risotto, and the asparagus with it was done to perfection.

The prices were a little higher than my usual price range (~$25 and up), but I feel it's worth it for the quality of food you are getting (locally sourced and preparation). I couldn't afford to go there all the time, but I would go back for a more special occasion anytime. 

The menus were on iPads (but very easy to use for the less technically inclined older folk), which I thought went against the theme behind the restaurant about getting back to our roots, but with an ever changing menu, it works better than paper. There was nothing on the menu for kids, but there was a couple young ones in there. It also seemed a little classy, but the guests were not dressed for classy, so I'm not sure what the dress code is supposed to be.

Highly Highly recommend.

Oh ya. The service was good too. Nothing exceptional, but friendly and got the job done timely and professionally. The owner (?) did come out to talk to us and ask how things were going which I thought was nice.

Great food and great service. Everyone was wonderful with our little girls and it was easy to order for them from the regular menu. 

They have a nice cocktail list and a good selection of wines although the menu made it hard for me to select a wine so i just stuck with a cocktail ok this hot day. 
We had the charcuterie board, steak tartare, steak and sausage, buttermilk chicken and spaghetti for the kids. If I could, I would have had the sous vide pork t bone. I love pork and the ones coming out of the kitchen looked amazing. 

Portions are enormous and I can't believe I did it, but I had my steak packed up to take home. How embarrassing. 

Try the restaurant, you won't regret it.

Our table of six had a wonderful experience!  The service was attentive and the server was very knowledgeable about the products on the menu and the prices were reasonable. Started with the parsnip fritters, the bread and the Charcuterie. The Saskatoon berry rhubarb chutney and the pickles were a great accompaniment to the cheese and meats on the board. For our mains we had the Lamb burger, gnocchi, meat balls and spaghetti, pork belly, 12 acre burger and the strip loin. Everyone enjoyed their meals and we all cleared out plates. The lamb burger was moist and very tasty. 
We enjoyed our night at 12 Acres and would go back.

Amazing product and amazing staff! Whether it be something for yourself or for someone else you'll be able to find a unique item. The quality is great and a lot of it is all locally made or within Alberta. Support a small local store and you won't be disappointed

*I'm trying to remember the prices as best I can, but I don't have my receipt on me to confirm 

We tried so hard to like it here but our entire experience was a disaster from the moment we arrived. We'd called prior to coming and was told to be there at 8:30. We arrived a few minutes early, but no one had any idea what happened to our table. There was no alternative table for us and we stood awkwardly by the door as 3 people tried to figure out what to do with us. We said we'd wait a bit, and was offered drinks for "our trouble." We thought that was complimentary, but were later charged for it.

We were eventually seated and ordered our food. The tartare duo ($18?) - the salmon was nothing special and I wish there was more of the red meat option instead) and the fried chicken (this was delicious and the fries were thick wedges that were crispy and yummy. For a $17 appetizer I wish there was more chicken) appetizers. We also ordered the daily bread ($3), which was a rye option. We were disappointed when the picture on the menu showed  little loaves, the table across from us received that, but we received little slices. I wish there was more consistency. As an entrée, we shared the carne platter ($34 I think) which was a half plate of arugula doused in vinegar that made it difficult to eat, a sliced steak (that was good, but a bit burnt on the edges) and the saltiest sausage ever (we didn't eat it) plus ordered a side of mashed potatoes ($4) that tasted like they were uninspired instant potatoes. For dessert, we ordered the flapper pie ($11) which was nice and light, and the salted caramel blondie ($9?). The blondie was hard and tasted stale. It was also served with a fruity ice cream/sorbet that really didn't suit the flavours of the dish. We also had a blueberry tea ($9) and a boozy latte ($11). Those were fine. 

The server was friendly but really didn't do much in terms of our feedback. When he asked how dinner was, we gave honest feedback and his response was basically, "oh that sucks." 

For the amount we paid, we were hoping for a better experience.
The menu says 20 Oz pints but my 1664 blanc were served in 16 oz glasses. At 9.50 per pint that seems excessive. Might explain why we were one of 2 tables on a sunny Sunday.
Awesome food, creative menu. So excited to have such a great, local, non-chain restaurant close to home.

Horrible. I ordered two kids meals and was told they did not have chicken strips. Got cold burgers and fries instead, there were no toys in the treasure box and a filthy drink station. The worst part of all was the overly loud and obnoxious music playing, full of swear words and offensive racial slurs. I couldn't believe my ears. Clearly the kids working the kitchen chose to blast their own music. So much for family friendly. I will never ever return here and neither will anyone in my family.
Enjoyed a lovely Sunday brunch on Easter Sunday . Service was warm and friendly and the food was plated beautifully and was super fresh. Only one small complaint / the eggs Benedict was a bit salty .

This place has delicious food! I had the buttermilk chicken and it was fantastic! The restaurant looked a bit like a pub when I got there and it wasn't clearly marked the restaurant. I spent a moment trying to figure out if it was the right place. If not for the poor signage, I would have given it 5 stars. 

And the best news... they have a food truck!

Good food! All dishes were very flavourful! I had the gnocchi and it was very tasty. I went with a big group and everybody was happy with their main dish! As appetizer We had the charcuterie plate to share and ordered all the cuts they had.  Some things were really good, like the duck or the chorizo. The lardo and the guanciale were not my favourite cuts. The wine was good and the desserts were great as well! The cheesecake was my favourite. The service was ok. Unimpressive for me. They were friendly, but the waitress was a little lost. The prices were not inexpensive; but not awful pricey... in general, this place was good... It's definitely not the best place I have ever been but it's not bad either...

I am a big fan of the Acro yoga class at Lahari Yoga. It is a little late at night (9:15-10:30) but it is worth staying up for! The instructor (Cole) is extremely friendly and extremely knowledgable. Safety is his #1 concern in the class so I never feel unsafe when practicing some of the Acro postures. I have gone to this class alone and also with a partner - it is a great class b/c you often get paired up with someone close to your size so it truly doesn't matter if you bring a partner alot (in fact the majority of the class comes into the class without a partner) The yoga studio itself is also beautiful with 2 different yoga rooms, a nice living room type area with a tea bar and tons of yoga related things for sale (clothes, mats, ect)

Went there tonight as we have eaten at their food truck and it was a good burger. We pulled up at 7pm on a Saturday night and the parking lot was empty. We almost drove away as this was a tell tale sign of what we were going to experience. We were seated right away and waited 20 minutes before the waitress even addressed us. The water girl came by twice to fill our water (should have left the tip solely with her). Ordered our apps and drinks. Drinks took another 10 mins and they were wrong when they arrived. Eventually got our drinks. The entrees we ordered the $35 steak and the $45 pork chop. The steak was a 5oz at best not 8oz and the pork chop was mainly fat on a bone. At last we ordered an old fashion as a last drink. It came and as I took a sip I noticed there was a house fly stuck to the side of the glass. How cliché is that lol! "Waiter there's a fly in my soup". Unfortunately it was true and very gross. We returned the drinks and asked for the bill of course. The manger Nathan came out and seemed skeptical of the fly and I provided feedback of the entire experience. He offered a gift card which I initially declined as I have no intentions of returning and really just wanted to give him feedback. He talked us into it and gave us our gift card. I will be mailing his $25 gift card back to Nathan as that just shows a lack of good will his failing restaurant is willing to do. No way would i return to spend a few hundred dollars with his $25 gc. River house grill will be missed. This place will be gone in 3-6 months I'd bet.

Well I had high hopes for this restaurant when I heard about it.  I always loved the idea of farm fresh protein and veggies.   Once the food actually arrived after an hour wait it was good.  This rating is for the service and lack of logistics that a well run restaurant needs to be world class. 

It was a struggle just to get us a table in a empty room.  I get you have reservations but so did we.    Then when we called an audible and asked for a table outside it was like throwing a wrench in the spinning wheel.  There was no script for that.  help!  

The iPad menus were cool, but that lost its luster once you realized there was only minimal entree choices and the same small amount of appetizers options as well. 

I know it has only been open for 2 weeks and every restaurant needs to iron out kinks, but in today's age of an ultra competitive restaurant landscape there isn't much room for error.  

I wish them all the success and hope they don't be come a statistic.

I love the knot! I used to go to O'malies but then the 18 year olds came in there and turned it into a place where every guy is looking to fight and every girl is fall down drunk. I like Crown and tower but the guys on the VLT's throw me off and the food isnt great. Celtic knot has got it right. They have a good crowd, good beer selection and also Great food! I love spending my weekends here! Great up and coming spot. I also know they have worked out a lot of kinks since my first visit right after the opening and the staff is getting it right!
Excellent lunch. Great steak sandwich etc service is always good. Would highly recommend stopping in for lunch and a pint. Great place meet friends for drinks, great atmosphere.

As far as Fatburger restaurants go, this location is a little unusual (unless the other ones have been converted as well).  The St. Albert Fatburger is a combination store which serve burgers as well as Buffalo Express wings and Marble Slab ice cream.  

First impression is great, it is new, it is clean and the menu is 3X the size of a normal Fatburgers.  The TVs on the walls were all tuned to sports of some sort, definitely enough to keep most people entertained during the wait.

I was greeted by the cashier immediately, service was prompt.  I had a tough time deciding between wings or burger but eventually settled on the large cheese burger with fries and drink.  Burgers come in 5 sizes now: small, medium, large, XL and XXL.  I ordered the large (thinking middle of the row should be safe); then I reviewed for food value chart, small = 400-600 cal, medium = 590-790 cal, large = 850-1050 cal, XL = 1350-1550 cal, and XXL = 1850-2050 cal.  Plus fries and icetea, OH MY, that was a lot of calories I consumed at lunch; lol.  

I took a picture of the wings and burger menus, have a look at the choices yourself.

The food came quickly.  The burger was a little on the crispy side.  Very well done, charred on one side (new location = inexperience chefs?).  Oh well, can't expect a perfect burger every time.  With a ton of lettuce and tomatoes on top, it was an okay burger.  The fries was great, fresh, hot and not over-salted like some other locations.  The meal was satisfying, although I do question whether it is worth $14 plus tax plus tips (a $18 fast food meal).  

Besides my stomach for eating too many fries, one thing did bother me a little, if you pay with a credit card, the "No Tip" option does not exist on the machine.  My personal dilemma has always been, if I tip at Fatburger, why don't I tip at McDonalds or Starbucks?  The staffs at these stores don't really do anything different.  May be I wouldn't be bothered if the staffs were friendly and cheerful, they really didnt look like they want to be there working today.

Fatburger is a good place to grab a burger; but, there is nothing special about their burgers.  Taste wise, Fatburger's burgers still trail behind Jack Burger Shack's burgers and Five Guys' burgers; price wise Fatburger is pricier.  Would I return, yeah, still need to try those wings but probably won't return for the burgers!
Will update once the wings have been had.

Looks like not much has changed since George H's review back in 2012.  The furniture still looks old and run down.

Service was decent though.  There was only two other tables occupied on a Sunday evening at 6:30 and there was one server and one bartender on.  The drinks stayed full and the food tasted good.  I only had a plate of poutine, but I was impressed.  The fries were really thick and had some kind of batter on them.  Great for holding onto the gravy and cheese.

I might come back for the poutine, but not there's nothing about the atmosphere that would pull me back in.

Solid restaurant. This place has a great building, awesome food, and great service. They make all their own ingredients and even have a farm where they grow their protein. Because of this, their dishes change on a regular basis and they actually bring you their menu on an iPad.

Last night hubby's took me to 12 acres because we love trying new places and it was also my birthday.  Although, 12 acres has been opened since May 2015.  I've only heard of it couple weeks ago on CBC's article on new restaurants in Edmonton.  To my surprise, 12 acres use to be the River house in St.Albert.  I was kinda of sad to see that river house is gone because I enjoyed their brunch a lot.  But after trying 12 Acres, I think it's a good change :) 

We had reservations but had to wait a bit cuz our table was still occupied.  Normally this would be a huge pet peeve of mine.  Making reservations and still have to wait but the manager/owner came up to us apologized and explained the situation.  Which we appreciated.  
Our table was a nice size and the most comfortable chairs ever!   Their menu was on a iPad which was nice because it's easy navigation (especially for the wine list) you just search for either the country or a certain type of wine and it would pop up with a list.  We were told by the manager that almost everything there is fresh and made by themselves.  Such as they pickled their own vegetable, cure their own meat, make their own bread and PASTA!  

We started off with mussels in white wine.  Wow, the mussels were huge! Every single one was big and juicy! I enjoyed the mussels a lot.  It comes with two slice of brown bread to dip into the white wine sauce! Delicious.  We also ordered a side of their homemade Rye bread.   

For our entree I had their 12 oz ribeye steak that came with mash potatoes and carrots.  There was some mustard on the plate.  I'm not a big fan of the mustard with my steak so I avoided it. The ribeye was very good but too big for me! As I was getting pretty full from the mussels and bread.  My husband had the beef cheek. Which was also huge and very good - the texture reminded me of beef brisket.  It was also served on a bed of their home made pasta.  The pasta is amazing.  I have no idea what kind of pasta or what sauce was on it.  But it was good.  I would love to try their pasta next time.  Like their gnocchi or spaghetti and meatballs.

For dessert we tried the New York cheese cake with a latte and Americano.  The cheese cake had apple sauce on it,  not a big fan of apple sauce.  The cheesecake was ok.  Nothing memorable about it.  Latte and Americano was good. 

Overall I will come back again.  Enjoyed the food and the chairs!

Bad beyond words.

We stopped in their on Wednesday for our first and last time.  We were barely seated when the server asked what we`d like to drink. What -- no time to look over their extensive beer list.  Not the it took very long since the list is mostly AB InBev standards.  We ordered our beer -- mine arrived 10 minutes before my husband`s (same beer).  I presume they were changing a cask but some communication would have been good.

Then the food.  Ah yes -- the food.  We ordered the `famous`steak sandwiches -- mine medium rare, his rare.  Mine arrived rare and cold.  His almost raw.  I told the server about it and here is what she had to say:  I don`t know what to tell - you.  It`s usually really good.   And then she walked away.

She came back later to ask if we wanted our bill.  I asked whether we were really expected to pay for that (the food) and she sent the manager over.  He was quite apologetic and took the food off the bill.  But that should have been a no-brainer.

The gong-show of food and service aside, we found the place to be loud and lacking any kind of personality.  

We find that decent food and service is getting harder and harder to find in St. Albert.  Too bad, really.

First of all, I love the farm to table concept. Supporting local is important to me, and 12 Acres doesn't disappoint. We visited for a late supper and sat at the bar. The bartender, Dakota, was great! He truly made our experience that much better. We had a view of a portion of the kitchen where we could see the staff preparing fresh sausage! It was so neat to see the care and attention that went into the process- not to mention to great atmosphere of those who work there- they are a team and it shows. The menu offered changes daily as each meal is as fresh as can be- and believe me, you can taste the freshness. The meals are prepared with some serious love and pack some serious flavour, even the cocktails are perfectly crafted. I had the chops with a  blackberry lavender soda and my spouse enjoyed the steak and sausage with a tap beer- both amazing! The owner of the farm who supplies 12 Acres dropped by while we dined, and we got to chatting- you can immediately recognize the passion he has for his farm and what he's a part of. 

The atmosphere is warm, and inviting- not to mention exciting. Don't be discouraged if something isn't on the menu- for example charcuterie. We learned all of their meats are cure in house some of which take over 5 months- it really shows they pride themselves on fresh and sustainable.

We enjoyed our supper experience so much that we returned for brunch today. The brunch menu had many options and the service was great again. The only thing i noticed was that they didn't have a traditional eggs and bacon meal- which I think is a missed opportunity. Would also be great to see a waffle option- although it may just not have been on the menu today. 

I will absolutely be returning- great addition to St. Albert.

First the wine I ordered they were out of. Then I ordered the Leprechaun Pie which took way too long to come. And then I sat for 10 minutes waiting for cutlery and my friend had to get up and get some for me. On top of that, it tasted terrible. Like there was a layer of salt on it. Finally when our waitress came back around and I told her, to she took it away. She came back a moment later and asked if I wanted something else. I ordered the Pumpkin Pie in a Jar. That dessert was okay. Not the greatest but at least edible. 
I guess The Celtic Knot is not the right place for dessert. :(

A fave icecream place for me in St. Albert right now, especially with it being summer. Actually may be one of the best icecream places in north Edmonton. Why?!!! Because they have plentiful options of sorbet for dairy free people like me. Yummy and unique flavours for both sorbet and gelato icecream. AND the scoops are of a grand size. I ordered 3 scoops my first time because of my excitement and I was blown away. I went a 2nd time and got 2 scoops and it was perfect  amount for me even though I wanted to get all the new flavours of sorbet they had. Sooo it just means I am going to continue to return to try more. 

1st visit- I devoured peach passionfruit, black currant and strawberry lemonade sorbettos in a cup

2nd visit- I devoured watermelon and grape sorbettos in a cup

Great customer service and reasonably priced. Location is in a industrial area but you can see the patio furniture outside the icecream shop and their sign. Plenty of parking along the road and some in the parking lot.

Didn't have a good of an experience as the first time I was there. Service was mediocre at best. We were never asked if we wanted another beer even though the glass was sitting there empty. It also seemed like the waitress was going to a lot of the other tables more frequently than ours. Who knows it may just be in our heads. 

Finally the food. The first time I went I had the pork chop and my partner had the gnocchi. The pork chop was gigantic and delicious. The gnocchi was very cold. They just didn't have the timing right, since the pork chop was so big I'm sure they Ill times the gnocchi. 

This time I had steak and it was the opposite. Supposedly it was a 10oz steak but seemed very small. It was probably the most unevenly cooked steak I had ever eaten. Medium rare in one spot, medium in another and well done in another. I should have sent it back because of this. Also the steak was charred a little too much on the outside. I don't know if it was cooked on a dirty grill but all I could taste was bbq char when I bit into it. Nothing ruins a steak more than when you taste char over the meat itself. On the plus side my partner had the Mac and cheese and it was creamy and delicious. As easy as Mac and cheese is, a lot of restaurants screw it up and dry it out. 


Unfortunately I don't think we will go back. It does seem close to being good though. A few tweaks of service and food and it could be there.
Service wasn't good, food was mediocre and menu was very limited. Not worth the (expensive) cost at all in my opinion. We won't go back.

So surprised that I am lucky enough to be the first to review this location!! So many good reviews are written on my Facebook and heard through friends that I was equally surprised I hadn't been in yet. 
I have been into this store more times than I can count for Christmas presents and there are always new items to look at! The selection is quite large for the size of the store and prices so that one could easily get an outfit for under $100!! 
The accessories are were my heart does an extra beat. They have everything from socks to skin lines to jewelry to browse. Be sure to stop on and give this store a look...I don't think you would be disappointed.
Great food and the concept is awesome. We had great service and the food was amazing! Could be a better atmosphere, but it is still enjoyable.

Hey, Bada Bing, Bada Boom.  Just like in the old country, a smooth and creamy dessert carefully hand crafted with love by an Italian angel. Talk to anyone behind the counter and if you can't feel the pride they have in their work, I'll send you an apology.
That's how much faith I got in dem. You hearing me? So go there, tell them you're a friend of mine and they'll take good care a yous. All a yous. Capiche?
OK, cliché aside, the Gelato flavours are their own. They are unique and made in small batches. Try the Peanutella, peanut butter... Wait for it... AND NUTELLA! Hyuk! The Stracciatella was actually like a cloud laced with dark chocolate shavings. Mango was sublime. Lemon was sweet and perfectly tart. Chocolate was robust and the mint was clearly intended for refreshing a delicate palate with subtleties in their flavours that elevate Gelato to a new level.
Almost expecting to receive this on a small plate with a sprig of mint and a fanciful drizzle of coulis, a simple syrup and wine reduction, or compote à la Iron Chef. The flavours are there.  Go, enjoy. Take your time. This is slow food. 
Boom. Now your mind is imploding.
Generally draws in an older crowd. Food is usually pretty great and the atmosphere is nice, especially when it's not too busy.

This is my absolute favourite yoga studio, ever! I started coming here a few years ago shortly after Larissa opened the space. The staff are welcoming and friendly, and always make me feel at home. The instructors are amazing but my favourites have been Michellene, Dani, Larissa, and Harry. Recently they added additional infrared panels to the ceiling in the hot room, making it feel even more like a spa treatment and a therapy session, rather than just yoga. I always leave the class feeling renewed, healthier, energized and/or relaxed. At the end of the class they come around with icy cold facecloths that are scented with lemongrass and place it across your forehead. The caliber of the instructors is outstanding and their customer service and human connection is next to none. Love this studio and I can't imagine life without it. Thank you to Larissa for creating this community, I have seen it grow fruitfully in the past 3 years to the point I now need to pre book many of my classes in order to get room for my mat. We all share this amazing energy and sense of community together.

We were extremely disappointed with this restaurant.   We went as a group of 9 and ordered the soups both the seafood soup and the tomato soup.  The seafood soup had to be returned was over salted and replaced with tomato soup.  The cooks must have a really heavy hand at salt which overtakes the flavoring of both soups.  Even the tomato  soup was over salted but we were able to consume them.

The entrees were a disappointment as well.  Can't say I've ever experienced any restaurant that would salt their sides of veggies so much.  Overpriced for the quality received as far as I'm concerned and will not be returning.
Ouch....I give this place 3-6 months unless they manage to get their act together. Wont be back.

My wife and I went here for a special night out to celebrate our fortieth wedding anniversary. We were very impressed with the comfortable surroundings, the service from friendly staff and great food!  I had the ten oz ribeye steak and my wife had the lamb sirloin and both were superb, cooked to perfection and top quality!  For dessert, the salted caramel blonde and the glutton free chocolate torte were to die for!  We will definitely be going back and taking our friends with us!  I rate this restaurant five stars!

My bf and I went here as we had a Groupon to use..cozy and casual feel and the staff were very friendly and ready to serve. We ordered the dry ribs to start which were so flavorful and robust it was crazy! Just note that these dry ribs are not your traditional crispy shriveled ribs you get at the local bar. I then had the 12 acres burger and my bf had the mac n cheese. Both dishes were a fair size and very rich and satisfying.  We topped it all off with a gluten free chocolate dessert which was dense and chocolatey. We were stuffed! We will definitely be back to this restaurant and recommend it to those looking for a nice chill and classy atmosphere and a big appetite.

There really are no words to express what a magical experience I continue to have at Sweet Boutique!  You make every customer feel warm, beautiful and important.  Giving us beautiful clothes by local artisans is the experience all women need.  A very special thank you to all your staff for making it a pleasure to shop and treat myself in a beautiful and supported environment! 

Warmly,

Debbie Jackman

Um... Yeah.  If you haven't tried Da Vinci Gelato, you are missing out!

You've seen their truck all around town (think Farmer's Markets like the St. Albert Farmer's Market) and they are now being featured in restaurants like Vivo in Edmonton.

The fabulous owner of Da Vinci Gelato custom creates and makes the batches from scratch locally in St. Albert!  Check out their website for more info: http://www.davinci-gelato.com/

Most recently, I had their gelato at a PIcnic in Edmonton and the whole fam jam was blown away with the quality.

Usually, my son who has a dairy allergy misses out on desserts or only has maybe one option - but not with Da Vinci Gelato!  They had not 1, not 2, but 3 dairy free flavours that were delicious and creamy if you can believe it!  

You can really taste the fresh ingredients like strawberries, mint leaves, or tart lemon in their gelatos!

I really cannot say enough good things about this company!

See you soon at St. Albert Mall or the Farmer's Market!

We stopped in not knowing the restaurant or menu. We had an amazing dinner and excellent service. This is a place that prides them self on no hormones or antibiotic raised meat and locally grown veggies.

Wow! What a delicious evening! We had the clams and muscles to start which had such a delicious sauce! We then had the duck carbonara which was so tasty and the perfect portion.  The roast chicken was our other option and the flavoring was wonderful and the chicken was soooo moist! It's also great that the Food is locally sourced and very fairly priced! We will be back!

Get in my mouth! Seriously... I am such a fan of Davinci, it's not even funny. They came out to Yelp's Ultimate Picnic Party and I couldn't imagine a better way treat myself! It was nothing but smiles from the two serving us. I tried the Peanutella (peanut butter and Nutella) and my husband had the chocolate. Ohhhhh yum. We even came back for seconds!! I tried out the Mango, and the husband had Vanilla. Smooth, creamy, fresh, and big flavors. I will for sure make the trek to St. Albert for this, or whever Davinci may go. I am hooked!

Dinner for 6.  Great service.  Great food.  Reasonable prices and great atmosphere.  Everyone's food was fresh and hot.  Drink refills we're timely.  We ordered an array of food and all were Happy with fish and chips, bangers, beef dip, Reuben sandwich.  Highly recommend.  We were there 6:30ish.

We went in to check out St Albert's newest restaurant! 
We ordered a drink and the "Caesar salad" to share... It was Very different. Not your usual Caesar.. Not sure about that one. 
So ... Naturally we were a little apprehensive about your main courses.. 
Well I must say we both were very impressed! The food was beyond delicious! 
I had the fried chicken .. The most perfectly cooked of any I'd Ever ordered anywhere before. The mix of flavours were awesome. 
My bf had the sous-vide t-bone pork .. So good! Tender beyond tender & the carrot risotto & asparagus was again perfectly cooked. 
All in all we were so impressed & our waiter Dave was so personable & helpful!! 
We will definitely be spreading the word!

I shouldn't have expected an improvement with the same owners and chef.  

My wife and I are huge supporters of local business in St. Albert, and despite previous bad experiences at the Riverhouse (since taken over from Willie) we thought we owed them a fair chance.  We made a confirmed reservation for 7:00 the day before.  They called the next afternoon and informed us that they had overbooked and had to bump us to 7:30.  When we arrived, our table wasn't ready and they said it should only be a few minutes.  Well the few minutes became 10 of sitting in the front entrance, where 3 girls including one who appeared to be one of the kitchen staff just stood there.  After 10 minutes they said that our table was still full and we could sit at the little side table while we waited.  It was another 30 before we had our table, for a total of 70 minutes from when we actually set the reservation.

The servers were genuinely apologetic, and did comp a drink while we waited.  It should be noted that the owner was wandering around looking busy and never acknowledged us.  Once we finally had our table I realized that I had a fantastic view of the wide open washroom.  During the course of our evening, I was even able to play a little game based on whether the seat was up or down when the guest was all finished!!

Please note, servers were very pleasant and as informative as they possibly could be.  And I'm bordering on over judginess, but I only need to be told once that things are made in house.  We get it.  

Please lose the iPads too.  Pictures are only good if there are actually pictures, and ordering involves the server bumbling with it at the table and asking 3 times what you wanted while it gets entered.  

The entrees are well priced, but that is cancelled out by the overpriced appetizers, such as the $16 beets.  Drinks, also expensive.  My appetizer was the steak tartare, which was half pickles.  It was accompanied with some sort of potato wedges, and Saskatoon preserve.  I'm not sure what everyone else thinks, but I'm not a big believer in putting jam on my pickles, or my potato wedges.  My wife and I both had the steak and sausage since the chicken and lamb were both unavailable.  ???  The sausage was pure salt to the point where my wife couldn't eat hers, and the miniscule tenderloin had no seasoning.  Potatoes were all good though.  On another note, BUY SOME PLATES!!!!!  The wooden cutting boards are just silly and you can't keep them hot in the kitchen, so they suck all the heat out of your food within 5 minutes.

Final tally, 2 people, 1 bottle of wine, 2 apps, 2 entrees, 2 desserts, 2 glasses of port, + tip = $210.
Best Fatburger location I've been too. Great service (the guy checked on us several times and offered to get me some water, even though I didn't ask).

We came here on a double date and enjoyed our visit despite a few hiccups.  The waitress didn't seem to know toon much about what they did and did not have for beer choices but we aren't too picky so that didn't bother us much. My husband and I ordered the nachos with beef to share since they were on special. They were great! The only thing is that when the bill came, we most definitely didn't get the "special" price which was a bit annoying. All in all it was a good time but we won't be rushing back.

St. Albert's 12 Acres Restaurant had their media preview and soft opening last week and a grand opening on the beautiful Friday. I have a soft spot for St. Albert (can you tell?) seeing that I work there and all. I had planned to give them a week to work out opening kinks but my friend Sharon seemed just as excited as I was for a farm-to-table restaurant so close to her home. Throwing our cautions to the wind, we made reservations that evening to check out the new space.

Farm-to-fork or farm-to-table is not a new concept to Edmonton and area, and with a number of restaurants now supporting local produce and local farms, to have another one open, 12 Acres Restaurant is keeping up with the trend. It's a trend that I support, a healthier and better alternative to know where your food came from and better yet, supporting a sustainable food system. The "red house" had long been The River House, and after a change of ownership three years ago to bring us The River House Grill, owners Nathan and Courtney Henry had a change in their food philosophy. 

Re-emerging as 12 Acres Restaurant and pairing up with City Life Farms (or 12 Acres Farm), the two have merged identities and becoming one of both a farm and a restaurant. Their goal? To become fully sustainable within the next two years, exclusively sourcing their meats and produce from only the farm. Currently, only meats are available as their greenhouses are still in the works. Greens are currently from Peas on Earth, a certified organic and local farm. Their flour is from Anita's Organic Mill in Chilliwack, BC, and Nathan boasted that their outstanding celiac baker could make any gluten-free nay-sayer a run for their money. As if in-house baking isn't enough, an assortment of charcuterie and sausages are also a focus for 12 Acres Restaurant. 

The space is grand, accommodating a hundred guests between both their lounge and dining area. The patio extends around the building, with a fantastic view of the Sturgeon River. The kitchen space and bar is open now to the diners, emphasizing on the contemporary comfort feel. 

Menus are on iPads. Yeah, that's right. Categories of "Appetizers", "Entrées", "Cocktails", etc, complete with pictures was quite unique! Apparently the cost of printing menus, especially changing seasonal menus, gets pretty expensive! Both diners and staff seem to love the iPads, a user-friendly option for all.

With over a dozen cocktails to choose from, it took me and Sharon a while to settle in. Sharon's Black Lavender Soda (vodka, lemon juice, blackberry honey, blackberries, and lavender bitters) was a winner in both our books, and my Blueberry Mint (vodka, mint, blueberries, lime juice, and simple syrup) was a refreshing start to dinner.

To start, we had the Tartare & Chips. Described as "some of the most tender and tasty animal bits", I had an inkling that it incorporated some offals and off-cuts! Rib-eye bits ended up being the cut of choice, a comfort to those who are squeamish to thyroids and the like. The texture was outstanding and the flavours on point. The raw onions were a bit overpowering for both our tastes but forgivable when eaten with large wedges of fried Kennebecs. We finished the entire dish!

My Sous-Vide 12 ACRES Pork T-Bone ($26) was surprisingly well made for such a large portion. I'm deathly afraid of overcooked pork. Served with a carrot risotto (holy delicious!), a Saskatoon berry jam, saved asparagus and pancetta crisps, my dish was one that I could reorder every single time. Really well executed and a great balance in flavours and textures.

Sharon ordered the Chicken a la Buttermilk ($25), fried chicken pieces with a spiced kale, rhubarb compote. Crisp, tender, and well-seasoned, the chicken was delicious! Definitely a favourite amongst diners and will be a staple on the menu. All menu items were under $26, making 12 Acres Restaurant quite affordable!

If 12 Acres Restaurant was a date, then I had purposefully left "my jacket at the house" to guarantee a second date. We left without dessert. Talking to our server, David, who was equally passionate about the restaurant's concept and food, and to Nathan and Courtney left both of us forgetful of the desserts. I will definitely be returning for my second date! Service had some hiccups, (a lost reservation, a confused server due to new tabletop numbers and layout, a mis-delivery of orders) but that was expected for opening night. Everything was very well handled, not only at our table but our neighbouring tables as well. A less than ideal steak was offered to go back to the kitchen, with a replacement steak out to the table within minutes. With some fine tuning, I have no doubt that service can reach top notch. Staff were very friendly, very enthusiastic, and having a ton of fun with diners - a great atmosphere for everybody. Definitely a must-visit when you're in St. Albert and worth the drive for Edmontonians. Bonus, they're even open for lunch and brunch!
Found a lovely shop that carries my favourite go to black leggings called sweet legs. Sooo comfortable and wear forever!!

Creamy, delicious goodness made from scratch? Check!  Yummy flavours- I've tried both the straciatella and coconut, and honestly I couldn't put the spoon down.  Davinci even offers several lactose free options, so no one is excluded.

The people working at Davinci are very friendly and passionate about gelato.  The prices are well worth the quality product- $4 for 1 scoop, and $7 for 2 scoops.  

Be sure to track down Davinci's truck at various farmer's market locations.  Their gelato can also be found at Leva.  They even do catering.  I will be back soon!

It's so great to see the quality of the River House recrafted into something so much more organic to the community of St. Albert opening its doors!

Paired with City Life Farms (owned by Jen & ...) and the fabulous Chef Nate and Courtney (formerly of River House), 12 Acres is really exciting!

The concept of #FarmToFork gets me really excited!  With the majority of the produce and animals for meat being raised just down the road, It can't get any more local than this!

From house cured meats to baked in house breads, they've got made from scratch down to the very animals that lay the eggs!

The long term goals include being completely self-sustainable for produce and meats.  To be able to birth the actual animals on the 12 acres of farm land that will produce future generations of the best free range and well cared for animals.

Imagine a restaurant that can order the animals as needed - the end result is less waste and fresher food.  

It's kinda like taking the trouble out of gardening & hunting combined with a master chef's keen eye to create the most delicious and sustainable food on your plate! 

12 Acres has ditched the grown up and fancy night out feel and swapped it for modern and accessible!  12 Acres feels like the kind of place I'd come with a group of girlfriends for drinks and bites or a date night out with my hubby that I can feel good about.

Lots of seating options from tables, benches, and bars to welcoming booths and a veranda with a stunning view of the Sturgeon River.

And let's not forget about the fabulous menus on iPads that let you get a visual of every item they offer!  What better way to know if it looks just as good as it sounds?  All that is left to do is try it!  Our server told us that they are only the 2nd restaurant in Alberta to offer a menu like this!

The Grand Opening was fabulous! My hubby loved the fried risotto with goat cheese and I will definitely be back for a wine and charcuterie night!  Can't wait to try mains :-) 

Cheers 12 Acres & Welcome!

Came here for a last minute dinner out. Pretty good service, good variety in their menu and good prices. I had the Yorkshire puddings appie, it was sooo yummy! Hubby had fish & chips, really nice flaky fish. I had chicken burger & sweet potato fries. It was really moist chicken with a panko batter, and nice mango salsa. The atmosphere left a little to be desired, it was more like a sports bar than pub. But the food was really great.

My home away from home! Lahari Yoga is one of the most welcoming establishments I've ever set foot in. Before I did my first yoga class, I wasn't even that sure if I liked yoga! But the facility is so nice that I kept coming back and pushing past the mental and physical boundaries I had set for myself. It's been approximately a year and a half since I first visited Lahari and I make sure to try to come in a couple times a week. The instructors taught me how to be so in tune with myself and I consider myself to be a "yogi" now. Owner Larissa is a brilliant mind and runs her studio with a very laid-back and casual approach - treating each customer like an old friend. As Lahari continues to gain traction and grow as a company, I'll be right there with them as a long-term supporter.

Total disaster!  Reservation at 6 p.m., seated at a table better suited for 2 rather than 4, drinks arrive, white wine very warm in a  "chilled"  glass. Our meal finally arrived at 7:30, the only salad  that was ordered never showed up at all.  Food was mediocre. Excuses where abundant,  my favorite was that the chef was over whelmed, sorry, you run on reservations and since you have been in the business previously one would suppose that you could at the very least make an educated guess at walk ins, so that just doesn't cut it.  Hugely disappointed as we were out to celebrate 2 birthdays and an anniversary and we're looking forward to hosting a nice evening.  Our meals were on the house in the end but that really doesn't diminish the impact of a ruined evening!
It seems that my review won't post unless I give a "star" rating, therefore I will indicate 1 star, since "minus" stars are not offered!

Definitely no complaints after the first visit to fatburger St. A. Food came out quickly and was definitely far above your regular "fast food" style burger. Had fries and gravy along with the burger and both were super tasty. Diner style decorating and seating inside, as well as big tvs with hockey and football on definitely make it a lot more appealing than other big burger chain stores

This is a lovely boutique offering some unique pieces of clothing and accessories. I mostly come here to get new leggings every now and then. They sell SweetLegs leggings which are one size fits all. These are super comfy! Plus they have so many colors and patterns there is surely one (or more) that you will LOVE! Leggins are versatile and you can dress these them up or down. I've even exercised in these and they stay in place! They also carry just as many of the SweetLegs in the petites sizes AND they have some for girls too!
In my last trip to this boutique, I noticed a large selection of scarves in various colors. They also have plenty of funky and humorous socks for both men and women. So if you are looking for a unique gift, this might be a fun idea!
The boutique also has a fair collection of jewelry for sale including the independent Canadian company eLiasz and eLLa. I just love their bracelets!
The staff are very friendly and helpful. Make sure to ask them about their points for frequent shoppers to earn money off your future purchases!
If you are shopping with a baby or kids there is a nice area in the corner for kids to play.

Not sure where they were heading on this one, but I am confident I won't be heading back.

I adore the theory, the execution can be worked on.

The decor and ambiance is rather an old cottage feel, too "fine dining" and mature for my taste. For whatever reason, I was expecting a gastropub designed for the younger and hip audience.

The draft craft beer selection was nice, however, all of them hovering around the 8-10$ range, put me off. I opted to look at the cocktail menu, all of which are the 11-14$ range. I settled for the 12 Acres Manhattan. It needs a bit more of a whimsical touch, something I am akin to at places such as 27 Ampersand and Woodwork. 

We went with a group of 16. I must say all the food came out without a hitch. Though, it did take 50% longer than I am use to. Perhaps it won't be an issue with a table of 2 or 4.  Portions were small-medium. I ended up eating my 2 of my neighbors' left over to feel satisfied. We started with the beef tartare, I think the mistake is to serve large potato fries to use as a scoop for the crumbling tartare. I mean, how can you expect a 3/4" area sustain a mound of meat? It was a challenge. The tartare itself was in its purest form: meat and chopped garlic. It needed seasoning. I had the pasta bolognese and ordered a side of lamb sausage. The pasta could use a bit more sauce, and maybe more EVOO to make it easier to swallow. Lamb sausage was very nice though, quite meaty and lean. 

I know a bunch of people in my group comment that they would return. But personally, I feel as if this place just serves comfort food in a small portion, and slapped on a higher price tag. I do love my comfort food though.

Such delicious, fresh ingredients. One of the few times I actually felt like I was going out to eat better food than what I could have at home.

The burger was cooked absolutely perfectly; crispy outside, juicy center. The bun was fresh. The fixings were tasty. 

Limited lunch menu, which I like. I don't like having too many options. Nice variety. 

Our service (Dakota) was fantastic. The owner was present in the seating area checking on customers, and very patiently dealing with a complaint from a grumpy man who expected a lot of special accommodations.  He handled it very well. 

I wish I could give 4.5 stars. 4 seems like too little. Once I've been again, I may update to a 5. It's close!!

Lahari Yoga welcomed my wife and I with open arms, honouring our recently purchased yoga sessions from Shakti Yoga which went out of business.

It's a bit of a jaunt up a flight of stairs but well worth the effort.  The wife has dragged me to at least a half dozen yoga studios over the past two years but this one certainly has a feel all of its own.

From the bright colours to the plush couches, Lahari feels like how Yoga should be.

Very much a Middle Eastern feel and look but modern enough to have a complimentary coffee/tea bar for before and after class with Mumford & Sons playing over the stereo.

I've been to two hot classes here so far and everybody that I've met on staff have been the friendliest of the friendly including an after class potluck party where I was served real Mexican beer.

Now, this is my kind of yoga studio.

The best Fatburger in Alberta. Lettuce wrapped offerings ensure I don't slide away from my meal plan. Staff is friendly and helpful and the location is a delight to visit. Flexible menu, quality ingredients and talented staff make it difficult to find any shortcomings. I will return often.

Sweet Boutique is a local shop that has something for every female in your life! Sometimes they even have a little something for the men too. 

The clothes are super cute and the company actively markets themselves through their social media accounts on insta and Facebook. I love it! I'm not huge on shopping so being able to see the clothes being tried on by real woman who have similar bodies to my own is SO HELPFUL. 

They also have super cute gifts. Bath soaks, socks, oven mitts and little gifts for those in your life who you have no idea to shop for. 

Thank you Sweet Boutique for making my Christmas shopping easy. And for those of you looking to support a local business, I would highly recommend you check this one out!
Sad to say this establishment has been sold and rebranded. Best of luck to the old owners and the new ones coming in.

We went to 12 Acres tonight for our 25th anniversary and were looking for a nice evening and some great food.
Their concept of organic and GMO free food is similar to Range Road restaurant but the comparison stops there.  I found myself distracted with this restaurant not sure what they were trying to be.  The prices are high and the menu suggests fine cuisine however the experience most certainly did not meet the expectation.  The service was poor and the wait for our food was long.
I had the pasta with prawns which was only average and my wife had the fried butter chicken which tasted like run of the mill fried chicken.  Very disappointing.  Range Road is also expensive with small portions however the quality of their food is far above this restaurant.  The drinks are also small and expensive.
Tonight there must have been family / relatives hanging around with their little kids running around the restaurant getting in the way of the waitresses and taking away from the whole experience.  The place felt like an ABC family restaurant.
I would not recommend this restaurant and unfortunately I give it a year and they will be closing the doors.

Different teachers every class. Hard to get to know people's teaching styles if there's new people pretty much every week-- there's times i've gone here expecting a specific teacher for a class and there's a different one there instead. Kinda frustrating if i don't like the other teacher's style. I also typically use the rental mats, and they ALWAYS smell like feet. I wouldn't be surprised if they're never cleaned. Gross.

I don't even know where to start about this business. First of all it doesn't feel like a business, it feels like going to your friends house to shop. From the owner to the sales girls, everyone is so friendly and takes pride in the store. They strive to make the customers happy. The owner goes out her way daily to make the customers happy and get what they need/want. This boutique has brought so many women in the community together and boosted the confidence of so many across Canada. Laura is a delight. She's witty, funny, smart, confident and an all around great person. I looked forward to her popping in live chats and her weekly Wednesday lives. She is one of the most engaged business owners I've ever come across. I look forward to many many many more trips to Sweet Boutique.

What a warm and inviting space. Each instructor brings their own personality into their classes, thru their music choices and sequencing of postures. The studio offers such an array of classes, excuses such as  "there won't be a class suitable for me" just don't fly. From hot to room temperature, restorative to vinyasa flow, this studio has it all. Larissa welcomes each of her students with open arms. I have met amazing instructors and fellow yoga practitioners. What have you got to lose, the first class is free. Join in and see what you have been missing.

I base this review on two visits.  One visit we waited over 45 minutes to receive our fast food order for two people.  When I
 brought it up to the employee, she said they were busy.  I did write to their head office and did not receive a response.  Another visit was ok. It's an average burger - that's all. Place was clean.

Great food and fast table serve, only Fatburger location I go to in Edmonton area (St.Albert) 

Still getting used to the early close times 8pm Thursday Friday Saturday and think Sunday. 7pm Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday. 

The Milkshakes are awesome.

Not sure what to say about this place. It has it all, burgers, wings, drinks and ice cream! The servers are very nice but I dunno how to fatburger... like can I get more things added? No one gave me options. So I am not sure could I have added to my burger? Also it wasn't worth the $18 price tag for the meal. I hate to say it but it wasn't. Not that it wasn't a good burger but I have had better for cheaper. All in all the staff is great and the food is average

We really love this place. Reviews are mixed on here, and frankly we don't get it. Excellent specials, fantastic food, great service and beers on tap from Grizzly Paw and Fernie Brewing? What's not to love?

We met a large group of friends on a Wednesday night for drinks recently and were again impressed. Cheap wine night, which Heather loved. I had a couple of pints of Project 9 Pils from Fernie Brewing Co. (a personal favourite). We shared some dishes... the sausage platter (we went Italian and chorizo, both excellent and the ballpark mustard is to die for), the pickles salad (fantastic) and the dry ribs (again amazing).

Some here have commented that this place seems pricey, but I find the local quality worth the price. Consider us fans.

Love LOVE love me some Sweet Boutique!

I've been shopping here since the days of parking lot chaos at their first location. 

Sweet Boutique recently celebrated their 5th birthday!  I love their new location on St. Albert Trail next to BP's.  (I think it's been almost 3 years here?)

From their live WIW (Win It Wednesday) Facebook streams to their name of the day discount, Sweet Boutique knows how to court their regulars. 

They've got it all, from the softest leggings on the planet to the best  jeans for every body type!  I love that Sweet Boutique has something to help every woman feel her best.  

They even have something for the men in your life.  Last year, I got sassy and funky dress socks for my kids' male teachers.

The customer service is second to none and the vibe is cozy chic from the moment you walk through the door. 

Be sure to sign up for their free loyalty program to earn rewards!

Best fish and chips in St. Albert, that's my opinion. (The only one I care about)
Great, happy staff and loads of beer to choose from and a few good wines too!

Sweet Boutique is located next to Boston Pizza on the south end of St. Albert. 

It's run by a local mom catering to the comfortable fashionista from day to night.  The boutique carries a sizes all the way from kiddo/tweens to plus size.  My daughter loves that we can get correlating or matching pieces here!

They travel the world to bring us the freshest and most on trend accessories and clothing items.  They have special shopping nights a couple times of the year around Xmas and Valentine's day with special hours just for guys, husbands, dad's to pop in and shop with help, usually beer ;-) and discounts!

And they do carry a few items for men throughout the year - definitely during gift giving season (items like mypackage boxer briefs).

They have a rewards program that earns you gift certificates - who doesn't love that?

They carry some pretty cool designers/brands like Grace & Lace, Sweet Legs (softest leggings on the planet in the funkiest patterns - think cats!), and my newest fave find and purchase is an off the shoulder sweatshirt that reads - All good moms drop the F bomb!  Bahahaha - this is so me.  My children get to charge me $1 every time they hear me swear but I feel like I should get at least one free pass per day that I wear this sweatshirt ;-)

They also support local!  There was a TO DIE FOR Star Wars and Harry Potter line of leggings/dresses painted by local a local artist (HotDame) but sadly only in kiddo sizes (HINT, HINT, NOT SO SUBTLE HINT - there is most definitely an adult market for this, too!).

Mostly it's the fabulous staff and owner, Laura, that makes this store shine!  Follow them on facebook for upcoming deals, watch their live videos like Win It Wednesday, and most of all... support local!

Love these fabulous ladies.

P.S. Husband, if you are reading this review - they have a really cool aromatherapy necklace right now that would make a great anniversary present ;-)

Food was of acceptable quality, nothing to write home about, but if my friends wanted to go I wouldn't say no.
However I will not return to the St. Albert location since while we were waiting for our food to be made and our number to be called one of the employees went behind the counter and took off his shoe and placed it on the order pickup/assembly counter to what looked like relace it. 
My brother in law (who has been a chef for 20 years) made a loud comment to get his shoes off a food service counter and how it was totally inappropriate to do that, and the kid mumbled about how food didn't go on that counter and then came out from behind the counter and sat at the table next to the pop machine and placed his shoe on the table. 

Totally unacceptable and we won't be back.

The food is always solid, probably one of the best places to go to if you don't want unexpected results or bad food. While the drinks are a bit more expensive than other places, they usually have rare drinks on tap that others don't.

Only had an issue with an order once, and they didn't charge for it! So they are always ready to remedy any issues.

yes and no. I love you guys! but today I went in with a girlfriend, and love to be able to shop and scope out the clothes, but within 5 min I was asked three times if I'm okay, if I'm looking for something specific etc. were only ones in there, so I would think the 3 employees would know they were asking us same thing.
