Once we politely said were okay, because weve been asked a few times, everyone left.  no one asked us if were okay in the change room or if we needed extra sizes. At checkout, I felt tension, and when we got in the car, everyone came out. This will definitely not keep me away, but left a bad taste in my mouth.

As others have said, you can really tell that they use fresh ingredients.  I've liked every flavour I've tried so far (as well as their tiramisu), and have to give a special mention to the black forest cake... it's to die for!

Wish it was easier to find their products in stores as their place is a little out of the way, but it's worth the trip!

I rate the entree menu "2 stars" -- due to a complete lack of seasoning.  "Bland" does not even cover it --- Where is the seasoning?  The Salt?  The Pepper?  Such wonderful meat cuts, but also overcooked.  Horribly disappointing, and this is over 4 visits.

But.

And there is a but.  The appetizer menu is easily worth "5 Stars" due to scrumptious, tasty flavours WITH SEASONING.  

And here is where I am confused.  Befuddled.  At a loss.

Why the disconnect?  Amazing appy's replete with flavours, seasoning and creativity.  But entree's that are overcooked, unseasoned and wholly bland.  

"Paying homage to the ingredients" (ie. To the cut of meat, the freshness of the produce), does NOT mean leave out the seasoning!

For your consideration.

We wanted to check out this new restaurant as we love to support buying local food, as well as local businesses, and we were not disappointed.  

When we arrived we were greeted warmly and seated at a nice table.  The decor is very nice and I loved the open cooler that show cases the meats that they prepare in house.  We had an opportunity to learn about where the meat comes from and were happy to hear that the animals roam freely around the farm, hence the tag Pasture to Plate; and we loved the fact that the animals are raised organically and are not given any growth hormones or antibiotics.  

The server informed us that she spends time at the farm and could tell us about the animals that are raised there - which was a really cool experience as a guest, to hear about how well the animals are cared for.

Our meal was delicious.  I had the buttermilk chicken and my husband opted for the burger; and we both tried their custom cocktails, which were very delicious.  The portions were very generous and the food was mouth watering delicious and more then satisfying; and the bill was very reasonable.  I can hardly wait to go back and try the lunch menu.

Well done 12 Acres, we will be back very soon!

We have a group of us that try out restaurants we have never been to before.
So this past Saturday night we decided to try 12 Acres for dinner.

Since we were a group of 8, we were able to make reservations, so were able to get one of the few bigger long tables.
I can see why there can be long waits here, as even though there are 2 separate rooms, there aren't many tables.  I'm not sure if it's typical, but noticed it wasn't as busy after about 8:30 or so this night, so that may be a good time to come by.

The iPad as a menu is a very nice idea, as you can see pictures of what you want beforehand.

As one reviewer stated, drinks can be a bit pricey with the average pint about $11, but I do love that they have so many different craft type beer and not the usual stuff.  You can get some bottles for around $7.25 too.

I started with the parsnip fritters.  Myself and a few of my friends that tried it agreed that it was a nice appy to start (and goes great with the beer).  A couple of friends ordered the beef tartar and it also looked quite good.  
I was hoping for my main entree to order the pork chops since heard many good reviews on them, but unfortunately they didn't have it on the menu that night. That's one thing to expect, a revolving menu daily, so I knew that going in.  I ended up ordering the lamb sirloin.  I found the meat perfectly cooked and tender and loved the sauce.  I just wish they would offer it with a bit more veggies other than potato.  My friend's lamb burger looked very good, and that's something I may have to try next time.

Service was very good, very attentive and always checking on us and refilling water.  That's all you can ask of any waitress/waiter.

Now my only complaint, and this actually extends to all restaurants that do it, is the automatic gratuity (I'm assuming it was because we were a party of 8).  I have no problem if places do this for large parties, my only issue is when they do not mention that it is already added on the bill.  Yes, I know we all should review our bills before paying, but the tax and tip part can be easily overlooked, as sometimes we just look at the itemized stuff, and can be worst in large groups, where people just look at their items and throw in what they estimate to owe (with tip).  I don't think it is hard for the server to let the group know that tip is already added.  This has always been a big pet peeve of mine.  Business' please take note, and instruct your servers to mention if tip is already included on the bill.

Will I come back?  Probably, but I think this would be more of a place to go for a special occasion or date night.
I do love the concept of range free farm raised and locally grown produce.

We've been here a couple times and we've typically had average experiences. However this week we showed up at 9:20. We were told that the kitchen closes at 9 and last call was at 9:15. Why would you even have a posted closing time of 10? Anyway, they completely wasted my time and I will not be going again. 
Go check out the new Endeavour Brewing in St Albert, they seem to be more appreciative of their customers.

The waitresses are really good, when they put down their phones. (Rarely) the food is not consistent, mine was good, 3 others at the table had the same meal but theirs was half the food. Their sandwiches looked like they ran out on meat making mine. We had a group of 7 and were pretty much ignored, 1 drink over the 45 minutes there. This is a review on the second trip, the first was no better for phones, or food. Don't eat the pizza.

The service was great but I wish there was more of a food selection. Looks like Friday and Saturday nights are the best dinner nights. 

Beer menu was good, and it showed that they switch out their beers regularly.

Don't be put off by appearances because this is actually a pretty decent little spot. Right in the middle of an industrial area, there's a large patio and plenty of parking. The entrance is on the street side though, so if you park in the lot by the dog groomer you have to walk around the building. 

Walking in, it looks older, dark and a little dicey.  We came specifically for the $9.99 prime rib special on Friday night though, so we were ready for a "get what you pay for" moment. Pleasantly surprised by how much we liked it. For the price you get warm potatoes, a yorkshire pudding with beer gravy, and a slice of garlic bread spread with a mayo of some sort and topped with prime rib and gravy. Definitely carb heavy.

Service was really quick and super friendly. Our yorkshire puddings were cold and I asked for it to be warmed up. She mentioned that they're baked earlier in the day and so it could explain the temp. I'm guessing it's kind of an assembly line to put the plate together. That said, the taste of everything was pretty good. The potatoes were tossed in a warm potato salad kind of way and the meat was tender and well seasoned. It was  great value at $10. Also had the peach ale and it was a wonderful summery beer.

If you're not looking for fancy, check it out.

Came here for beverages before another event and had a great time sitting on the patio with a friend.  Server seemed knowledgeable about the beer and could recommend beer for even someone who usually HATES it. Only thing they need is a solid appie menu!
Food is good and moderately priced. Great patio and frozen drinks in the summer. It's nice to have a restaurant in the industrial area of St. Albert as it's convenient for the people that work there.

When I saw the advertisement saying "$4.99 Chicken and Ribs" I thought it was a typo, but no, that is the Beer Factory's Saturday night special: a plate of chicken and ribs with coleslaw and potatoes for the low, low price of five dollars.  

The Beer Factory is located in an industrial neighborhood of St. Albert, and there aren't any other restaurants or retail stores located around it.  Parking is terrible, with one small lot located on a steep incline (be careful not to catch the underside of your car on the curb exiting, we sure did).  We had to street park and walk; I'm not sure where all the cars were from, as the restaurant wasn't terribly busy.

The atmosphere is casual, and has a bit of a dive bar feel to it.  The restaurant is attached to the Hogs Head brewery, so if you're going to sample beer, there's a good selection of what they offer, plus a tasting flight.  The menu was pretty limited, lots of fried bar-style food, with no salads or lighter fare.  Other than the special Saturday night food, most dishes were $10 for appetizers and $15-20 for mains.  I think their lunch menu may be a bit better, but nothing sounded great on the dinner menu based on the descriptions. 

Because it was Saturday, everyone in my group got the chicken and ribs.  I expect the cheap price is to bring people in to eat and drink, but the problem was most of the food was either bad or inedible.  I have never had chicken that was so dry and so overcooked in my life.  The pieces I managed to pull off the bone tasted like old fish and I didn't keep eating for fear of getting food poisoning.  The others in my group loved their ribs, but I found them fatty and full of gristle.  The coleslaw was vinegary and the only saving grace was the potatoes, which had a mustard sauce on them that was pretty good.  The regular dishes must be better than this special, otherwise the restaurant would be out of business in a week.  As an added bonus I got to take home the smell of the frying oil on my clothes and hair.  

Two stars instead of one because the food was dirt cheap (you get what you pay for?), and because our service was quick and friendly.

Good selections of on tap craft brews, good service. We went on a Saturday night with playoff hockey on the screens.
We ordered the beer marinated chicken wings which the waitress informed us are now "boneless chicken wings" . We thought sure why not. However when it came to us it was 4 dry CHICKEN STRIPS for 14.99 with one sliced carrot one sliced celery stick and I don't mean the whole carrot or celery. These were not chicken wings in any way. Therefore we didn't want to try ordering any of the other food items. One of my fellow guests ordered one of their drinks on the menu which had jack Daniels listed in the ingredients. The waitress stated we are almost out of Jack Daniels can I substitute for Canadian club? It only called for .5 ounce of JD-- we declined the Canadian club substitution and went with knob creek. To top it off at 9:30 pm we were told it was last call because they decided they were going to close at 10:30... okay?  So all in all, good beer but I won't be returning.

Wish I could rate this higher. We used to frequent this place a lot when it was Hogs Head Brewing. We still go because it has a certain charm and appeal and we hope it has future potential.

  My late uncle always said the best bars are little hideaways where you can slip away for a sneaky pint. This very much describes this place. Other positives are friendly staff, a very cool patio/ deck, and a nice comfortable room.

  The food is good, not great in my opinion. Some great deals on certain days and some disappointments we have had in the past. It seems very hit and miss. But the big disappointment here is the beer. We go to a spot called Beer Warehouse for the beer. On paper they have a good selection of local Alberta taps but in reality they are ALWAYS out of half of what they list. It literally happens every time we go. Disappointing.

We will keep going and cross our fingers for improvements. This place is above average currently but could be great.

I went to the Beer Factory in St Albert today for the chicken and Rib special. I am just starting out on Yelp and almost did not go after reading what the girl Nicole wrote about the place. She must be very unhappy in her life because this place was great. Good beer good staff and food for 5 bucks yikes. The rotisserie chicken was done perfect and the ribs were to die for. Parking was no problem I liked how quiet the area was. Nicole should stick to McDonald's

This place is great! Have been a number of times now and Beer Factory has yet to disappoint! The food is delicious and the beer selection is awesome. Service here is always top notch, the staff does a really great job and will always take the time to help with the menu or explain the many varieties of beers on tap!! Definitely worth checking out if you are looking for something different and new in the St. A area!

The best hidden secret in St Albert!

The food is spectacular and it's all prepared by a real Chef. Now that things have turned around for this place, I only have great things to say about it. 

The new owners of Beer Factory gives their hart and soul into this place and great things are happening. 

If you have not came back within the last 4 month, I recommend that you do! You'll be surprised of the quality of food that comes out of this unusual location to have craft food that DOES NOT DISAPPOINT!    

Go see for yourself. This is a coming from a guy who lives within walking distance and loves when a place has character and employees who actually care. 

I don't normally write good reviews, let along 5 stars, but this place has exceeded my expectations over and over again. 

If you like craft food, craft beer, and the owners from the top down caring that you enjoy your experience as much as you do..... Check it out.

This used to be Hog's Head Brewing, and something apparently happened with the business partners so it is now owned by Beer Factory.   They are apparently under construction with a very small brewing operation so they didn't have any of their own products.

Their beer list was basic with a few local drafts.     The server didn't know much about the beer when we had questions.  

We were there on a Saturday and the men in our group ordered the $5 chicken and ribs special.  They all enjoyed it, and raved about the great value of coleslaw, potatoes, chicken and ribs all for five.. yes five dollars!    I ordered the donair sub which was just mediocre.

Overall, the visit was just okay, but I wouldn't really go back for any reason considering it is in a somewhat out of the way industrial area of the city.
Great beer, enthusiastic service, and a great place to get a bite while your kids are in dance class or soccer practice!  We will be back!

Once upon a time there were a bunch of guys that wanted to start up the craft beer industry in Edmonton.  They all got together and opened up a small brewery in St. Alberta and called it Hogshead. They made some wicked pumpkin spice beer.  

Run badly was an understatement.  The 2015 end of Hogshead was an embarrassing mess.  The unfortunate end still continues to add backlash to the new establishment "The Beer Factory".  

Patrick Spilstead was a graduate from the NAIT culinary program that was hired in 2014 to head the kitchen of Hogshead.  When the whole thing derailed, Patrick and his father Richard rescued the operation and turned it into what is now "The Beer Factory".  

They were first on my radar after an event where they were networking and my boss from the Edmonton Muse had a pamphlet on her table.  I perused it and added it to my "hit list" of places to visit.  

Patrick is cooking today because of an unfortunate accident.  He was raised in a family that had a strong culinary background but he went to pursue being a Mechanic.  The accident would plague him with knee problems, so he found himself shifting focus - to culinary.  

He was with Chop for several years and disliked the corporate environment of the kitchen.  On to smaller and better things with The Beer Factory! 

Everything on the menu is infused with beer or moonshine.  You have some gastropub favourites, and then there are some awesome comfort food options as well like spicy beef stroganoff.  Note: the menu has changed from what is posted on the website. 
 
My first visit was because I had to try the Friday Prime Rib Special for $9.99.  That got me in a seat to see the menu and try one of their craft brews, the "Dark and Malty".  This has become one of my favourite local brews. Not available anywhere but in their taproom. It has the darkness of a stout, but the smoothness of a lighter ale. 
 
They also make a Mosiac Pale Ale, a "hop oriented beer that is a bit tamed".  I'm not an IPA girl personally. I have not tried this one.  

The ambience is casual.  This is more of a pub feel.  The staff are friendly and attentive.  There is a patio area for summer time and an overhead door to let the fresh air in.  You are in the middle of an industrial area in St. Albert, so there isn't a pretty view.

The Prime Rib was delicious.  They were also putting out information for a special Valentine's dinner that was taking place in a couple of weeks.  I read over the menu and completely swooned, and made reservations immediately. Patrick was given full creativity and let loose! 

The Valentine's Dinner was AMAZING!   

We had the Elk Carpaccio; thinly shaved Elk tenderloin seasoned with lime and cracked black pepper.  This was absolutely delicious and delicate. What a great way to get the taste buds ready for the rest of the meal. 
 
Ginger Peach scented pork with mango chutney; pork tenderloin rolled in ginger peach tea, served with house made mango moonshine chutney.  This dish paired so well with the wild rose mead that was suggested.  

Dessert was raspberry and white chocolate creme brulee, chocolate dipped strawberries and moonshine cherry tea cookies.   

Patrick knocked it out of the park!  The whole experience was culinary heaven.  The price tag on this experience was $50 for two.  Beverages were not included, but what a great deal! I can't wait until they do another special event.   

I was able to have a chat with Richard.  He is Patrick's dad and co-owner of the brewery.  Richard is also a Chef. They like to source the menu locally whenever possible.  He was also telling me that they do BBQ in the summertime and they have a huge rig to be able to do mobile BBQ catering. That will be another article in the future for sure!
 
We have been back a few times to enjoy food and beer.  The taps rotate with local craft favourites and the two brews that The Beer Factory produces on their own.  

Fun fact; they are the smallest craft brewery in Western Canada!  

Advice for your visit: 

Ignore the ratings.  There were a lot of angry customers with the whole Hogshead disaster. 

Be patient!  The kitchen is small and there are a lot of regular customers.  Good food takes time. It will be worth the wait!  

Try one of their brews!  They may not be geared towards everyone's palate, but they are definitely worth a taste.

My boyfriend and I celebrated our 5th anniversary here, first time at this restaurant and it didn't dissapoint, service was excellent, food was superb! we started with the calamari and then my boyfriend had the primerib cooked to perfection, I had the special which was Steak Oscar, it had a delicious sauce with a big serving of it, we both picked the mashed potatoes, they were so creamy and each dish had a corn, carrot, broccoli and cauliflower, portions were huge! The meal started off with some sourdough bread as well, you will leave full and happy! Looking forward to coming back

Splash Juicery just opened up offering the first cold-pressed juicery in St. Albert!

Thus far, my favourite is Dragon's Blood containing Beets, apples, lemons, carrots!  Their website description makes me giggle: According to ancient myth, the Vietnamese people originated from dragons and fairies. They believe dragons bring rain for agriculture. They represent the emperor, the power and prosperity of their nation. Help us bring rain for the fruit and vegetables to grow, and to fuel the power of our nation. Dragon's Blood is filled with protein for strength, and vitamin K for your own blood and bone benefits. Allow us to help you onto your throne with this juice, as you become the  emperor of your life.

You can check out each and every one of their cold pressed juices and smoothies on their website and of course, their fabulously entertaining descriptions.

I was first introduced to Splash Juicery when they paired with Edmonton Hot Yoga Wellness for their Grand Opening.  

Prices range from about $6-$8 per bottle and upwards for their cleanse/detox programs.

Follow them on Twitter @SplashJuicery for details about up and coming flavours and specials.

I'm excited to have Splash in my neck of the woods as fresh-pressed juices filed with fruits, veggies, and goodness like ginger are definitely my choice for a treat over more processed and frozen alternatives that I would previously take my daughter to (like Booster Juice).

Also, admittedly, I am not a juicing expert and didn't even know the difference between cold-pressed and centrifugal juicing methods prior to checking out their website.  It definitely intrigues me and I think they give a good quick overview here:
http://www.splashjuicery.ca/cold-pressed-vs-centrifugal/
It's definitely a topic that I'll do a little more googling on to learn about but I can certainly say that the juices I had left me feeling satisfied, energized, and balanced for hours after my Hot Yoga class.  

I'd love to see them offer smaller sizes in the future or maybe a 6 pack of the most popular flavours to take home :-)

Cheers to Splash Juicery - looking forward to seeing what's yet to come!

Its Sunday night in St Albert and there are a few restaurants open down town. Stop in here a 6. Place is completely deserted. Not one customer and not a soul in sight. Waited to be seated but no one showed up. Left. 

Other posts say it is under  the same ownership as when it was Ricks grill so I am not surprised the service is still terrible. Didn't know that when we stopped or I wouldn't have dropped in to start with. Only time I was at Ric's the review I wrote flamed it pretty hard but fully earned.

Food was very good and price was right. I don't know why but the restaurant was empty on a Friday night a 7??? That probably explain why the service was excellent. Only negative point was that we ordered a couple items from the menu and the kitchen didn't have it. but overall it was a good experience.
Awesome Juice!  Awesome customer service!  The owner is amazing source of health knowledge!  Great local business to support!

I love Splash Juicery!!! First & foremost it's ORGANIC! The juice combinations are great. They have teas, smoothies and raw food. The staff are friendly and helpful. We make the 45 minute drive to Splash everytime we need a fix. I hope to see Splash grow and pop up everywhere! This is exactly what this world needs more of! We need to be nourished. The only things I'd like to see done is please add nut milks to your menu, and hopefully in the future you can switch to glass bottles for the environment. Thanks for doing what you do, and we shall see you soon.

This is a new place to St. Albert that opened Winter 2014. Ran by a mother/daughter team who are very nice. I love the selection of juice blends and smoothies. Everything is so fresh and so good. I learned from them that you have to drink fresh juice within a short period of time... I think 3 days? Something like that so it's nice to get it while it's cold. It's has a nice sterile ambiance so that makes me feel good knowing that they clean and my juice is treated with only love. 

Sometimes they don't have a juice in stock but I can deal. There's always something I can find that's just as good.

I'm glad to say the second time I visited this restaurant it was just as great! Had the prime rib, it was huge! Love the au jus and horseradish, the mashed was great, my boyfriend had the same but with asparagus risotto, the risotto was amazing, so creamy and delicious, we started off with the jumbo shrimp cocktail (not soo jumbo) and the spinach dip that was served with tortilla chips, dip was really good. Service was excellent!!! Looking forward to coming back again :)

Great location, friendly staff, way over priced for quality of work. Thought I would treat myself to the full experience and pay a little bit extra, BIG MISTAKE!  I was pretty clear as to what I wanted, or so I thought, perhaps I wasn't. There were no mirrors where the color was applied so it was hard to see what was going on. It felt good. When my hair was washed and dried I couldn't tell that there was anything done. Seemed pretty much the same. Decided to put some extensions in to fill the sparse spots. I had never had them before so I trusted and assumed that the girl knew what she was doing. Seemed to look ok when I left. Got home looked in the three way mirror and noticed that the extensions where about an inch and a half longer than my hair. I have naturally wavy hair and they were poker straight. Where they were attached was loose and like a wave (very bumpy) along where they were attached. After doing some research I realized that they were number one, they wrong type for my hair (Way to thick/coarse). The nightmare began when I washed it and tried to style it. I had to spend three times as much time to get it to look half decent. After two days there was a ugly long string sticking out of the back of my head. I ended up having to go and pay for another haircut to try to blend the two together and deal with the string, plus she ended up having to sew the string in. five days later... I did some searching and found a wonderful lady on Kijiji. Her name is Loralee. She instantly got back to me. She works out of a small salon, not a fancy place, but what a professional and caring person. She took the time to explain all of my options on how we could deal with the existing extensions, with no sale pressure. I ended up taking them out and replacing them with wavy, individual thinner pieces that matched my hair perfectly, and at a super reasonable price. I can't believe how I was taken by Elixir. I got better service and better work by far. Loralee has given me permission to giver her contact information. I highly recommend her, you won't be disappointed. Phone or text: 780-318-0654. She is located right on 118/Kingsway Ave and 123 Street. Save your money and get it done right!!!

We popped in here on a Monday night because our original destination was closed. The place was barren... not a table in there had people at it other than ours. It wasn't terribly late, maybe 8PM. We were told that they were out of tuna, and running low on mashed potatoes. 

Honestly we were looking forward to a nice glass of wine more than anything, so the wine list was pretty disappointing. We went with an Argentinian Malbec, which is a safe bet. Reliable but not anything special. 

For food, we nibbled on some peppercorn cheese fries, that weren't too bad. The price for the size of the order, though, left something to be desired! $7 for a small handful of fries and fifty cents worth of sauce. 

My main was a Goat Cheese Chicken Salad, and I subbed the menu dressing for a lime shallot vinaigrette. It was fresh, and the chicken wasn't horribly overcooked. The strawberries and blueberries were mostly fresh (I did run into a couple of blueberries that had seen better days, but not many, honestly). There were three balls of goat cheese on the top of the salad that lasted the entire salad (nothing worse than running out half way through your meal!). There were also almond slivers over the salad. All in all, this wasn't bad. 

Service was on top of things (but with only one table to work with, I would be very disappointed if they weren't!)

Most of the menu was very overpriced for what it seemed you were getting. Honestly I'm not too surprised they were empty. Pair that with the wine list? There wasn't a bottle on the list that you would pair with a $40 steak. 

Overall, underwhelming. There are better options in town.

I have only been to this place twice but really enjoyed it!
The juices are delicious and made with organic fruits and veggies.
The smoothies are also very tasty and filled with healthy ingredients.
They also do juice cleanses which I am excited to try one day!

My boyfriend and I have been to splash juicery whenever we are in St. Albert and want something healthy to eat or drink.. my favorite juice is the signature splash, however, each one has its own unique flare to it. I've done their juice cleanses 3 times already and i'm looking forward to doing another one of them as they not only supply you with the juice, but probiotics, digestive enzymes and fiber tablets. Hopefully their juices will be situated in other wellness locations around town in the future.

Well this place is meh...

It was super dead - even for a Monday! We had a fabulous server, but that doesn't make up for a sub-par wine list that is paired with a very expensive food menu. Seriously, if i'm having a $40 fish or steak dinner, it would be nice to have a decent bottle of wine with it... and none, NONE of the wines by the bottle were more than $20 retail. 

I had the peppercorn fries; which were not bad - kind of like a steakhouse poutine. The real, whole, peppercorns made for a spicy surprise when you bit into one (or 4) of them in one bite. Then I had the less than sub-par chicken sandwich. It wasn't bad... it just wasn't good, at all. Not much flavour. Just, not much of anything. Oh, and the soup on the side - horrible! 

My best synopsis of this place is that it is like an airport restaurant. The food won't kill you, but it's going to be over priced, and really not taste all that great. But, it will fill you up until you get somewhere better.

gross! two really unfriendly experiences here in a row. their juice menu is very small, and they claim they arrive here two hours early every morning, but there are multiple juices that they don't seem to get around to making until the afternoon. this seems weird for a "juicery". the staff even refused my offer to wait for them to make the flavour i was after saying they didn't have time.

they also have a little fridge with some homemade snacks but no pricing sign. i guess they had taken it down to update it or it fell off, but just four little peanut butter balls in a mini-sized ziploc bag were $10! that's more expensive than a large bottle of any of their juices. two mini ziplocs of peanut butter treats and two bottles of juice later, it was a $42 snack trip.

i'm not opposed to spending money for good quality, but to top it off, they were stale.

when i tried to bring any of this to the store's attention, there wasn't a single apology or even an offer to make the next experience better. just derisiveness and snark, so i guess i'll be driving to edmonton to a proper juicery the next time i'm in the mood!

A beautiful salon to walk into. Has a great first impression. That staff all seem friendly and professional. I enjoyed a shampoo and blow out this morning leaving me feeling pampered and beautiful. My stylist was sweet, beautiful and very good at what she does.

Went to dinner last night with a group of 12.  Service was excellent, food was great!  I had the summer steak special 4 course meal and will definitely be back again.  Steak was cooked perfectly.  Most people ordered the special but those that didn't also enjoyed their meal just as much as everyone else. Thank you Blue Rare!

Meh. My dish was good (Cajun chicken) but my aunt's ribs tasted like mustard. And her veggies tasted like they were soaked in vinegar. It was weird. I tried them both. Not sure what happened there? My dessert was kind weird too. It tasted greasy.... the chocolate brownie Sundae

I have never really had a stellar experience with Splash Juicery, but the most recent time was by far my worst experience.
Firstly, the prices are exorbitant for what you get. I know that not always fresh fruit is used in their blended drinks, which to me doesn't reflect the price.
I have been asking for a nutritional breakdown of one of their drinks for some time, but have never received a clear answer. They tote this  drink around as if it's an amazing detox but appear afraid to say what the nutritional info is. Red flag!
The last time I went in it was to grab a bottle of their new hemp water. I stood at the till for no less than 20 minutes while one worker cleaned the back and the other blended a family's drinks. While I understand that the family of three came in first, I was repeatedly given the "one minute" gesture and not rung through. The other worker in the back saw me standing there but didn't seem to concern herself with me. It was coming close to closing time. I've worked in customer service almost my entire life and I would never prioritize closing duties over a paying customer. Eventually she did end up coming to the front, but it was only to help the other staff member when she was struggling at the till to ring in the family. She avoided any and all contact with me. In fact, they told the family "we will take you at the till here" and gestured toward where I was standing. So essentially they implied for me to move out of the way without directly telling me to do so. It was strange and rude. 
I still don't understand why the worker who was making 2 blended drinks couldn't step away while one drink was blending to check me out. Instead she wandered around doing other tasks. I really should have walked out but I didn't want to make the other customers feel bad (I could tell by the looks on their faces that they wanted me to get checked out as much as I did). After paying $10 for two water bottles, I'm opting to stay away this time.

I hit Blue Rare this past Friday night to meet my friends for drinks. 

 I didn't eat so I can't comment on the food as of yet, but my friends raved about their steaks  and I enjoyed the atmosphere and my drinks so much that I will definitely be returning in the near future to dine.

I'm very happy to have such a nice salon in St. Albert!
Firstly, the decor is fabulous. The salon looks immaculate and modern. 
I came in to see Jill by referral, and what a fabulous referral it was. She seemed to completely understand my hair without me having to explain anything to her. She managed to cut off a substantial amount of split ends (I went far too long in between trims) without it even looking much shorter. She is probably the first hairdresser I've ever met who has actually convinced me to keep up with my regular trims.

Excellent location for high quality service without the overcrowding or the wait. I had found Elixir since it was convenient and close to my workplace. When I gave it a chance, the staff was attentive, the service excellent and management was on point.  Will visit again soon, a hidden gem in Northridge.
Good atmosphere, great wine selection and fantastic food.  Friendly staff.

I came to this salon after I found them on the website of the hair product I like. I had received a very poor haircut at another salon geared towards men. After some quick vetting, I made an appointment with Madison. She is awesome! Great to chat with and does a great haircut. Price-wise, about $40, and worth every penny. When it comes to hair cuts, I believe you get what you pay for.

Stopped in to get a snack for my son. They have a limited smoothy menu but then you can also make your own using their special juice menu. My son went with a mango banana smooth with coconut milk. 

With each smooth you also have the option of adding a super food. These included Chia seed, flax seed, baobab, and a bunch other I can't remember. I had a few sips of my son's drink but wasn't really impressed. I also noticed that they used frozen mango fruit. I kinda felt that for almost $7 they should have used fresh fruit.

The place itself is kinda cute bit at the same time had a bit on a dingy feel to it that I couldn't really pun down.

Anyway I won't be bothering to go back. To expensive considering they don't even use fresh fruit. I wonder if they use frozen fruit in their fresh juices as well.

PLEASE READ TO THE END... If there was an option for zero stars i would choose that. Hi Allan. No you're wrong... my son was NOT happy that the stylist MASSON changed the style that we planned for weeks, with photos on our phones to prove it. He just felt uncomfortable for Masson because I was UPSET with her for not doing a job that we requested & that she was paid to do.

Really more of a 3.5 star restaurant, but I'm an optimist and like to round up. 

Some Yelpers and I came here after the Fit Club event because the restaurant we wanted to go to was closed for the day. We were here later (probably 730ish) and the place was pretty quiet. 

We ordered some drinks. Two of the four got beer, the other two split a bottle of wine. They don't have a huge wine list, but they have a few reds and whites, a small selection of domestic and foreign beers, and some standard cocktails. 

We ordered food, got the peppercorn fries to share. I had a few bites and they were pretty good. The gravy was rich and peppercorns added a nice bite. There is grated cheese on the dish, but it's not poutine because they're not cheese curds. I really appreciate the fact Blue Rare didn't try to falsely advertise this dish as poutine. 

I got the blackened chicken. It's a cajun spiced grilled chicken breast topped with a fruit salsa. The chicken was nice, a little spice but not unbearable and pretty moist (even with the blackened part it certainly wasn't burnt). The fruit salsa was good but there was hardly any on the chicken, it amounted to a few diced pineapple pieces on top. More salsa, even a small dish would have been nice. 

It comes with cooked veggies, which were the most random veggies, a cooked carrot, piece of grilled corn, one piece of steam broccoli and cauliflower.

Food was all right. Service was friendly but a little slow. I wouldn't go out of my way to come here again, but it was ok.
